tasks.deliverable: .github/workflows/ pipeline with a lint/typecheck/test matrix, Trivy gate, GHCR image publish on tag, environment-protected deploy job, and branch protection rules documented in the README.

tasks.title: Add Redis Caching, Sessions, and Rate Limiting to the API
tasks.description: Treat Redis as infrastructure you must reason about, not a black box. Introduce a cache-aside layer for your most expensive queries with explicit TTLs, key naming, and invalidation-on-write, move sessions/rate-limit counters into Redis, and implement a sliding-window limiter. Then prove the effect with measurements and handle the failure modes: cache stampede, stale reads, and Redis unavailability degrading gracefully to the database.
tasks.deliverable: Redis-backed cache-aside layer, session store, and sliding-window rate limiter, plus a before/after load-test report (k6 or autocannon) showing p95 latency and DB query-count reduction, with a documented invalidation and fallback strategy.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: You are already strong at cloud networking - Azure Firewall, VNets, subnets, NSGs, UDRs and Palo Alto policy. This phase converts that expertise into the AWS equivalents hiring managers expect, then deploys the containerized app onto real managed infrastructure. Lean on your networking depth: your design of VPC tiers, security groups, and flow logs will be stronger than a typical full-stack candidate's, so make that visible.

tasks.title: Map Azure Security Networking onto an AWS VPC + IAM Baseline
tasks.description: Deliberately translate what you already know rather than learning AWS from zero. Build a three-tier VPC (public/private/data subnets across two AZs) with security groups mirroring your NSG design, NACLs as the stateless analogue, route tables and NAT gateways replacing your UDR patterns, VPC flow logs standing in for Azure Monitor network diagnostics, and least-privilege IAM roles replacing Azure RBAC assignments. Write the mapping down - it is an interview talking point that most full-stack candidates cannot produce.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform module provisioning VPC, multi-AZ subnets, security groups, NAT gateways, flow logs and scoped IAM roles, plus an Azure-to-AWS equivalence doc (NSG->SG, UDR->route tables, Azure Firewall->AWS Network Firewall, Log Analytics->CloudWatch Logs Insights).

tasks.title: Deploy the Containerized App to ECS Fargate behind an ALB
tasks.description: Take the Phase 1-2 application and run it as a real service: ECS Fargate task definition and service behind an Application Load Balancer, a target group with health checks, RDS Postgres in the private data tier, ElastiCache Redis in place of your local container, secrets pulled from Secrets Manager at runtime, and an autoscaling policy on CPU/request count. Prove zero-downtime rollout and rollback with ECS deployment circuit breakers.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-defined ECS Fargate service + ALB + RDS + ElastiCache + Secrets Manager, a green/blue or rolling deployment runbook including rollback steps, and evidence of a zero-downtime release.

tasks.title: Instrument the Stack with Logs, Metrics, Traces, and Alarms
tasks.description: Reproduce on AWS the monitoring discipline you already run in Azure Monitor and Log Analytics. Emit structured JSON logs with correlation IDs, instrument the API with OpenTelemetry traces spanning the ALB, service, Postgres, and Redis, and build CloudWatch dashboards plus alarms for error rate, p95 latency, queue depth, and DB connections.
tasks.deliverable: CloudWatch dashboard and alarm set with an SNS notification path, structured logging with request correlation IDs, and an OTel trace demonstrating an end-to-end request through app -> Postgres -> Redis.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: The largest conceptual gap between your current role and a full-stack engineering offer is system design. This phase teaches you to reason about correctness, failure, and scale in a payments context, and to implement the patterns interviewers probe hardest - idempotency, webhooks, and consistent data under load - reusing the infrastructure you built in Phase 3.

tasks.title: Design a Stripe-Style Payment Platform End to End
tasks.description: Produce a complete design document for a payments platform: merchant onboarding, an idempotent charge API, a ledger with double-entry bookkeeping, webhook delivery, and reconciliation. Cover C4 context/container diagrams, sequence diagrams for happy path and failure paths, capacity and QPS estimates, storage choices, consistency tradeoffs (why a ledger cannot be eventually consistent), and an explicit failure-mode analysis. Defend every decision in writing the way you would defend a firewall policy change to a CAB.
tasks.deliverable: 8-12 page design doc with C4 and sequence diagrams, capacity math, a consistency/durability argument, and a written failure-mode and rollback analysis.

tasks.title: Implement Idempotency Keys and Verified Webhook Delivery
tasks.description: Build the two patterns that separate payments engineering from CRUD: exactly-once effects over at-least-once transport. Add an idempotency key layer that stores request fingerprints and replays prior responses without double-charging, implement a Stripe-style webhook sender with HMAC signature verification, timestamped replay protection, exponential-backoff retries, and a dead-letter path, and make the receiver idempotent. Test it adversarially against duplicate and out-of-order delivery.
tasks.deliverable: Idempotency-key middleware backed by Postgres/Redis, signed webhook sender and verifier with retry and DLQ handling, and integration tests that inject duplicate, replayed, and out-of-order events.

tasks.title: Scale the Data Layer: Pooling, Replicas, Partitioning, and Caching
tasks.description: Remove the single-node assumptions from your project. Introduce connection pooling, route read-heavy traffic to a read replica and measure replication lag, partition the highest-volume table (e.g. events or ledger entries) and show query-plan improvement, and layer the Phase 2 Redis cache over read paths with a documented stale-read budget. Include what breaks first at 10x, 100x, and 1000x traffic and the mitigation order.
tasks.deliverable: Load-test benchmark report comparing baseline vs pooled vs replica-routed vs cached reads (throughput, p95/p99, lag), EXPLAIN plans before/after partitioning, and a phase-and-justify scaling plan.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert built artifacts into offers. Consolidate the work from Phases 1-4 into a coherent public portfolio, drill the practical interview formats Stripe favors (bug-squash, integration, and design rounds) rather than only abstract algorithms, and reframe your Accenture security operations experience as engineering impact - incident ownership, risk reduction, and automation metrics.

tasks.title: Ship a Public, Deployed Portfolio Project with a Strong README
tasks.description: Consolidate Phases 1-4 into one presentable artifact: the deployed payments-flavored API and a minimal front end on top of it, running on the AWS stack from Phase 3, with a README that leads with architecture, then tradeoffs, then run instructions. Include the CI badge, the Terraform, the load-test numbers, and the design doc so a reviewer can judge you in five minutes.
tasks.deliverable: Live demo URL on AWS, public repo with architecture diagram and CI badge, seeded demo data, and a README linking the design doc, load-test report, and infrastructure code.

tasks.title: Drill Stripe-Style Practical Coding and Debugging Rounds
tasks.description: Stripe interviews are practical: integration and bug-squash exercises in an unfamiliar repository, often in the language of your choice. Train for that format specifically - extend a small unfamiliar codebase against a written spec, debug seeded faults under time pressure, and describe your reasoning out loud. Pair this with a focused set of ~50 data-structure and complexity problems to cover the algorithmic baseline, tracking weak topics for repetition.
tasks.deliverable: Three completed timed bug-squash/integration mock exercises with written post-mortems, plus a 50-problem log with complexity notes and a list of repeated weak areas.

tasks.title: Rehearse System Design Interviews and Reframe Your Security Experience
tasks.description: Run your Phase 4 design doc as a live whiteboard interview for a payments/API prompt, scored against a rubric covering requirements clarification, estimates, data model, scaling, and failure handling. In parallel, convert your Accenture work into engineering narratives: managing enterprise firewall policy at scale, end-to-end incident ownership with RCA, rule-base audits that removed overly permissive access, and ticket SLA performance - each mapped to a STAR story about impact and measurement.
tasks.deliverable: Three recorded mock system-design interviews scored against a rubric with a fix-list per round, and six written STAR stories with quantified impact drawn from your cloud/network security work.

careerPlans.summary: A 10-14 week plan that converts deep Azure/Palo Alto network-security experience into a Full Stack Engineer offer at Stripe by closing the five identified gaps in dependency order. Phase 1 builds the substrate: a containerized TypeScript/Node + Postgres app with tests and quality gates. Phase 2 attacks the highest-priority gaps at production depth - hardened Docker images, a multi-stage GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline with gates and approvals, and Redis as a real cache/coordination layer. Phase 3 maps your VPC/NSG/UDR and Azure Monitor strengths onto their AWS equivalents and deploys the app to ECS Fargate with RDS, ElastiCache, and full observability. Phase 4 targets the largest conceptual gap, system design, by designing and then implementing a Stripe-style payment flow with idempotency, signed webhooks, and a scaling strategy for the data layer. Phase 5 consolidates everything into a deployed portfolio and drills the practical bug-squash, integration, and design interview formats Stripe uses, reframing your security operations tenure as measurable engineering impact. Each task names a concrete artifact, so progress is inspectable rather than self-reported - by the end you hold a deployed payments-flavored full-stack system plus the numbers and design docs to defend it.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Build the container-first foundation every Full Stack Engineer is hired to have. The candidate's strength is infrastructure policy (Azure Firewall, NSGs, UDRs, Palo Alto) but their delivery loop is manual and console-driven; this phase forces the app, its tests, and its quality gates to be reproducible inside a container and enforced by an automated pipeline, which is the prerequisite for the Docker and CI/CD gaps.

tasks.title: Containerize the Full-Stack Reference App
tasks.description: Take a real app (React/Next.js frontend + Node/Express or FastAPI backend + Postgres) and define it entirely in containers instead of local installs. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile per service (deps -> build -> runtime), a .dockerignore, and a docker-compose.yml wiring frontend, backend, and Postgres with named volumes, a shared user-defined network, .env-driven config, bind mounts for hot reload, and a Postgres healthcheck with depends_on. Prove it from a clean machine with one command.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile for frontend and backend plus docker-compose.yml with named volumes, healthchecks and hot reload; a README section showing `docker compose up` booting the full stack on a clean machine.

tasks.title: Enforce Language-Level Quality Gates
tasks.description: Harden the baseline: TypeScript strict mode (or mypy/pyright for Python), ESLint + Prettier (or Ruff + Black), and a Husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook that blocks non-conforming commits. Define lint, typecheck, format and test as npm/Make scripts so the exact same commands run locally, inside the Docker build, and in the pipeline. This is the quality gate your CI job will later call - no re-implementation in YAML.
tasks.deliverable: Committed ESLint/Prettier (or Ruff/Black) config, strict tsconfig (or mypy config), Husky pre-commit hook, and a Makefile/npm scripts contract used identically by local dev and CI.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Automated Test Suite
tasks.description: Prove the app is testable in isolation, the way a pipeline tests it. Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests for API routes that run against a real Postgres started with Testcontainers (or a dedicated compose service). Cover one happy path, one validation failure, one auth/permission denial for the core resource, and one Redis-backed cache hit/miss. Emit a coverage report and set a coverage threshold that fails the run when breached.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest/Jest + Supertest (or Pytest) suite running against a Testcontainers Postgres with a Redis test service, a coverage report with an enforced threshold, and a `test` script that needs no pre-started database.

tasks.title: GitHub Actions CI Pipeline with Lint and Test Matrix
tasks.description: Wire the container-first loop into continuous integration. Create a GitHub Actions workflow triggered on pull_request and push to main that installs dependencies with lockfile-based caching, runs lint/typecheck, runs the test suite with a Postgres and Redis service container, and builds (but does not push) the Docker images using buildx with layer caching. Add a matrix over the supported Node/Python versions, upload coverage as an artifact, and enable branch protection requiring green checks before merge.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with lint + test matrix and a buildx image-build job (cache-enabled), coverage artifact, and enabled branch protection with a link to a passing PR run.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Close the Docker and Redis gaps to a production bar. Phase 1 made the stack runnable and tested in containers; this phase makes those images small, non-root and scanned, models a realistic six-service distributed stack locally, and introduces Redis as a first-class component (cache-aside, sessions, rate limiting) rather than an afterthought.

tasks.title: Production-Grade Image Hardening
tasks.description: Rebuild the images for production: slim/alpine or distroless bases, run as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem where possible, copy only built artifacts into the runtime stage, pin base image digests, set OCI labels, and produce multi-arch builds. Order Dockerfile layers so dependency layers cache across code-only changes. Measure before/after size and wasted layers with `docker image ls` and `dive`, and handle SIGTERM for graceful shutdown.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfile producing a sub-300MB non-root runtime image with a pinned digest, committed .dockerignore, SIGTERM handling, and a size/layer comparison report (dev vs production).

tasks.title: Six-Service Local Orchestration with Compose
tasks.description: Model the distributed stack you will later deploy: frontend, API, background worker, Postgres, Redis, and an Nginx reverse proxy. Use a base compose file plus dev and prod overrides, separate frontend/backend/data-tier networks so Postgres and Redis are unreachable from the edge, healthcheck-gated depends_on, CPU/memory limits, and JSON-file log rotation. Seed the database and confirm data and cache survive a full down/up cycle.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml + override files orchestrating six services with isolated networks, healthchecks, resource limits and log rotation; a verified down/up cycle preserving volumes plus a service-topology diagram.

tasks.title: Redis Caching, Sessions and Rate Limiting
tasks.description: Learn Redis as a working component, not a buzzword. Implement a cache-aside layer for a hot read endpoint with explicit TTLs and key-namespacing; move session storage from in-memory to Redis so multiple API replicas share sessions; add a sliding-window rate limiter using atomic INCR/EXPIRE (or a Lua script); and use a sorted set for a leaderboard/feed-style query. Benchmark the cached vs uncached endpoint, record hit rate, and document an invalidation strategy and a cold-cache stampede guard.
tasks.deliverable: Redis-backed cache-aside module, Redis session store, sliding-window rate limiter, and a benchmark report with hit-rate and p95 latency before/after plus a written invalidation and stampede-protection strategy.

tasks.title: Container Security and Supply-Chain Scanning in CI
tasks.description: Bring your security-operations instincts from Azure/Palo Alto into the build pipeline: treat images as untrusted artifacts. Scan images with Trivy (or Grype) for CVEs, generate an SBOM with Syft, strip secrets from layers, and adopt a secrets strategy (BuildKit build secrets / injected env rather than baked-in keys). Add the scanner as a CI job that fails on HIGH/CRITICAL findings, and document remediation of at least three real findings.
tasks.deliverable: CI-integrated Trivy scan job with fail-on-severity policy, generated SBOM, secrets-handling policy, and a remediation log showing three CVEs found and fixed.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the Dockerized stack as code. The candidate already reasons fluently about VPCs, subnets, route tables, NSGs and user-defined routes in Azure - this phase explicitly maps that mental model onto AWS (VPC, subnets, route tables, security groups, NACLs, IGW/NAT) and then adds managed compute, data, and an OIDC-based CI/CD deployment path.

tasks.title: AWS Account Baseline with Least-Privilege IAM as Code
tasks.description: Build the foundation the same disciplined way you administer Azure policy. Create a non-root admin identity with MFA, a least-privilege IAM role and user for deployment, AWS CLI v2 profiles, and a billing budget with an alarm. Provision all of it with Terraform (or CDK) in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking and encrypted state - no console clicking. Compare each construct against its Azure equivalent (IAM role vs Entra RBAC, SCP vs Azure Policy) in a written mapping.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles/policies, budget alarms and an S3 + DynamoDB remote state backend, plus an Azure-to-AWS identity/authorization mapping table.

tasks.title: Design the AWS Network Layer from Your Azure VPC Experience
tasks.description: Reproduce, in AWS, the network control you already run in Azure. In Terraform, build a VPC across two Availability Zones with public and private subnets, an internet gateway, NAT gateways, route tables and user-defined routes, security groups with least-privilege ingress, NACLs, and VPC flow logs to CloudWatch Logs. Explicitly translate: Azure VNet -> VPC, Subnet -> Subnet, Route Table/UDR -> Route Table, NSG -> Security Group + NACL, Azure Firewall -> AWS Network Firewall / WAF. Validate with reachability tests that private subnets have no inbound internet path.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform VPC module (2 AZs, public/private subnets, IGW, NAT, route tables, SGs, NACLs, flow logs) with a documented Azure-to-AWS control mapping and connectivity test results.

tasks.title: Deploy Containers to ECS Fargate behind an ALB
tasks.description: Ship the Phase 2 production images. Push them to Amazon ECR, define ECS task definitions and a Fargate service spread across two AZs in private subnets, and front it with an Application Load Balancer plus target-group health checks and path-based routing to the API and frontend. Only the ALB is internet-facing; tasks have no public IP. Parameterize the whole stack with Terraform variables for environment, image tag and task sizing, and capture the differences between ECS and your Azure container experience.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned ECR repository, ECS Fargate service (2+ AZs, private subnets) and ALB with health checks; a reachable public URL serving the app plus a deployed-architecture diagram.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Secrets and Redis on AWS
tasks.description: Replace local containers with managed services so the app is production-shaped. Provision RDS Postgres in private subnets with a security group that accepts traffic only from the ECS service, a versioned S3 bucket with a least-privilege bucket policy for uploads, ElastiCache for Redis in the data tier reachable only from the ECS tasks, and Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store) for DB credentials, Redis endpoints and app secrets injected at task start. Run migrations against RDS and confirm the cache layer works against ElastiCache.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned RDS + S3 + ElastiCache Redis + Secrets Manager, security-group wiring restricting DB/cache access to ECS, a migration executed against RDS, and proof of a file upload persisted to S3 and a cache round-trip against ElastiCache.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives'. This phase adds the operational depth - observability, autoscaling under real load, Redis at scale with asynchronous processing, and multi-environment cost and recovery discipline - that turns a candidate with strong security operations into a Full Stack Engineer who can own a production system end to end.

tasks.title: Observability, Alarms and Request Correlation
tasks.description: Apply the monitoring discipline you already practice in Azure Monitor and Log Analytics to CloudWatch. Emit structured JSON logs with request IDs, ship them to CloudWatch Logs with retained retention policies and metric filters, publish custom business and latency metrics (or embedded metric format), and build a dashboard covering request rate, p95 latency, error rate, ECS CPU/memory and Redis hit rate. Create alarms on error rate, p95 latency, unhealthy ALB targets and Redis evictions, and trace one request across ALB -> API -> Redis -> worker via correlation IDs. Write the Azure Monitor/Log Analytics to CloudWatch translation table.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, at least four alarms (error rate, p95 latency, unhealthy targets, Redis evictions), a documented correlation-ID trace of one request, and an Azure Monitor to CloudWatch mapping table.

tasks.title: Redis at Scale and Asynchronous Workloads
tasks.description: Remove synchronous bottlenecks and prove the cache is safe under scale. Extend the cache-aside layer with cache warming, negative caching and a distributed lock (SET NX PX) so concurrent misses do not stampede the database; instrument hit rate and eviction metrics and tune maxmemory-policy. Move slow work (email, image processing, report generation) to a background worker consuming an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue and idempotent processing, containerize the worker with its own image, and run it as a separate ECS service that shares Redis with the API.
tasks.deliverable: Redis cache layer with warming, negative caching and a distributed lock, plus an SQS-backed worker as a separate ECS service with a DLQ; a before/after benchmark showing latency and DB-load reduction.

tasks.title: Autoscaling and Load Testing Under Real Traffic
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it with numbers. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling using target tracking on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target, define min/max task counts and cooldowns, then drive load with k6 (or Locust) against the deployed endpoint. Capture p95 latency, throughput and error rate at each stage, identify the first bottleneck (API, database, or cache) and fix it, and define an SLO with the scaling policy tuned to meet it.
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies (CPU + ALB request count) with tuned min/max and cooldowns, a k6/Locust load-test script, and a load-test report (throughput, p95, errors) showing scale-out behaviour and the identified bottleneck.

tasks.title: Multi-Environment Terraform, Cost Control and Disaster Recovery
tasks.description: Make the infrastructure repeatable, affordable and recoverable. Parameterize Terraform into dev/staging/prod workspaces (or var-files) with environment-specific sizing and deploy a second environment end to end from the same modules. Produce an AWS Cost Explorer analysis with three applied optimizations (rightsizing Fargate tasks, RDS instance class, Redis node type or reserved capacity where justified) and document an RTO/RPO backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3, then actually rehearse it.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-environment Terraform (dev/staging/prod) with a second deployed stack, a cost analysis with three applied optimizations and before/after monthly estimate, and a tested backup/restore DR runbook with measured recovery time.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the hands-on work into interview performance. Every artifact from Phases 1-4 becomes a story, a diagram and a defensible design decision aimed squarely at the Stripe Full Stack Engineer loop: system design, container/cloud depth, and a portfolio that demonstrates production judgement.

tasks.title: System Design Drills Anchored in Your Own Stack
tasks.description: Practice designing out loud, using the architecture you actually built as the reference. Write design docs for three prompts - a payments-adjacent idempotent transaction API, a multi-tenant SaaS API, and an image-upload/processing pipeline - covering API contracts, data model, idempotency keys, caching with Redis, queueing, container/hosting topology on AWS, scaling, consistency and failure modes. Draw boxes-and-arrows diagrams and rehearse each to a 35-minute whiteboard timebox.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design documents with architecture diagrams, tradeoff tables for caching/queueing/idempotency choices, and a self-review noting where an interviewer would push back.

tasks.title: Harden and Document the Portfolio Repository
tasks.description: Turn the project into evidence. Consolidate code, Terraform, compose files, CI workflows, tests, SBOM and runbooks into one clean public repository with a strong README: problem statement, architecture diagram, tech stack, `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment guide, screenshots, cost notes, load-test results and CVE remediation log. Add a one-command demo path so a reviewer can run it without asking questions.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with an architecture diagram, Docker quickstart, AWS deployment guide, screenshots and a RESUME.md mapping each project capability to a resume bullet.

tasks.title: AWS Knowledge Consolidation and Practice Exams
tasks.description: Turn practical AWS experience into interview-grade fluency. Work the core SAA-C03 (or Cloud Practitioner as a checkpoint) domains: IAM, VPC/networking and security groups, ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, S3, ElastiCache, SQS/SNS, CloudWatch and cost models. Summarize each service into a one-page cheat sheet emphasizing how it differs from its Azure counterpart, and sit at least three timed practice exams, reviewing every wrong answer down to the service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: AWS service cheat sheets for 10+ services with Azure comparisons, and three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log targeting consistent 80%+.

tasks.title: Mock Interviews and STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full Full Stack Engineer loop: a live coding round (containerized app plus a tested API endpoint), a Docker/CI/AWS deep-dive, and behavioral questions. Build a STAR story bank from real Phase 1-4 work and from your Azure/Palo Alto security operations record, quantifying wherever possible - reduced image size from 1.2GB to under 200MB, diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop, cut a hot endpoint p95 by 60% with Redis, eliminated 40+ overly permissive Palo Alto rules. Run two recorded or peer mock interviews and log every question with a tightened answer.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock-interview sessions, a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist.

careerPlans.summary: A roughly 10-13 week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a Cloud & Network Security Engineer moving into a Full Stack Engineer role at Stripe, built specifically around the five priority gaps: Docker, CI/CD, System Design, AWS and Redis. It is sequenced so each phase feeds the next - Phase 1 makes the app runnable, testable and lint-gated inside containers with a GitHub Actions matrix; Phase 2 hardens images, orchestrates a six-service compose stack and makes Redis a real component (cache-aside, sessions, rate limiting); Phase 3 lifts that stack onto AWS as code, explicitly translating the candidate's existing Azure VNet/NSG/UDR/Palo Alto mental model into VPC, subnets, route tables, security groups and Network Firewall, then deploys ECS Fargate behind an ALB with RDS, ElastiCache, S3, Secrets Manager and OIDC-based CI/CD; Phase 4 adds production depth with CloudWatch observability, autoscaling under real load, Redis at scale with SQS async workers, multi-environment Terraform and a rehearsed DR runbook; and Phase 5 converts every artifact into interview-ready system design docs, a documented portfolio repository, AWS exam fluency and metric-backed STAR stories. Each task names the exact gap it closes and produces a concrete, inspectable deliverable. Saved to /me/career-roadmaps/full-stack-engineer-roadmap.json.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Boot the application-development baseline the candidate has not yet exercised: a Full Stack app (React/Next.js + Node or FastAPI + Postgres) that runs from one command, is covered by tests, and passes automated checks. Because the candidate's experience is Azure/Palo Alto security operations rather than shipping product code, this phase deliberately builds the container-first loop (Docker), the automated gate (CI/CD), and the code-quality discipline that every later phase - Redis caching, ECS deployment, system design - depends on. Nothing here is generic: each task wires Docker, CI/CD, or testing into this specific reference app.

tasks.title: Containerize the Reference Full-Stack App End-to-End
tasks.description: Build the app the rest of this roadmap deploys: a React/Next.js frontend, a Node/Express (or FastAPI) API, and Postgres. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile for the API (deps -> build -> runtime) and one for the frontend, then a docker-compose.yml wiring frontend, API, and Postgres with a named volume for DB data, an isolated network, .env-driven configuration, and a Postgres healthcheck. Add bind mounts for hot reload in dev. This closes the Docker gap from the first line of code rather than bolting it on later.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile per service plus a docker-compose.yml with named volumes, isolated network, healthcheck and hot reload; README section proving `docker compose up` boots the whole stack on a clean machine.

tasks.title: Enforce Code-Quality Gates Inside the Container
tasks.description: Adopt the quality bar a Full Stack Engineer is expected to ship with. Turn on TypeScript strict mode (or mypy/pyright for Python), configure ESLint + Prettier (or Ruff + Black), add a Husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook that blocks non-conforming commits, and expose `lint`/`typecheck` npm scripts that run identically on the host and inside the Docker image built in task_1_1.
tasks.deliverable: Committed ESLint/Prettier (or Ruff/Black) config, strict tsconfig (or mypy config), a working Husky pre-commit hook, and documented lint/typecheck scripts reused by the Docker build.

tasks.title: First CI/CD Pipeline: Lint + Typecheck + Test Matrix
tasks.description: Create the GitHub Actions workflow that will grow into the deployment pipeline. On every pull request, install dependencies with caching, run lint and typecheck, run the test suite, and build the Docker images without pushing. Use a matrix across the supported Node/Python versions, upload the coverage artifact, and enable branch protection requiring green checks before merge. This is the first concrete step of the CI/CD gap.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with lint/typecheck/test matrix plus an image-build job, dependency caching, coverage artifact upload, and branch protection requiring green checks; link to a passing PR run.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Automated Test Suite with Testcontainers
tasks.description: Make the app provably testable the way it will be tested in a pipeline. Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests for API routes that run against a real, containerized Postgres started by Testcontainers (or a dedicated compose service). Cover one happy path, one validation failure, and one auth/permission case for the core resource, and make the same `test` command run locally and in the Phase 1 CI pipeline.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest/Jest + Supertest (or Pytest) suite running integration tests against a Testcontainers Postgres, a committed coverage report, and a `test` script that needs no manually pre-started database.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Deep-dive the two container-adjacent priority gaps - Docker and CI/CD - to a production bar, and plant the first Redis workload. Phase 1 produced images and a pipeline; this phase makes the images small, hardened, and supply-chain-scanned, turns the pipeline into a real delivery pipeline with environments and promotion, orchestrates a multi-service stack, and introduces Redis as the cache/queue substrate the candidate will later host on ElastiCache.

tasks.title: Production-Grade Image Optimization and Hardening
tasks.description: Rebuild the API and frontend images for production: slim/alpine or distroless base images, non-root runtime user, only build artifacts copied into the runtime stage, a real .dockerignore, OCI provenance labels, pinned base-image digests, multi-arch builds, and layer ordering so dependency layers cache across code-only changes. Measure before/after size with `docker image ls` and `dive`.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfiles producing sub-300MB runtime images running as non-root with pinned digests, a committed .dockerignore, and a size/layer report comparing dev vs production images.

tasks.title: Multi-Service Orchestration with Redis in the Stack
tasks.description: Model a realistic distributed stack locally: frontend, API, background worker, Postgres, Redis, and an Nginx reverse proxy. The API reads a hot endpoint through a Redis cache-aside path and the worker consumes jobs from a Redis list or stream, with Redis configured with a password, a maxmemory policy, and AOF/RDB persistence settings you can explain. Provide dev and prod compose files with overrides, custom networks isolating the DB and Redis from the public tier, healthcheck-based depends_on, resource limits, and JSON log rotation.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml + override/prod files orchestrating six services (including Redis with password, maxmemory policy and persistence) with isolated networks, healthchecks, resource limits and log rotation, a verified `docker compose down && up` preserving volumes, and a service-topology diagram.

tasks.title: Delivery Pipeline: Build, Push, Version, and Promote
tasks.description: Grow the Phase 1 CI workflow into a delivery pipeline. On merge to main, build versioned Docker images tagged with the git SHA and semantic version, push them to a registry, and gate promotion through environment stages (dev -> staging) using GitHub Environments with required reviewers. Use buildx layer caching, job caching for dependencies, concurrency groups to cancel superseded runs, and manually-triggered `workflow_dispatch` rollbacks to a previous image tag.
tasks.deliverable: A build-and-push workflow with SHA + semver image tags, GitHub Environments with manual approval gates for promotion, buildx layer caching, concurrency control, and a demonstrated rollback run to a previously pushed tag.

tasks.title: Supply-Chain Scanning and Secrets Hygiene in CI
tasks.description: Treat images and dependencies as untrusted artifacts. Add Trivy (or Grype) image scanning and `npm audit`/Dependabot dependency scanning as CI jobs that fail on HIGH/CRITICAL findings, generate an SBOM with Syft and attach it as a retained artifact, scan the repo for committed secrets with Gitleaks, and adopt a secrets strategy that injects values at runtime/build-secrets instead of baking them into layers. This reuses the candidate's real security-operations instincts in a build-pipeline context.
tasks.deliverable: CI jobs for Trivy image scan, dependency audit and Gitleaks secret scan with HIGH/CRITICAL failure thresholds, a generated and retained SBOM file, a documented secrets-handling policy, and a remediation log of three real CVEs or leaked-secret findings fixed.

tasks.title: Container and Cache Debugging Runbook
tasks.description: Learn to operate containers rather than only build them. Reproduce and diagnose five incidents using `docker logs`, `exec`, `stats`, `inspect`, and `events`: a crash loop, an OOM kill, a port conflict, a service-to-service DNS failure, and a Redis connection-refused/timeout. Apply memory and CPU limits, demonstrate graceful SIGTERM shutdown, and write down the symptom, root cause, and fix you actually verified - the same incident-response framing the candidate already uses for security incidents.
tasks.deliverable: Container/cache debugging runbook covering five reproduced incidents with root cause and fix, a demonstrated SIGTERM graceful-shutdown, and a `docker stats` before/after report under applied resource limits.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by moving the Dockerized stack onto managed cloud infrastructure provisioned as code, and by translating the candidate's deep Azure networking and firewall expertise into AWS equivalents (VNet -> VPC, NSG/UDR -> Security Groups, NACLs and route tables, Azure Firewall -> WAF/NAT/security-group egress design). Phase 2 built the artifacts; this phase deploys them to ECR/ECS Fargate with RDS, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis, driven by an OIDC-based deployment pipeline.

tasks.title: AWS Landing Zone as Code: VPC, IAM, and Azure->AWS Network Translation
tasks.description: Stand up a clean AWS foundation entirely in Terraform (or AWS CDK) with remote state in S3 + DynamoDB locking: a VPC with public/private subnets across two AZs, internet and NAT gateways, and route tables, plus a least-privilege deployment IAM role, MFA on the root/admin identity, and a billing budget alarm. Write a mapping document translating each Azure concept the candidate already operates (VNet, subnets, NSG rules, UDRs, Azure Firewall policy) to its AWS counterpart (VPC, subnets, security groups, route tables, NACLs, WAF/NAT), and design egress so only the ALB is internet-facing.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning VPC/subnets/route tables/NAT, least-privilege IAM, and S3+DynamoDB remote state; a committed Azure-to-AWS networking mapping document; a budget alarm screenshot.

tasks.title: Deploy Containers to ECR + ECS Fargate behind an ALB
tasks.description: Take the Phase 2 production images to the cloud. Push them to Amazon ECR, define ECS task definitions and a Fargate service spread across two AZs in private subnets, and front it with an Application Load Balancer and target group with health checks. Use a security-group model where the ALB accepts public traffic and the ECS tasks only accept traffic from the ALB, mirroring the least-privilege traffic-flow design the candidate enforces today. Provision all of it in Terraform with variable-driven environments.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned ECR repository, ECS Fargate service (2+ AZs, private subnets), and ALB with health checks; a reachable public URL serving the app plus a deployed-architecture diagram including security-group boundaries.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Storage, and Secrets on AWS
tasks.description: Replace local containers with managed services. Provision RDS Postgres in private subnets whose security group accepts connections only from the ECS service, a versioned S3 bucket with a least-privilege bucket policy for uploads, and AWS Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store) for DB credentials and app secrets injected at task start instead of at build time. Run the schema migration against RDS and confirm the app reads and writes managed data and uploads a file to S3.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned RDS Postgres + versioned S3 bucket + Secrets Manager entries, security groups restricting DB access to ECS only, a migration executed against RDS, and proof of a file upload persisted to S3.

tasks.title: Keyless CI/CD to AWS with OIDC and Automated Rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery without long-lived AWS keys. Configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a scoped trust policy, then extend the Phase 2 pipeline to build the image, push to ECR, render the new task definition, and perform a rolling ECS deployment that waits for service stability. Add a manual approval gate for production, deploy-failure alarms, and a documented and tested rollback (re-deploy the previous task revision).
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based GitHub Actions deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS rolling deploy) with a scoped IAM trust policy, production approval gate, and a tested rollback procedure with logs showing a successful deploy and a successful rollback.

tasks.title: ElastiCache Redis: Managed Caching and Queues
tasks.description: Move the Phase 2 Redis workload onto Amazon ElastiCache. Provision an ElastiCache Redis cluster (or replication group with a read replica) in private subnets, reachable only from the ECS task security group, with encryption in transit and at rest and an auth token stored in Secrets Manager. Point the API cache-aside path and the worker's job queue at it, demonstrate a cache hit/miss and eviction policy, and benchmark the hot endpoint with Redis on versus off.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned ElastiCache Redis (private subnets, TLS, auth token from Secrets Manager), app wired to the managed cache with a documented hit-rate, and a before/after latency benchmark of the cached endpoint.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move the deployed system from 'it runs' to 'it survives load and failure'. This phase builds the operational depth - observability, autoscaling under measured load, Redis-backed caching and async processing at scale, and system design reasoning about the candidate's own architecture - that distinguishes a mid-level from a senior Full Stack Engineer. The observability work deliberately maps the candidate's Azure Monitor / Log Analytics experience onto CloudWatch and OpenTelemetry.

tasks.title: Observability: Structured Logging, Metrics, Dashboards, and Alarms
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end. Emit structured JSON logs with a request ID, ship them to CloudWatch Logs, and publish custom business and latency metrics via the CloudWatch SDK or embedded metric format. Build a CloudWatch dashboard (request rate, p95 latency, error rate, ECS CPU/memory, Redis hit-rate) and at least three alarms on error-rate, p95 latency, and unhealthy targets. Explicitly document how each signal maps to the Azure Monitor / Log Analytics dashboards and alerts the candidate administers today.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, three or more alarms (error rate, p95 latency, unhealthy targets), a request-ID trace across ALB -> API -> worker, and a written Azure Monitor/Log Analytics-to-CloudWatch observability mapping.

tasks.title: Autoscaling and Load Testing Under Real Traffic
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target-tracking on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target, then generate load with k6 (or Locust) against the deployed endpoint. Capture p95 latency, throughput, and error rate before and after scale-out, tune the target value, cooldowns and min/max task counts to a defined SLO, and verify the Redis cache keeps the read path from collapsing the DB under peak load.
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies (CPU + ALB request count) with tuned min/max, a k6/Locust load-test script, and a load-test report (throughput, p95, error rate) showing scale-out behaviour and DB protection via the cache.

tasks.title: Redis Caching Patterns and Asynchronous Processing at Scale
tasks.description: Remove synchronous bottlenecks and go deeper on Redis. Implement and compare at least three patterns on a real endpoint - cache-aside, write-through (or write-behind), and a rate limiter using Redis atomic counters or a sliding window (or a distributed lock) - and choose data structures deliberately (hashes for objects, sorted sets for leaderboards/rate windows, TTLs and eviction policies). Move slow work (email, image processing, report generation) to a background worker consuming an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue and idempotent processing, and run that worker as a separate ECS service.
tasks.deliverable: Redis cache-aside plus rate-limiter (or write-through) implementations with a written pattern-comparison and measured hit-rate/latency improvement, an SQS-backed worker as a separate ECS service with a DLQ and idempotency keys, and before/after benchmarks.

tasks.title: System Design of Your Own Stack, Multi-Environment, and Cost Control
tasks.description: Turn the built system into a designed system. Write an architecture decision record set for your stack covering API contract, data model, caching, queueing, container/hosting topology on AWS, scaling, and failure modes, with explicit tradeoffs and a capacity estimate (requests/sec, cache size, DB connections). Then parameterize Terraform into dev/staging/prod with environment-specific sizing, stand up staging end to end, and produce an AWS Cost Explorer analysis with three applied optimizations (rightsizing Fargate, RDS instance class, cache/queue savings), plus an RTO/RPO backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3.
tasks.deliverable: Architecture decision records with a capacity plan and tradeoff tables, multi-environment Terraform (dev/staging/prod) with a deployed staging stack, a cost analysis with three applied optimizations, and a tested RDS/S3 backup-and-restore DR runbook with measured recovery time.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the hands-on build into interview performance against the Full Stack Engineer loop. Every deliverable from Phases 1-4 becomes a story, a diagram, or a defensible design decision. This phase rehearses system design out loud, consolidates AWS knowledge into exam-grade fluency while framing the Azure background as an asset, hardens the portfolio repository, and drills STAR answers anchored in real metrics.

tasks.title: System Design Drills Anchored in the Built Stack
tasks.description: Practice designing systems out loud using your own deployed architecture as the reference. Produce written design docs for three prompts - a URL shortener, a multi-tenant SaaS API, and a payments-style idempotent write API relevant to Stripe - covering API contracts, data model, caching with Redis, queueing, container/hosting topology on AWS, scaling, idempotency, and failure modes. Whiteboard each with boxes-and-arrows diagrams and time yourself to 35 minutes per prompt.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design documents (URL shortener, multi-tenant SaaS API, idempotent payments write API) with architecture diagrams, tradeoff tables, and a self-review of where an interviewer would push back.

tasks.title: Harden and Document the Portfolio Repository
tasks.description: Turn the project into evidence a hiring manager can inspect. Consolidate the application code, Terraform, compose files, GitHub Actions workflows, tests, and runbooks into one clean public repository with a compelling README: problem statement, architecture diagram, tech stack, local `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment guide, screenshots, cost notes, the CVE remediation log, and the load-test and cache benchmark results from earlier phases.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, Docker quickstart, AWS deployment guide, screenshots, and a RESUME.md mapping each project feature (containers, CI/CD, ECS, Redis caching, observability) to a resume bullet.

tasks.title: AWS Knowledge Consolidation and Azure-to-AWS Narrative
tasks.description: Convert practical AWS experience into exam-grade, interview-ready fluency. Work through the core SAA-C03 domains - IAM, VPC/networking and security groups, ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, S3, SQS, ElastiCache, CloudWatch, and cost models - and summarize each service into a one-page cheat sheet. Sit at least three timed practice exams, review every wrong answer to a service-level explanation, and rehearse a narrative that positions the Azure Firewall/VNet/NSG/Palo Alto background as directly transferable cloud-security depth.
tasks.deliverable: AWS service cheat sheets (10+ services), three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log targeting 80%+, and a rehearsed Azure-to-AWS transferable-skills narrative.

tasks.title: Mock Interviews and STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full Full Stack Engineer loop: a live coding round (add a tested API endpoint to the app), a Docker/AWS/Redis deep-dive, a system design round, and behavioral questions. Build a STAR story bank from your real work - 'cut image size 1.2GB -> 200MB', 'diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop', 'ended a security incident end-to-end at Accenture', 'removed over-permissive firewall rules in a Palo Alto audit' - run two recorded or peer mock interviews, and log every question with a tightened answer.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ stories tied to concrete metrics (including security-operations stories), two recorded mock-interview sessions, a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist.

careerPlans.summary: A 10-week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap built specifically for a Full Stack Engineer (Stripe) candidate whose priority gaps are Docker, CI/CD, System Design, AWS, and Redis, on top of a strong Azure network-security foundation. It is sequenced so each phase feeds the next: Phase 1 establishes a Docker-compressed dev/test/CI loop with code-quality gates; Phase 2 deep-dives Docker and CI/CD (image hardening, multi-service orchestration with Redis, build-push-promote delivery, supply-chain scanning, debugging runbooks); Phase 3 closes the AWS gap by translating the candidate's Azure VNet/NSG/UDR/Firewall expertise into a Terraform-defined AWS VPC and deploying the stack to ECR/ECS Fargate with RDS, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis via keyless OIDC CI/CD with rollback; Phase 4 adds production depth (CloudWatch observability mapped from Azure Monitor, autoscaling under real load, Redis caching patterns and SQS async processing, system design of the built stack, multi-environment and cost control); and Phase 5 converts every artifact into interview-ready system design docs, a documented portfolio repo, AWS exam fluency with an Azure-to-AWS narrative, and metric-backed STAR stories. Each task names the specific gap it closes, cites the candidate's transferable security experience where relevant, and produces a concrete, inspectable deliverable.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Establish a reproducible, container-first delivery baseline. The candidate's depth is in cloud network security operations (Azure Firewall, NSG/UDR policy, CAB-governed change), not application delivery: there is no container, pipeline or test evidence yet. This phase converts the change-control discipline already used for firewall rule governance into engineering discipline - everything the app needs to run, lint and test is declared as code and boots with one command.

tasks.title: Containerize the Local Full-Stack Dev Environment
tasks.description: Pick one reference app (React/TypeScript frontend + Node.js API + PostgreSQL) and declare the whole environment in containers instead of installing anything on the host, mirroring how the candidate administers Azure topology declaratively rather than by hand. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile for the API (deps -> build -> runtime) and a separate one for the frontend, then a docker-compose.yml wiring frontend, API and Postgres with named volumes, an isolated bridge network, environment variables from .env, and a pg_isready healthcheck with depends_on: condition: service_healthy.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile for the API and frontend plus a docker-compose.yml with named volumes, isolated network and a DB healthcheck; README section proving `docker compose up` boots the full stack on a clean machine with no local Node/Postgres install.

tasks.title: Code Quality Gates as Declared Policy
tasks.description: Apply the same 'no unaudited change reaches the rule base' principle to code. Turn on TypeScript strict mode (strict: true, noImplicitAny, noUncheckedIndexedAccess), configure ESLint + Prettier, and add a Husky + lint-staged pre-commit hook that blocks commits failing lint, format or tsc --noEmit. Define npm scripts (lint, format, typecheck, test) executed with identical commands inside the Docker image and in CI, so a local pass predicts a pipeline pass.
tasks.deliverable: Committed eslint.config.js, .prettierrc and strict tsconfig.json with zero type errors, a Husky pre-commit hook, and a documented script set that runs byte-identically in the container and in CI.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Automated Test Suite
tasks.description: Prove the app is testable in isolation, the way a pipeline must test it. Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests for API routes that run against a real Postgres started by Testcontainers (not a mock), covering one happy path, one validation failure and one authorization failure for the core resource. Add a Redis container to the test harness only when Phase 2 introduces caching, and emit a coverage report.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest + Supertest (or Jest) suite running integration tests against a Testcontainers Postgres via `npm test`, with a coverage report showing >=80% on the API layer and no manually pre-started database required.

tasks.title: First CI Pipeline with Lint and Test Matrix
tasks.description: Replace manual change review with an automated pipeline. Create a GitHub Actions workflow triggered on pull_request and push to main that checks out, caches npm deps, runs lint, typecheck and the test suite, then builds both Docker images without pushing. Use a matrix across two Node versions, publish the coverage artifact, and enable branch protection so a red check blocks merge.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with lint, typecheck, test and image-build jobs across a Node version matrix; branch protection enabled and a screenshot of one deliberately-failed PR turning green after the fix.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take Docker from 'it runs' to 'it is safe to ship', and add the caching skill the role lists. Phase 1 gave a working compose stack; this phase hardens the images, models a realistic multi-service topology, treats images as untrusted artifacts in CI, and introduces Redis so read-path latency becomes a design decision rather than an accident.

tasks.title: Harden and Shrink Production Images
tasks.description: Rebuild images for production: distroless or slim base, pinned base-image digest, dedicated non-root user, only build artifacts copied into the runtime stage, OCI labels, and a complete .dockerignore excluding node_modules, .git and .env. Order layers so dependency installation caches across code edits and no secret is ever baked into a layer. Measure before/after size and layer count with `docker image ls` and `dive`.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfiles producing a <300MB non-root runtime image with a pinned digest, a committed .dockerignore, and a size/layer report comparing dev vs production images.

tasks.title: Multi-Service Topology with Isolated Networks
tasks.description: Model the segmented topology the candidate already reasons about at the network layer, but for application services: frontend, API, background worker, Postgres, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy, with a public edge network and a private data network so the database has no route to the internet. Use docker-compose.yml plus override/prod files, healthcheck-based depends_on, CPU/memory limits, JSON-file log rotation, and seed data that survives `docker compose down && up`.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml with dev/prod overrides orchestrating six services across two isolated networks, with healthchecks, resource limits and log rotation; a topology diagram plus proof that DB volumes persist a restart and that the DB is unreachable from the edge network.

tasks.title: Image Supply-Chain Scanning and Secrets Hygiene in CI
tasks.description: Treat container images the way the candidate treats an untrusted traffic source: verify before allowing. Add a Trivy (or Grype) scan job to the pipeline that fails the build on HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs, generate an SBOM with Syft and commit it as a release artifact, move all credentials to build-time secrets / runtime env injection, and remove any secret that leaked into a layer (rebuild history to confirm). Remediate at least three real findings and log them.
tasks.deliverable: CI Trivy job failing on HIGH/CRITICAL, committed SBOM file, a secrets-handling policy, and a remediation log of three CVEs found and fixed with before/after scan output.

tasks.title: Redis Cache-Aside Layer with TTL and Invalidation
tasks.description: Add Redis as a compose service and put a cache-aside layer in front of the hottest read endpoint (for example a transaction/ledger summary). Define an explicit key-naming scheme and TTL policy, choose a data structure beyond plain strings (sorted set or hash) where it fits, invalidate or update the key on every write path, and handle cache-stampede and Redis-outage fallback so the API degrades to the database instead of failing.
tasks.deliverable: Redis cache-aside implementation with a documented key/TTL policy, write-path invalidation, and a benchmark report showing hit rate plus p95 latency before vs after caching; a chaos note proving the API still serves traffic with Redis stopped.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by migrating the containerized stack into real AWS infrastructure provisioned as code. The candidate already owns the concepts - VNets and subnets, NSGs, route tables and UDRs, Azure Monitor and Log Analytics - so each AWS service is introduced as the direct equivalent being re-learned with a different API, IAM model and operational semantics, and nothing is done by console clicking.

tasks.title: Reproduce the Known Network Topology as an AWS VPC in Terraform
tasks.description: Provision, as Terraform, the AWS equivalent of the Azure topology the candidate already administers: a VPC with public and private subnets across two AZs, an internet gateway, NAT gateway for egress, route tables with an explicit private-subnet route to the NAT (the UDR equivalent), security groups scoped like NSGs by port and source, network ACLs, and VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch. Add an S3 + DynamoDB remote-state backend and a non-root, MFA-protected IAM identity with least-privilege deploy permissions and a billing budget alarm.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning the VPC, subnets, IGW/NAT, route tables, security groups, Flow Logs and remote state; a side-by-side table mapping each Azure construct (VNet, subnet, NSG, UDR, Azure Firewall) to its AWS counterpart, plus a screenshot of the active budget alarm.

tasks.title: Deploy the Containers to ECR and ECS Fargate behind an ALB
tasks.description: Push the Phase 2 production images to Amazon ECR, define ECS task definitions with CPU/memory and environment-specific secrets references, and run the service on Fargate across two AZs in private subnets, fronted by an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks. Allow inbound traffic only from the ALB security group to the task security group, exactly as an NSG-to-NSG rule would be written. Deploy the worker as a second ECS service with no load balancer.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned ECR repo, ECS Fargate service (2 AZs, private subnets) plus worker service, and an ALB with health checks; a public URL serving the app and a VPC/ECS architecture diagram with the security-group flow between tiers.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Object Storage and Secrets on AWS
tasks.description: Replace local containers with managed services: RDS PostgreSQL in private subnets with a security group accepting 5432 only from the ECS task security group, multi-AZ standby, automated backups and a parameter group; a versioned, encrypted S3 bucket with a least-privilege bucket policy plus a lifecycle rule for uploads; and Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store) entries injected into tasks at start. Run migrations against RDS and verify the app reads/writes managed data.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Postgres + S3 + Secrets Manager, a migration executed against RDS, proof of an upload persisted to S3 and retrieved, and a security-group matrix showing the DB is reachable only from the ECS tier.

tasks.title: Keyless CI/CD to AWS with a Health-Gated Rolling Deploy and Rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery with no static AWS keys: configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role whose trust policy is scoped to the repo and branch. Extend the Phase 1 pipeline to build and push the image to ECR, render the new task definition, and perform a rolling ECS deployment that waits for service stability behind a deployment circuit breaker. Add a manual approval gate for production and document the rollback path (redeploy the previous task revision), then rehearse it against a deliberately broken release - the deployment equivalent of the change rollback already practised through the CAB.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based GitHub Actions deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS rolling deploy) with IAM trust policy, an environment approval gate, and logs of both a successful deploy and a successful rollback after a failed health check.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives and it can be reasoned about'. The candidate's operational strength - monitoring, alerting and incident RCA in Azure Monitor and Log Analytics - transfers directly to CloudWatch; this phase adds the application-level architectural depth (observability, autoscaling under load, asynchronous decoupling, multi-environment cost and recovery discipline) that a senior full-stack system design round probes.

tasks.title: Observability: Structured Logging, Metrics, Dashboards and Alarms
tasks.description: Port the monitoring practice from Azure Monitor and Log Analytics to CloudWatch. Emit structured JSON logs with a request ID from API, worker and frontend BFF, ship them to CloudWatch Logs, and publish custom metrics (requests, latency, cache hit rate, queue depth) via the SDK or embedded metric format. Build a dashboard (request rate, p95 latency, error rate, ECS CPU/memory, RDS connections, Redis evictions) and at least three alarms wired to an SNS topic - for example elevated 5xx rate, p95 latency breach and unhealthy ALB targets - then reproduce one deliberate failure and capture the alarm, the log query and the RCA note.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, three CloudWatch alarms with SNS notification, and one written incident RCA (detection -> triage -> containment -> root cause) produced from a deliberately injected failure, mirroring the candidate's production incident workflow.

tasks.title: Autoscaling and Load Testing to a Defined SLO
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it with numbers. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target-tracking policies on both CPU utilization and ALB request-count-per-target, with tuned min/max tasks and cooldowns, then run k6 (or Locust) scenarios against the deployed endpoint: a steady ramp, a spike, and a soak. Record p95/p99 latency, throughput and error rate before and after scale-out, and tune the target value until the service holds a stated SLO (e.g. p95 < 300ms at 200 rps).
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies (CPU + ALB request count) with tuned min/max, a k6/Locust script set (ramp, spike, soak), and a load-test report with charts showing scale-out behaviour and the achieved SLO.

tasks.title: Asynchronous Processing and Caching at Scale
tasks.description: Remove synchronous bottlenecks from the request path. Move slow work (email, receipt generation, image handling) onto an SQS queue consumed by an idempotent worker - unique message IDs, dedupe table, at-least-once delivery assumed - with a dead-letter queue, visibility-timeout tuning and an alarm on DLQ depth. Extend the Redis layer from Phase 2 to ElastiCache and use it for a second pattern beyond caching (rate limiting or a leaderboard via sorted sets), documenting the eviction policy and failure fallback.
tasks.deliverable: SQS-backed worker deployed as a separate ECS service with a DLQ and depth alarm, an idempotency design note, ElastiCache Redis integration with a documented eviction/fallback policy, and a before/after latency benchmark for the now-asynchronous endpoint.

tasks.title: Multi-Environment Terraform, Cost Control and Disaster Recovery
tasks.description: Make the infrastructure repeatable and affordable. Parameterize Terraform into dev/staging/prod workspaces or var-files with environment-specific sizing, stand up a second environment end to end from the same modules, and confirm it can be destroyed and rebuilt with one apply. Produce a Cost Explorer analysis with three concrete optimizations actually applied (rightsize Fargate task CPU/memory from the load-test data, downsize or reserve the RDS class, quantify Redis/SQS savings), and write an RTO/RPO backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3 that you execute once and time.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-environment Terraform modules with a deployed staging stack, a cost analysis with three applied optimizations and the resulting monthly delta, and a tested backup/restore DR runbook with measured recovery time.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the built artifacts into interview performance. Every deliverable from Phases 1-4 becomes a diagram, a metric and a defensible tradeoff. This phase rehearses application-level system design, consolidates AWS fluency, hardens the portfolio repository, and reframes the candidate's network-security and incident-response experience as transferable strength rather than a pivot risk.

tasks.title: System Design Drills Anchored in the Built Stack
tasks.description: Practice designing systems out loud, using the architecture you actually built as the reference instead of generic templates. Produce three written 35-minute design documents - a high-throughput payments/ledger API, a multi-tenant SaaS backend, and an image upload/processing pipeline - each covering API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy, queueing and idempotency, deployment topology on AWS, scaling limits, and failure modes. Include a tradeoff table per design (SQL vs NoSQL, sync vs async, cache-aside vs write-through) and a self-review noting where an interviewer would push back.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design documents with boxes-and-arrows diagrams, tradeoff tables and a self-critique section; a timed recording of at least one of them delivered aloud.

tasks.title: Harden and Document the Portfolio Repository
tasks.description: Turn the project into inspectable evidence. Consolidate the application code, multi-stage Dockerfiles, compose files, Terraform, GitHub Actions workflows, tests and runbooks into one clean public repository with a README covering the problem statement, architecture diagram, tech stack, one-command `docker compose up` quickstart, the AWS deployment guide, screenshots, the load-test and cache-hit-rate numbers, and the CVE remediation log. Add a short 'security decisions' section (non-root images, least-privilege IAM, security-group segmentation, secrets handling) that shows the security background as an asset for a full-stack role.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, Docker quickstart, AWS deployment guide, screenshots and test/load evidence, plus a RESUME.md mapping each project capability to a resume bullet and the security-decision notes.

tasks.title: AWS Knowledge Consolidation and Practice Exams
tasks.description: Convert hands-on AWS work into interview-grade fluency, using the Azure-to-AWS mapping built in Phase 3 as the study spine. Cover IAM, VPC and networking (security groups vs NACLs, route tables vs UDRs, VPC endpoints), ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SQS/SNS, CloudWatch and cost models. Write one-page cheat sheets for ten or more services and sit at least three timed practice exams (SAA-C03 level), reviewing every wrong answer down to a service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: Ten-plus AWS service cheat sheets (each with its Azure analogue), three timed practice-exam score reports, and a wrong-answer review log targeting consistent 80%+ before booking the real exam.

tasks.title: Mock Interviews and STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full Full Stack Engineer loop: a live coding round (a containerized, tested API endpoint), a Docker/AWS/CI-CD deep dive, a system design round, and behavioral questions. Build a STAR story bank from real Phase 1-4 work and from the current role - e.g. 'cut the runtime image from 1.2GB to under 300MB', 'diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop from CloudWatch metrics', 'migrated an NSG/UDR policy model to AWS security groups and route tables', 'ran a firewall rule-base audit that removed unused and conflicting rules'. Run two recorded mock interviews and log every question with a tightened answer plus a final readiness checklist.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories bridging network-security and full-stack work, two recorded mock-interview sessions with review notes, a question log with revised answers, and a one-page interview readiness checklist.

careerPlans.summary: A 10-week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a Full Stack Engineer (Stripe) candidate whose priority gaps are Docker, CI/CD, System Design, AWS and Redis, and whose current depth is cloud and network security operations (Azure Firewall, VNet/subnets, NSGs, route tables and UDRs, Azure Monitor and Log Analytics, Palo Alto NGFW, CAB-governed change and incident RCA). The plan is sequenced so each phase feeds the next: Phase 1 turns existing change-control discipline into a reproducible container-first dev, test and CI baseline; Phase 2 takes Docker to a production bar with hardened images, a segmented multi-service topology, supply-chain scanning and a Redis cache-aside layer; Phase 3 lifts that stack into AWS provisioned as Terraform, deliberately mapping every known Azure construct (VNet, subnet, NSG, UDR, Azure Monitor) onto its AWS counterpart while adding ECR/ECS Fargate, RDS, S3 and Secrets Manager and a keyless OIDC deploy with a rehearsed rollback; Phase 4 adds production depth with CloudWatch observability and alarm-driven RCA, autoscaling validated by load tests, SQS asynchronous processing with idempotency and DLQs, and multi-environment cost and disaster-recovery discipline; Phase 5 converts every artifact into interviews - system design drills, a documented portfolio repo, AWS exam fluency and a STAR story bank that positions the security background as an advantage. Each of the 20 tasks names the specific gap it closes and produces a concrete, inspectable deliverable such as an optimized multi-stage Dockerfile with a docker-compose topology, a GitHub Actions lint/test matrix and OIDC deploy workflow, a Trivy/SBOM-scanning CI job, a Redis cache-aside implementation with a hit-rate benchmark, a Terraform AWS stack, a k6 load-test report and a CloudWatch alarm-and-RCA write-up.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Rebuild the candidate's daily loop around the two things a Full Stack Engineer at Stripe is assumed to already own: a reproducible containerized environment and an automated quality gate. Today the candidate operates Azure/Palo Alto security controls from tickets and the Change Advisory Board; here they learn to own the code path itself - Docker, tests, and the first CI pipeline - so every later phase has a working build-test-ship loop to build on.

tasks.title: Containerize the Local Full-Stack Dev Environment
tasks.description: Stand up a reference full-stack app (Next.js/React frontend + Node/Express or FastAPI backend + Postgres + Redis) and define it entirely in containers. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile for each service (deps -> build -> runtime), then a docker-compose.yml wiring frontend, API, Postgres and Redis on one named network with named volumes, .env-driven config and a Postgres healthcheck. Add bind mounts for hot reload and document the one-command startup. The candidate's Azure Firewall/NSG work makes them think in flows and policies - translate that instinct into container networks, ports and healthchecks.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile per service plus docker-compose.yml booting the full stack with `docker compose up` from a clean machine; README with quickstart and a diagram of the container network.

tasks.title: Language-Level Quality Gates (strict types + lint + pre-commit)
tasks.description: Enable TypeScript strict mode (or mypy/pyright in strict mode for Python), configure ESLint + Prettier (or Ruff + Black), and add a Husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook plus a commitlint conventional-commit rule. Expose the exact same commands as `lint`, `typecheck` and `format` npm scripts so they can be invoked identically inside the Docker build and inside CI - a single source of truth for code quality.
tasks.deliverable: Committed strict tsconfig (or mypy config), ESLint/Prettier (or Ruff/Black) config, Husky pre-commit hook, commitlint config, and an npm script list that runs unchanged locally and in a container.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Automated Test Suite
tasks.description: Prove the app is testable in isolation, exactly as a pipeline will test it. Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests against a real Postgres spun up with Testcontainers (or a dedicated compose service). Cover one happy path, one validation error, and one authorization/permission case for the core resource - mirroring the least-privilege thinking from the candidate's NSG and firewall-rule work.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest/Jest + Supertest (or Pytest) suite with Testcontainers-backed integration tests, a coverage report (60%+ on the API layer), and a `test` script requiring no pre-started database.

tasks.title: First GitHub Actions CI Pipeline: Lint + Test Matrix + Image Build
tasks.description: Close the zero-CI/CD gap with the smallest useful pipeline. Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every pull request: installs dependencies with caching, runs lint/typecheck, runs the test suite, and builds the Docker images without pushing. Use a matrix over supported Node/Python versions, upload the coverage artifact, and enable branch protection requiring the checks before merge.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with a lint/typecheck/test matrix and an image-build job, branch protection enabled, and a link or screenshot of a green PR pipeline run.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take Docker and CI/CD from 'it runs' to production bar. Images get small, non-root and scanned; the local stack becomes six independently deployable services; and the pipeline becomes a reusable, environment-aware delivery system with smoke tests and rollback. This is the container and pipeline literacy the candidate is missing on paper and must be able to defend in an interview.

tasks.title: Production Image Hardening and Supply-Chain Scanning
tasks.description: Rebuild the images for production: slim/alpine or distroless bases, non-root user, only build artifacts copied into the runtime stage, a proper .dockerignore, OCI labels, multi-arch builds and pinned base-image digests. Layer the Dockerfile so dependency layers cache across code changes. Scan with Trivy, generate an SBOM with Syft, remove any baked-in secrets, and measure before/after size with `docker image ls` and `dive`.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfile producing a runtime image under 300MB running as non-root on a pinned digest, .dockerignore, generated SBOM, Trivy scan report, and a size/layer comparison of dev vs production images.

tasks.title: Multi-Service Orchestration with Dev/Prod Compose Overrides
tasks.description: Model a realistic distributed system locally: frontend, API, background worker, Postgres, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy. Define a base compose file plus dev and prod override files, custom networks that isolate the database tier from the public tier, healthcheck-based `depends_on`, resource limits and JSON-file log rotation. Seed the database and confirm state survives a `down`/`up` cycle.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml plus override/prod files orchestrating six services with tier isolation, healthchecks, resource limits and log rotation; a verified volume-persistence test and a service-topology diagram.

tasks.title: Reusable Parameterized CI with Environment Gates and PR Previews
tasks.description: Level up from a single workflow to a real CI system. Extract a reusable workflow (`workflow_call`) plus composite actions for setup/test/build so jobs stop duplicating YAML. Add path filters and concurrency groups (cancel superseded PR runs), dependency and container scanning jobs that fail on HIGH/CRITICAL, caching of Docker layers with buildx, and short-lived per-PR preview environments. Inject configuration through GitHub Environments with required reviewers on the protected environment.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable GitHub Actions workflow + composite actions used by CI, buildx layer caching, concurrency groups, scanning jobs gating merges, PR preview environment, and a documented .github/ structure diagram.

tasks.title: Continuous Delivery Pipeline with Smoke Tests and One-Click Rollback
tasks.description: Extend CI into delivery. On merge to main, build and tag the image with the commit SHA, push to a registry (GHCR, later ECR), deploy to a hosted environment, run post-deploy smoke tests against the live URL, and notify on failure.
