Add a prompt-free rollback job that redeploys the previous image tag, and track basic DORA metrics (lead time, deploy frequency, change-failure rate, MTTR). Explicitly connect this to the change-control discipline the candidate already practices through the CAB, but automated and evidence-generating.
tasks.deliverable: Deploy workflow (build -> registry -> deploy -> smoke test -> notify) with a rollback job, a documented release/rollback runbook, and a DORA metrics table from at least three real deploys.

tasks.title: Container Debugging and Runtime Performance Runbook
tasks.description: Learn to operate containers, not just build them. Reproduce five incidents on purpose - crash loop from a bad entrypoint, OOM kill under a memory limit, port conflict, Docker-network DNS failure, and volume permission error from running as non-root - and diagnose each with `docker logs`, `exec`, `stats`, `inspect`, `events` and `docker compose`. Handle SIGTERM for graceful shutdown and record before/after `docker stats` under applied CPU/memory limits. This is the container equivalent of the incident triage and RCA the candidate already runs today.
tasks.deliverable: Container debugging runbook with five reproduced incidents (symptom, diagnosis command, root cause, fix), a SIGTERM graceful-shutdown demo, and a resource-limit before/after stats report.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the Phase 2 containers to managed infrastructure provisioned as code - and deliberately map the candidate's existing Azure fluency (VNet, subnets, UDRs, NSGs, Firewall policies, RBAC) onto AWS VPC, security groups, route tables and IAM. They are not learning networking from zero; they are translating it, which is a genuine interview strength to be able to state explicitly.

tasks.title: AWS Baseline as Code: IAM, Budgets, and Remote State
tasks.description: Set up a clean AWS foundation: a dedicated non-root admin identity with MFA, a least-privilege deployment role/user, AWS CLI v2 profiles, and a budget alarm. Provision everything with Terraform (or AWS CDK) in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking. Write an explicit Azure-to-AWS mapping note (Entra ID/RBAC roles -> IAM policies and roles, Azure Policy -> SCPs, resource groups -> tags and accounts) so the candidate's existing governance experience transfers instead of resetting.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles/policies, budget alarms and an S3+DynamoDB state backend; least-privilege deployment policy documented; Azure-to-AWS concept-mapping sheet; screenshot of the active budget alarm.

tasks.title: Deploy Containers to ECS Fargate behind an ALB in Private Subnets
tasks.description: Push the hardened images to Amazon ECR and run them on ECS Fargate across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks. Place tasks in private subnets with a NAT gateway path, expose only the ALB through a security group, and define the VPC, subnets, route tables and routes in Terraform. This task is where the candidate's UDR/route-table and subnet-design experience becomes directly reusable - document the Azure VNet/UDR to AWS VPC/route-table equivalences as they build it.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned VPC (public/private subnets, route tables, NAT), ECR repo, ECS Fargate service on 2+ AZs, and an ALB with health checks; a reachable public URL plus a deployed-architecture diagram with the Azure-to-AWS equivalence callouts.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Secrets, and ElastiCache Redis on AWS
tasks.description: Move off local containers to managed services. Provision RDS Postgres in private subnets whose security group accepts traffic only from the ECS service, a versioned S3 bucket for uploads with a least-privilege bucket policy, Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store) entries for database credentials injected at task start, and an ElastiCache Redis cluster. Wire the app's Redis client to ElastiCache and prove caching works in the cloud, not just on localhost. Security-group-to-security-group rules are the NSG concept the candidate already knows well - note it explicitly.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Postgres + S3 + Secrets Manager + ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining; a migration run against RDS; proof of an S3 upload; and an app screenshot showing a cache hit served from ElastiCache.

tasks.title: GitHub Actions to AWS with OIDC, Blue/Green Deploy, and Rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery to AWS without storing static keys: configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a scoped trust policy, then extend the Phase 2 pipeline to build, push to ECR, render a new ECS task definition, and perform a rolling (then CodeDeploy blue/green) deployment that waits for service stability. Add a manual approval gate for production and a tested rollback to the previous task revision.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS rolling and blue/green), IAM trust policy, GitHub Environment approval gate, and logs proving both a successful deploy and a successful rollback.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives'. Here the Redis and System Design gaps are closed together: Redis as a cache and rate-limit/queue dependency, and system design as the vocabulary for the caching, consistency, async and scaling tradeoffs the candidate has now actually implemented. Observability reuses the Azure Monitor and Log Analytics fluency as CloudWatch and OpenTelemetry fluency.

tasks.title: Observability: Structured Logs, Metrics, Alarms, and Tracing
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end. Emit structured JSON logs with request IDs, ship them to CloudWatch Logs, and publish custom latency and business metrics via the CloudWatch SDK or embedded metric format. Build a dashboard (request rate, p95 latency, error rate, ECS CPU/memory) with alarms on error-rate and latency thresholds and unhealthy targets. Add OpenTelemetry tracing across ALB -> API -> worker. Frame it as the CloudWatch/OTel translation of the Azure Monitor and Log Analytics KQL work the candidate already does from the alerting side.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, three or more CloudWatch alarms, an OTel trace of one request across services, and a one-page Azure Monitor/Log Analytics to CloudWatch/OTel translation table.

tasks.title: Autoscaling and Load Testing to a Defined SLO
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target, then drive load with k6 (or Locust) against the deployed endpoint. Capture p95 latency, throughput and error rate before and after scale-out, and tune target values, cooldowns and min/max task counts to hit a stated SLO. Document the observed bottleneck (in most cases the database connection pool) and the fix.
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies for CPU and request count with tuned min/max, a k6/Locust load-test script and report (throughput, p95, error rate) showing scale-out, plus a bottleneck analysis note.

tasks.title: Redis Caching, Rate Limiting, and Async Queue Processing
tasks.description: Close the Redis gap with three production uses, not one tutorial. First, a cache-aside pattern for a hot read endpoint with explicit TTLs, cache-key versioning and stampede protection, benchmarked against ElastiCache. Second, a Redis token-bucket rate limiter on the public API - the same enforcement concept as an Azure Firewall rate rule, now implemented in application code. Third, move slow work (email, image processing, report generation) to a background worker consuming an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue and idempotent handlers, with Redis used for job status. Containerize the worker with its own image and run it as a separate ECS service.
tasks.deliverable: Cache-aside layer with measured hit-rate and latency improvement, Redis token-bucket rate limiter with a test proving 429 behavior, and an SQS-backed worker as a separate ECS service with DLQ, idempotency keys and a before/after latency benchmark.

tasks.title: System Design Fluency: Caching, Queues, Consistency, and Failure Modes
tasks.description: Turn implementation into design language. Write three design documents - a multi-tenant SaaS API, an image-upload and processing pipeline, and a payment/event flow with exactly-once processing concerns - each covering API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy and invalidation, queueing and backpressure, idempotency, consistency tradeoffs, hosting topology on AWS, scaling limits and failure modes. Back every choice with something built in Phases 2-4 (e.g. 'Redis cache-aside with TTL plus versioned keys because we measured X'). Include a tradeoff table comparing SQL vs Redis vs queue for each read/write path.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design docs with architecture diagrams, tradeoff tables, capacity/SLO estimates, a failure-mode table (retry, timeout, circuit breaker), and a self-critique list of where an interviewer would push back.

tasks.title: Multi-Environment Terraform, Cost Control, and Disaster Recovery
tasks.description: Make the infrastructure repeatable and affordable. Parameterize Terraform into dev/staging/prod workspaces or var-files with environment-specific sizing, stand up a second environment end to end, and confirm the same pipeline promotes between them. Produce a Cost Explorer analysis with three applied optimizations (rightsizing Fargate, RDS instance class, savings from the Redis cache) and document an RTO/RPO backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-environment Terraform (dev/staging/prod) with a deployed staging stack, a cost analysis with three applied optimizations and actual dollar deltas, and a tested backup/restore DR runbook with measured recovery time.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert Phase 1-4 artifacts into interview performance for the Full Stack Engineer loop at Stripe. Every deliverable becomes a story, a diagram and a defensible decision. The candidate also rehearses the one thing that makes their profile distinctive: a cloud security and networking background now backed by hands-on shipping - which is an advantage in reliability, compliance and review culture, not a gap to hide.

tasks.title: Timed System Design Drills with Whiteboard Diagrams
tasks.description: Convert the Phase 4 design docs into verbal fluency. Run at least six timed 35-40 minute mock prompts alone and two with a peer or recorded video: a URL shortener, a feed/notification system, a payment-idempotency service, a rate-limited public API, an analytics ingestion pipeline, and a multi-tenant SaaS. For each: clarify requirements, estimate scale, sketch boxes and arrows, choose a data model, place caching and queues, name the bottleneck and the failure mode, then write the answers you would give to the three hardest follow-ups.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design drill packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, tradeoff decisions, follow-up answers) plus two recorded mock design sessions with a reviewed list of recurring weak points.

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Architecture Writeup, and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate the code, Terraform, compose files, CI/CD workflows, tests, SBOM/scan reports and runbooks into one clean public repository with a README that reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment guide, observability screenshots, load-test numbers, cost notes and the rollback runbook. Then write RESUME.md mapping each project feature to a resume bullet, and rewrite the Accenture experience to show the transferable core (incident RCA, change control, least privilege, policy enforcement) alongside the new shipping skills.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, container quickstart, AWS deployment + rollback guides, dashboards and screenshots, a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping, and a rewritten resume section reviewed for the Full Stack Engineer target.

tasks.title: AWS Knowledge Consolidation and Practice Exams
tasks.description: Convert practical AWS experience into exam-grade, interview-ready fluency. Work the core SAA-C03 domains - IAM, VPC/networking, ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SQS, CloudWatch, cost models - condensing each service into a one-page cheat sheet that pairs the service with the thing you actually built with it. Sit at least three timed practice exams and review every wrong answer to a service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: Cheat sheets for 10+ AWS services each linked to a project artifact, three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log, targeting a consistent 80%+ before scheduling the real exam.

tasks.title: Mock Interviews and a Metrics-Backed STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop: a live coding round (add a tested endpoint to a running containerized app), a Docker/AWS/Redis deep dive, a system design round, and behavioral questions. Build a STAR bank of 8+ stories from real Phase 1-4 work with numbers - 'cut image size from 1.2GB to 220MB', 'diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop', 'raised cache hit rate to 85% and cut p95 by 60%', 'automated a CAB-style approval into an OIDC-gated pipeline' - and one story that frames the security background as a shipping advantage (threat-aware design reviews, least-privilege infrastructure, incident RCA habits). Log every question asked and tighten the answer.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (one coding, one system design), a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist covering Docker, CI/CD, AWS, Redis and system design.

careerPlans.summary: A 10-week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a Cloud & Network Security Engineer targeting Full Stack Engineer at Stripe, with five priority gaps to close: Docker, CI/CD, System Design, AWS and Redis. It is sequenced so each phase feeds the next. Phase 1 builds a reproducible containerized dev/test loop and the first GitHub Actions pipeline; Phase 2 hardens images, orchestrates six services locally with Compose, and turns CI into a reusable delivery system with scanning, environment gates, smoke tests and rollback; Phase 3 translates the candidate's real Azure networking and policy depth (VNet, subnets, UDRs, NSGs, Firewall) into AWS as code - Terraform, VPC, ECS Fargate, ALB, RDS, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis - with OIDC-based blue/green delivery; Phase 4 adds production depth (CloudWatch/OTel observability, autoscaling under k6 load, Redis cache-aside plus rate limiting plus SQS async workers, system design docs, multi-environment cost and DR discipline); Phase 5 converts every artifact into timed system design drills, a documented portfolio repository, AWS exam fluency and metric-backed STAR stories. No task is generic: each one names the specific gap it closes, reuses a concrete piece of the candidate's existing experience, and produces an inspectable deliverable.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: The candidate already ships microservices in JavaScript/TypeScript on Node.js/Express with PostgreSQL, Redis and Docker, and claims high test coverage. Phase 1 therefore raises the floor of that existing loop instead of re-teaching it: strict typing end to end across the React client and the Express API, one enforced quality gate, a reproducibly containerised dev environment, the first owned CI pipeline (CI/CD is only partially evidenced today), and the first Python muscle, since Python is a hard gap at Stripe for tooling, data and services.

tasks.title: Strict TypeScript Contract Across Client and Server
tasks.description: Turn the existing React + Express codebase into one strictly typed workspace: enable strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes, ban any via @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any, and extract every request/response DTO, error envelope and pagination shape into a shared @contracts package built from Zod schemas with types inferred from them. Type the Express middleware chain (Request/Response/NextFunction generics), the Redis client wrapper and the Postgres query layer, so a contract change cannot reach the frontend without tsc failing on both sides.
tasks.deliverable: Monorepo with a shared @contracts package (Zod schemas + inferred DTO types), strict tsconfig for client and server, zero tsc --noEmit errors, and a README example proving the same contract type is consumed by a React hook and an Express route.

tasks.title: One Enforced Quality Gate: Lint, Format, Typecheck, Pre-commit
tasks.description: Standardise code quality so later phases can reuse it verbatim. Configure ESLint flat config with the React hooks and Node plugins, Prettier, Husky + lint-staged running lint/format/typecheck only on staged files, a commitlint conventional-commit rule, and --max-warnings=0 so warnings cannot silently accumulate. Expose identical lint, typecheck, format and test scripts that run unchanged on the host, inside the container and in CI, making one command surface the single source of truth.
tasks.deliverable: Committed ESLint/Prettier/commitlint configs, a working Husky + lint-staged pre-commit hook, a package.json script surface (lint/typecheck/format/test) shared by local, container and CI runs, and a screenshot of the hook rejecting a non-conventional or lint-failing commit.

tasks.title: Turn High Unit Coverage into Real Integration and Contract Tests
tasks.description: The candidate reports high test coverage, but coverage that only exercises mocks does not prove the system works. Add Testcontainers-backed integration tests that boot real PostgreSQL and Redis per suite with no pre-started database, contract/schema snapshot tests asserting every public endpoint against the shared DTOs, an enforced coverage gate of 85% lines and branches on the API layer with per-file thresholds for critical services, and Stryker mutation testing on the two highest-risk services so the suite is measured on breakage detection, not line execution.
tasks.deliverable: Testcontainers integration suite (self-provisioning Postgres + Redis), contract tests covering every public endpoint, coverage gate enforced at 85% with per-file thresholds, and a Stryker mutation score report for the payments/orders service with a note on the mutants that survived.

tasks.title: Container-First Reference Environment with One-Command Boot
tasks.description: Rebuild the local loop around containers rather than a hand-configured machine. Write multi-stage Dockerfiles (deps -> build -> runtime) for the React/Vite frontend served by Nginx and for the Node/Express service, run both as non-root users with pinned base-image digests and a proper .dockerignore, and wire API, web, PostgreSQL and Redis into one docker-compose.yml with an isolated network, named volumes, healthchecks and depends_on: condition: service_healthy. Add bind mounts for hot reload and prove a clean clone boots with a single command.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile per service plus a docker-compose.yml with healthchecks, volumes and an isolated network that boots the whole stack via `docker compose up` from a clean clone; documented cold-start time and a container topology diagram.

tasks.title: Python Foundations for a Polyglot Full-Stack Engineer
tasks.description: Close the Python gap by mapping it onto the candidate's existing JS/TS model: modern Python 3.12 typing (Protocol, generics, TypedDict), packaging and environments with uv, pytest with fixtures and parametrisation, ruff plus mypy --strict, async I/O with asyncio/httpx, and FastAPI + Pydantic v2 mirroring the Express service's routing and validation. Re-implement one narrow endpoint (a health route plus a Redis-backed rate-limit check) in FastAPI and hold it to the same contract tests written in Phase 1.
tasks.deliverable: A FastAPI service that is mypy --strict clean and ruff clean, re-implementing one Express endpoint with Pydantic v2 models, a pytest suite of 12+ tests including parametrised edge cases, and a JS/TS-versus-Python idiom cheat sheet for the concepts the candidate already knows.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Kubernetes is the first hard gap and Docker is the natural bridge into it. This phase hardens the images the candidate already builds, then moves the working stack onto a real cluster and finally into a production-grade Helm release, while Python grows from 'I can write a script' to 'I can operate a service' with async I/O, migrations and queue consumption. Every task produces manifests, a chart or a runbook the candidate can defend under questioning.

tasks.title: Production Image Hardening and Supply-Chain Attestation
tasks.description: Rebuild the images for production: distroless or slim bases on pinned digests, non-root UID, read-only root filesystem where feasible, only compiled output copied into the runtime stage, multi-arch builds with buildx, and secrets kept out of layers entirely. Generate an SBOM with Syft, scan with Trivy failing the build on HIGH/CRITICAL, sign images with cosign and verify signatures before deploy, and measure image size and layer count against the Phase 1 dev images.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened runtime images under 200MB running as non-root on pinned digests, .dockerignore, a Syft SBOM, a Trivy scan report wired as a CI gate, cosign signatures plus a verification step, and a dev-versus-prod image size comparison.

tasks.title: Local Kubernetes Cluster: Translating Compose into Manifests
tasks.description: Create a kind (or minikube) cluster and port the whole stack: Deployments for web and API, ClusterIP Services plus an ingress-nginx Ingress, ConfigMaps and Secrets, liveness/readiness/startup probes, resource requests and limits, a rolling update strategy with tuned maxSurge/maxUnavailable, namespace isolation, and kustomize base plus dev/staging overlays. Write the mapping table as the work happens so every Docker concept the candidate knows (networks, healthchecks, volumes, compose overrides) has a named Kubernetes equivalent.
tasks.deliverable: kind cluster config plus kustomize base/overlay manifests deploying web, API, PostgreSQL and Redis, an Ingress serving the app on localhost, and a Compose-to-Kubernetes concept mapping table (networks->Services, healthchecks->probes, volumes->PVCs, overrides->kustomize).

tasks.title: Stateful Workloads, Jobs and Helm Packaging
tasks.description: Run state correctly: PostgreSQL as a StatefulSet with a PersistentVolumeClaim and headless Service (with a written note on when a managed database replaces it), Redis with persistence and a password Secret, schema migrations as a Helm hook Job rather than a startup side-effect, CronJobs for cache warm-up and report generation, a HorizontalPodAutoscaler on CPU plus a custom queue-length metric, and a PodDisruptionBudget. Package the whole thing as a Helm chart with values-dev.yaml and values-prod.yaml and rehearse helm rollback.
tasks.deliverable: A Helm chart deploying the full stack (Postgres StatefulSet + PVC, Redis, migration hook Job, CronJobs, HPA, PDB) installable with one `helm upgrade --install`, values files per environment, and a documented, tested `helm rollback`.

tasks.title: Python Service in Production: Async, Migrations and Queue Consumption
tasks.description: Promote the Phase 1 FastAPI service into a real second service. Add async SQLAlchemy 2.0 with Alembic migrations against PostgreSQL, Redis-backed idempotent job consumption from a queue, Pydantic settings for twelve-factor configuration, structlog JSON logging with request and correlation IDs, graceful shutdown on SIGTERM, and pytest + Testcontainers integration tests. Ship it with its own Dockerfile and Helm chart and run it beside the Node API in the same cluster, then benchmark both services on the same endpoint.
tasks.deliverable: A deployed FastAPI worker consuming jobs with idempotency keys, Alembic migration history, structured JSON logs, a SIGTERM graceful-shutdown demo, and a Python-versus-Node throughput and p95 comparison on an identical endpoint.

tasks.title: Kubernetes Failure Drills and Operations Runbook
tasks.description: Operate the cluster by breaking it deliberately: reproduce a CrashLoopBackOff from a misconfigured probe, an ImagePullBackOff from a bad digest, an OOMKilled pod from an under-set memory limit, a Service whose selector matches no pods, an Ingress returning 503, a PVC stuck Pending, and a node cordon-and-drain during a rolling node upgrade. Diagnose each with kubectl describe, logs --previous, get events, top and exec, record symptom, command, root cause and fix, and practise rollout undo and resource-quota exhaustion.
tasks.deliverable: A troubleshooting runbook with 7 reproduced failures (symptom, diagnostic commands, root cause, fix), a recorded kubectl rollout-undo demo, and a one-page kubectl command cheat sheet for live interviews.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: AWS is the second hard gap. Here the Kubernetes stack the candidate just built is deployed onto managed AWS infrastructure provisioned entirely as code, with no long-lived credentials anywhere. The Security Compliance gap starts being closed at the platform layer: encryption, logging, guardrails and least privilege are implemented as Terraform modules and evidence is mapped to SOC 2 and PCI DSS, so compliance reads as an engineering control rather than a policy document.

tasks.title: AWS Foundation as Code: IAM, GitHub OIDC and Guardrails
tasks.description: Stand up a clean AWS account: MFA-protected root, a dedicated administrative identity, AWS CLI v2 profiles, and a Terraform (or CDK) repository using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking. Add budget and billing alarms, a tag standard, and a GitHub OIDC identity provider with a scoped deploy role so no static AWS keys exist in the project. Run terraform plan on every pull request and apply only from the protected main branch.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles and policies, the GitHub OIDC provider, an S3+DynamoDB state backend and budget alarms; a permission table documenting the least-privilege deploy policy; a screenshot of the live budget alarm; and a scan showing zero long-lived AWS access keys committed or configured.

tasks.title: EKS Cluster as Code with IRSA, ALB Ingress and Cluster Autoscaling
tasks.description: Terraform an EKS cluster across two or more Availability Zones with a managed node group plus a spot capacity group. Attach per-service IAM roles through IRSA so pods never inherit node-wide credentials, install the AWS Load Balancer Controller so Ingress provisions an ALB, add the EBS CSI driver for PVCs, cluster-autoscaler for node elasticity, external-secrets-operator to project Secrets Manager values, and default-deny NetworkPolicies between namespaces. Deploy the Phase 2 Helm chart unchanged to prove portability.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned EKS cluster (2+ AZs, managed and spot node groups) with an IRSA role per service, an ALB-backed Ingress serving the app on a public hostname, external-secrets wired to Secrets Manager, default-deny NetworkPolicies, and a deployed architecture diagram.

tasks.title: Managed Data Tier: RDS, ElastiCache, S3 and SQS
tasks.description: Move state out of the cluster onto managed services. Provision RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ in private subnets whose security group accepts traffic only from the application security group, with parameter-group tuning, automated backups and a real point-in-time restore rehearsal; ElastiCache Redis with encryption in transit and an auth token; a versioned S3 bucket with SSE-KMS and lifecycle rules for uploads; and an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue for the Python worker. Scope every IAM policy to a single resource ARN, then run the Alembic and migration suites against RDS and repoint the applications with no code change.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Multi-AZ, ElastiCache, S3 (SSE-KMS, versioning, lifecycle) and SQS with DLQ using security-group chaining; a completed point-in-time restore test with measured duration; and application evidence of a Redis cache hit and an S3-backed upload.

tasks.title: CI/CD to EKS with Progressive Delivery and Rollback
tasks.description: Extend the Phase 1 pipeline into real delivery. Build and push images to ECR with buildx layer caching and an SBOM attestation, render Helm values per environment, and deploy with Argo Rollouts canary (or a rolling update) whose analysis watches error rate and latency before promotion. Authenticate with GitHub OIDC rather than stored keys, require a reviewer on the production GitHub Environment, run post-deploy smoke tests against the live URL, and configure automatic rollback when the analysis fails. Capture lead time, deploy frequency, change-failure rate and MTTR across at least five deploys.
tasks.deliverable: A GitHub Actions deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> Helm -> canary) using OIDC, a production approval gate, a demonstrated automatic rollback on a deliberately failing release, and a DORA metrics table from five real deploys.

tasks.title: Security and Compliance Controls as Code
tasks.description: Implement the controls a Stripe-grade environment assumes, as Terraform rather than as prose: KMS customer-managed keys for RDS, S3, EBS and Secrets Manager; TLS on every hop with ACM plus cert-manager and no plaintext internal traffic; VPC flow logs and CloudTrail with log-file validation; AWS Config rules (encrypted-volumes, s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, iam-policy-no-statements-with-admin-access); GuardDuty; SCP-style guardrails against region and service drift; scheduled secret rotation; and an IAM review with Access Analyzer. Map every control to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and PCI DSS v4 requirements with its automated check and evidence link.
tasks.deliverable: A control matrix mapping each implemented control to a SOC 2 TSC and PCI DSS v4 requirement (owner, evidence link, automated check), Terraform for Config rules, GuardDuty, CloudTrail and KMS keys, secret rotation configured, and an IAM Access Analyzer report with zero unresolved findings.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: This phase turns a stack that deploys into a system whose behaviour is measured. The System Design partial is levelled up through design documents that are backed by real numbers, the Security Compliance gap is closed where it matters most for Stripe - payment flows, PCI scope reduction, privacy rights and audit evidence - and the candidate's existing PostgreSQL, Redis and Node depth is pushed to its production limits under load, failure and cost pressure.

tasks.title: Observability: Metrics, Traces, Logs and SLOs
tasks.description: Instrument both services end to end with OpenTelemetry, exporting traces across the ALB -> Node API -> Python worker path with correlation IDs. Stand up kube-prometheus-stack plus Grafana (or CloudWatch and X-Ray) with RED and USE dashboards, ship structured JSON logs, add five alert rules (p95 latency, error rate, saturation, queue depth, unhealthy targets) routed to a real contact point, and define three SLOs with error budgets. Every alert links to its runbook entry so alerts are actionable rather than noisy.
tasks.deliverable: OTel tracing across three services, dashboards for request rate, error rate, p95 and saturation, five alert rules wired to notifications, three documented SLOs with error budgets, and runbook links attached to every alert.

tasks.title: Load Testing, Bottleneck Elimination and Autoscaling
tasks.description: Set a concrete SLO (for example p95 under 200ms at 500 requests per second), then write k6 scenarios for steady state, spike, a 30-minute soak and a cache-miss hot-key case. Measure the real bottleneck - expect PostgreSQL connection-pool exhaustion and N+1 queries - and fix it: pgbouncer or pool tuning, indexes verified with EXPLAIN ANALYZE against 1M+ seeded rows, a read replica for reporting, and a Redis cache-aside layer with TTL and stampede protection. Then configure HPA on CPU plus queue depth via KEDA and cluster-autoscaler for nodes, and re-measure.
tasks.deliverable: A k6 scenario suite and before/after reports (throughput, p95/p99, error rate), an EXPLAIN ANALYZE index-tuning writeup on 1M+ rows, HPA/KEDA and cluster-autoscaler policies, and a bottleneck-to-fix table with measured deltas.

tasks.title: PCI Scope Reduction and Payment-Flow Correctness
tasks.description: Build the payment capability the way Stripe expects its own engineers to build it: integrate Stripe Elements or Checkout with tokenisation so raw card data never touches the application, logs or database (keeping the workload in SAQ-A scope), enforce idempotency keys on every mutating payment endpoint, verify webhook signatures with replay protection, and model money as a double-entry ledger in PostgreSQL (transactions, entries, balance invariants, check constraints) that stays consistent under concurrent writes via serializable isolation or advisory locks. Add an append-only audit log of every state change and a STRIDE threat model, then walk the OWASP ASVS L2 checklist and remediate.
tasks.deliverable: A Stripe-integrated payment flow with idempotency keys, verified webhooks and a log grep proving no PAN or CVV is ever written; a double-entry ledger schema with a concurrency test proving balances stay consistent; a STRIDE threat model with mitigations; and a completed OWASP ASVS L2 checklist with remediation notes.

tasks.title: Data Protection, Application Access Control and Audit Readiness
tasks.description: Treat privacy and access as features: define a data classification and retention policy, then implement right-to-erasure and data-export endpoints backed by a job that scrubs PII across PostgreSQL, Redis, S3 objects and backups (proven end to end), add field-level encryption or tokenisation for PII columns, and build RBAC with least-privilege authorization middleware covered by a permission test matrix. Harden sessions with short-lived access tokens, rotating refresh tokens and revocation; add rate limiting and abuse protection; run dependency and IaC scanning in CI; and produce a quarterly access-review pack that doubles as audit evidence.
tasks.deliverable: A data classification and retention policy, working erasure and export endpoints with an end-to-end test proving PII removal from database, cache, object storage and backups, an RBAC permission test matrix, token rotation and revocation implemented, and an access-review plus audit-evidence pack.

tasks.title: Design Documents, Chaos and DR Testing, and Cost Discipline
tasks.description: Write three design documents grounded in what was actually measured this phase - a high-throughput payments API, a multi-tenant SaaS backend, and an event-driven ledger/notification pipeline - each covering API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy, queueing and backpressure, idempotency, consistency tradeoffs, hosting topology, capacity math, scaling limits and failure modes, with a tradeoff table for every read and write path. Then test the claims: kill pods, fail the Redis primary, drain a node and simulate an Availability Zone loss, recording blast radius and the fixes applied, plus a documented RTO/RPO restore drill and a Cost Explorer review with three applied optimizations.
tasks.deliverable: Three design docs with diagrams, capacity estimates and tradeoff tables; a chaos and DR report covering four experiments with observed blast radius and fixes; a tested backup/restore runbook with measured recovery time against a stated RTO/RPO; and a cost analysis with three applied optimizations and dollar deltas.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert four phases of artifacts into interview performance for the Stripe Full Stack Engineer loop: coding rounds in both TypeScript and Python, Kubernetes/AWS/compliance deep dives, a system design round, and behavioural questions. Every answer is anchored to something the candidate actually built and measured, and the portfolio repository makes the whole journey inspectable to a hiring panel.

tasks.title: Timed System Design Drills with Whiteboard Diagrams
tasks.description: Convert the Phase 4 design docs into spoken fluency with six timed 35-40 minute prompts: a rate-limited public API, a payment idempotency service, a notification/feed fan-out, a URL shortener, an analytics ingestion pipeline and a multi-tenant SaaS backend. Hold a fixed structure every time - clarify requirements, estimate scale, define the API contract, choose a data model, place caching and queues, name the bottleneck and the failure modes - and pre-write answers to the three hardest follow-ups per prompt, citing the numbers measured in Phases 3 and 4.
tasks.deliverable: Six design drill packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, tradeoff decisions, follow-up answers) plus two recorded mock design sessions with a reviewed list of recurring weak points.

tasks.title: Dual-Language Coding Drill Set: TypeScript and Python
tasks.description: Pair the candidate's TypeScript strength with the Python gap so neither language is a liability in a live round. Implement six interview-class problems twice, once in strict TypeScript and once in typed Python: an LRU cache, an idempotency key store with TTL and eviction, a sliding-window and token-bucket rate limiter, event deduplication, a paginated API over a stream, and a concurrent-safe balance transfer. Write the tests first in vitest and pytest, note complexity and edge cases, and run two recorded 45-minute mock coding sessions with a log of every hint taken and the improved solution afterwards.
tasks.deliverable: Twelve reference implementations (6 problems x TypeScript and Python), each with tests and complexity notes, two recorded mock coding interviews with feedback, and a hint log pairing every struggle with its corrected solution.

tasks.title: Kubernetes, AWS and Compliance Deep-Dive Preparation
tasks.description: Turn hands-on work into crisp verbal answers. Build one-page cheat sheets for each service used (EKS, IRSA, ALB Controller, cluster-autoscaler, RDS, ElastiCache, SQS, KMS, Config, GuardDuty, CloudTrail), each linked to the exact artifact the candidate built with it. Assemble a 60+ question deep-dive bank covering probes versus readiness, HPA versus cluster-autoscaler, StatefulSet versus Deployment, IRSA versus node instance roles, PCI DSS scope reduction, SOC 2 evidence, secret rotation and incident triage. Sit three timed practice exams (AWS SAA and/or CKA) and review every wrong answer to a service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: Ten or more service cheat sheets linked to project artifacts, a 60-question deep-dive bank with written answers, and three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log targeting a consistent 80%+.

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Architecture Case Study and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate code, Terraform, Helm charts, CI/CD workflows, tests, SBOMs, scan reports, dashboards, load-test results and runbooks into one public repository whose README reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, one-command quickstart, AWS/EKS deployment guide, observability screenshots, measured numbers, cost notes and the rollback runbook. Then write RESUME.md mapping each artifact to a resume bullet and rewrite the Technology Firm experience to surface microservice ownership, the testing and code-quality outcomes and the measured production impact, with keywords aligned to the Stripe Full Stack Engineer posting.
tasks.deliverable: A public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, container quickstart, EKS deploy and rollback guides, dashboards and load-test screenshots, a feature-to-bullet RESUME.md, and a rewritten resume section reviewed against the target job description.

tasks.title: Mock Interviews, STAR Story Bank and Final Readiness Review
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop end to end: live coding in TypeScript and Python, a Kubernetes and AWS deep dive, a system design round, a security and compliance discussion, and behavioural questions. Build a STAR bank of eight or more stories carrying real numbers from Phases 1-4 - image size reduction, p95 before and after under k6 load, cache hit rate, mutation score, deploy frequency and change-failure rate, an Availability Zone failure recovery - plus one story that frames the compliance work as an engineering advantage. Log every question asked and tighten the weakest answers, then close with an honest readiness review against each gap.
tasks.deliverable: A STAR story bank of 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (one coding, one system design), a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist covering TypeScript/Node, Python, Docker/Kubernetes, AWS, CI/CD, security compliance and system design.

careerPlans.summary: An approximately 11-week roadmap built for a Full Stack Developer with real, current depth in JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Node.js/Express, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Redis and Docker, who is targeting Full Stack Engineer at Stripe and carries four hard gaps - Kubernetes, AWS, Security Compliance and Python - plus two partials to level up, CI/CD and System Design. It never re-teaches what the candidate already has: Phase 1 instead raises that existing loop to a strict, tested, container-first standard and adds the first Python foundations; Phase 2 takes Docker to hardened production images and goes deep on Kubernetes with a real cluster, StatefulSets, Helm and failure drills while Python becomes an operated service; Phase 3 provisions the whole stack on AWS as code - IAM and GitHub OIDC, EKS with IRSA and ALB Ingress, RDS, ElastiCache, S3 and SQS - with progressive delivery and the first security and compliance controls mapped to SOC 2 and PCI DSS; Phase 4 makes it survive with OpenTelemetry observability and SLOs, k6 load testing that eliminates a named bottleneck, PCI scope reduction and payment correctness, data protection and audit readiness, plus three measured system design documents backed by chaos and DR testing; Phase 5 converts every artifact into timed system design drills, dual-language coding practice, deep-dive question banks, a case-study portfolio repository and metric-backed STAR stories. Each task names the specific gap it closes, reuses a concrete piece of the candidate's existing full-stack experience, and ends in an inspectable deliverable such as a Helm chart, a Terraform module, a control matrix or a load-test report.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Reinforce the JavaScript/TypeScript and Node.js foundation you already have while closing the Python gap and raising overall code quality. The goal is a single, well-tested, strictly-typed service that all later phases build on, so gaps in typing, testing, and Python tooling never resurface during interviews.

tasks.title: Harden a TypeScript/Node.js service with strict compiler and lint gates
tasks.description: Take an existing Express microservice and enable strict TypeScript (strict, noImplicitAny, noUncheckedIndexedAccess), fix every resulting error, and centralize runtime validation with Zod. Add ESLint + Prettier with a shared config and zero-warning policy.
tasks.deliverable: Strict-mode TypeScript Express service with tsconfig, Zod request/response schemas, and a committed ESLint + Prettier config passing with zero warnings

tasks.title: Python fundamentals bridge for a backend engineer
tasks.description: Translate your existing Node/Express knowledge into Python: type hints, virtualenv/uv, pytest, pydantic, and a FastAPI service exposing the same REST contract as your TypeScript service. Focus on idiomatic Python (comprehensions, context managers, async/await) rather than literal line-by-line ports.
tasks.deliverable: FastAPI service mirroring your Express API, with typed pydantic models, uv-locked dependencies, and pytest coverage on every endpoint

tasks.title: Build a shared test strategy with real coverage thresholds
tasks.description: Add unit, integration, and contract tests for both services. Use Vitest/Jest for Node and pytest for Python, wire coverage reporting, and enforce minimum coverage (80%+) so the metric is a gate rather than a report.
tasks.deliverable: Test suites for both services with coverage config enforced at 80%, plus a TESTING.md documenting the test pyramid

tasks.title: Establish local reproducibility with Docker Compose
tasks.description: Containerize both services with multi-stage builds (builder + slim runtime, non-root user, pinned base images) and orchestrate app, PostgreSQL, and Redis via docker-compose with healthchecks and a hot-reload dev profile.
tasks.deliverable: Optimized multi-stage Dockerfiles for Node and Python plus a docker-compose.yml with Postgres, Redis, healthchecks, and a dev override

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Directly attack the two highest-impact gaps for a Stripe-style role: Python as a production language and Security Compliance. Security is treated as an engineering discipline — auth, payments-grade data handling, secrets, and dependency hygiene — not a checklist.

tasks.title: Ship a production-grade Python service with async I/O
tasks.description: Extend your FastAPI service into a real workload: async Postgres access via SQLAlchemy 2.0, Redis caching, background jobs, structured logging, and dependency injection. Add Alembic migrations and graceful shutdown handling.
tasks.deliverable: Async FastAPI service with SQLAlchemy 2.0, Alembic migrations, Redis caching layer, and structured JSON logging

tasks.title: Implement OWASP-aligned auth and authorization
tasks.description: Build JWT-based auth with refresh-token rotation, bcrypt/argon2 password hashing, role-based access control, rate limiting, and strict input validation. Explicitly cover the OWASP API Top 10 — broken object-level authorization, injection, and mass assignment — with tests proving each is blocked.
tasks.deliverable: Authentication/authorization module with refresh-token rotation, RBAC middleware, rate limiting, and tests covering OWASP API Top 10 controls

tasks.title: PCI-aware data handling and secrets management
tasks.description: Design how sensitive payment-adjacent data is handled: field-level encryption at rest, tokenization, never logging PII/PCI data, GDPR-style data deletion, and audit logging. Move all secrets out of code into a manager (AWS Secrets Manager or Vault) with rotation.
tasks.deliverable: Data-handling design doc plus working implementation of field-level encryption, tokenization, audit logging, and secrets-manager integration with rotation

tasks.title: Automated security scanning in the dependency pipeline
tasks.description: Add SAST and dependency vulnerability scanning to the build: Semgrep/Bandit for code, npm audit and pip-audit for dependencies, Trivy for container images, and a dependency-update bot. Fail the build on high-severity findings.
tasks.deliverable: Security scanning job config with Semgrep, pip-audit/npm audit, and Trivy, plus a remediation runbook for triaging findings

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Move from local Docker to real cloud infrastructure. Cover AWS core services, Kubernetes as the deployment target, and the CI/CD pipelines that connect them — the two 'partial' skills (CI/CD, container orchestration) become production habits here.

tasks.title: Provision AWS infrastructure as code
tasks.description: Learn core AWS by building it: VPC with public/private subnets, IAM roles with least privilege, S3, RDS Postgres, ElastiCache Redis, and Secrets Manager — all defined in Terraform. Deploy your app to ECS Fargate behind an ALB with autoscaling.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform stack provisioning VPC, IAM, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, Secrets Manager, and an ECS Fargate service behind an ALB with autoscaling

tasks.title: Deploy and operate a Kubernetes cluster
tasks.description: Stand up a managed cluster (EKS), then deploy your services with Deployments, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps, Secrets, resource requests/limits, liveness and readiness probes, HPA, and RBAC. Add Helm charts so environments are parameterized rather than copy-pasted.
tasks.deliverable: EKS deployment with Helm charts, Ingress, HPA, probes, resource limits, and RBAC manifests for both services

tasks.title: End-to-end CI/CD pipeline with progressive delivery
tasks.description: Build a full pipeline: lint and test matrix on pull requests, container build and push to ECR, IaC plan/apply, and environment-staged deploy (dev to staging to prod) with manual approval on prod. Add blue/green or canary rollout via Argo Rollouts.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with lint/test matrix, image build and ECR push, Terraform apply, staged deploys, and canary rollout config

tasks.title: Infrastructure observability for deployed workloads
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack: Prometheus/Grafana or CloudWatch dashboards, distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, centralized logs, and alerting on latency, error rate, and saturation. Define SLOs and add alerts that page on burn rate.
tasks.deliverable: Monitoring stack with dashboards, OpenTelemetry tracing, log aggregation, SLO definitions, and alert rules wired to a notification channel

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Turn a running system into a designed system. Close the System Design gap with concrete architecture exercises, then prove scalability and resilience with data-layer scaling, caching strategy, load testing, and failure-mode analysis.

tasks.title: Write and defend a system design document for a payments-scale checkout
tasks.description: Design a checkout/payment flow at scale: API gateway, service boundaries, idempotency keys, exactly-once payment semantics, saga/outbox pattern for consistency, queues for downstream processing, and an SLO-driven capacity estimate. Include trade-off analysis and rejected alternatives.
tasks.deliverable: System design doc with architecture diagrams, idempotency and saga design, capacity math, and a written trade-off analysis

tasks.title: Scale the PostgreSQL and Redis data layer
tasks.description: Move beyond single-node data: index analysis with EXPLAIN, connection pooling via PgBouncer, read replicas, partitioning, and a migration path toward sharding. For Redis, implement cache-aside and write-through patterns, eviction policies, rate-limit counters, and stampede protection.
tasks.deliverable: Scaling implementation with PgBouncer, read-replica routing, indexed query plans, and documented Redis caching/eviction strategy with benchmarks

tasks.title: Load test and capacity-plan the system
tasks.description: Run k6 or Locust load tests against the deployed stack, identify the bottleneck (DB, cache, connection pool, or CPU), fix it, and re-test. Produce a capacity model that states the throughput ceiling and what breaks first.
tasks.deliverable: k6 load-test scripts, before/after performance report with bottleneck analysis, and a capacity model with documented limits

tasks.title: Resilience and failure-mode hardening
tasks.description: Introduce circuit breakers, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, timeouts, bulkheads, and graceful degradation. Run chaos experiments (kill a pod, drop the DB, throttle the network) and confirm the system degrades predictably instead of failing outright.
tasks.deliverable: Resilience patterns implemented plus a chaos-test report showing recovery behavior for at least three injected failure scenarios

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert engineering work into interview performance. Build a portfolio narrative around the system you built, drill coding and design interviews under realistic constraints, and rehearse Stripe-specific signals: rigor, security mindedness, and clear technical communication.

tasks.title: Codify the final system as a portfolio case study
tasks.description: Produce a public repo and write-up for the full system: architecture diagram, AWS/Kubernetes topology, security decisions, CI/CD pipeline, scaling results, and trade-offs. Make the README tell the story of decisions, not just list technologies.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repo with architecture diagrams and a case-study README covering design decisions, security model, and scaling evidence

tasks.title: Algorithm and coding interview drills
tasks.description: Work through 40-50 problems across arrays, hashing, graphs, dynamic programming, and concurrency, timed to 35 minutes each, implemented in both TypeScript and Python. Track weak patterns and re-solve misses after a week.
tasks.deliverable: Annotated solutions repo covering 40+ problems in TypeScript and Python with a pattern/weakness tracker

tasks.title: Mock system-design and behavioral interviews
tasks.description: Run at least four mock interviews: two system design (payments/ledger and rate-limited public API) and two behavioral focused on ownership, incident handling, and cross-team collaboration. Record them, review for structure and signal, and iterate on feedback.
tasks.deliverable: Four recorded mock interviews with written self-critiques and revised answer frameworks for design and behavioral questions

tasks.title: Stripe-targeted review of gaps and talking points
tasks.description: Review the original gap list (Kubernetes, AWS, Security Compliance, Python, CI/CD, System Design) and confirm each is now backed by a deliverable and a crisp 60-second story. Prepare answers on idempotency, PCI scope, reliability, and API design, plus questions that show genuine interest in Stripe's engineering.
tasks.deliverable: Gap-closure checklist mapping each missing/partial skill to a concrete artifact and a rehearsed interview story, plus a prepared question list

careerPlans.summary: This plan converts your strong JavaScript/TypeScript, React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Docker foundation into Stripe-ready full-stack depth by methodically closing your four priority gaps. Phase 1 hardens your fundamentals and introduces Python; Phase 2 attacks Python and Security Compliance head-on with auth, OWASP controls, PCI-aware data handling, and automated scanning; Phase 3 turns Docker into real AWS and Kubernetes deployment with full CI/CD; Phase 4 closes System Design through payments-scale architecture, data-layer scaling, load testing, and resilience work; Phase 5 packages the whole effort as an interview-ready portfolio and drills coding, design, and behavioral rounds. Every task produces a concrete artifact, so by the end your gap list is fully backed by demonstrable work rather than claimed familiarity.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Lock in the fundamentals Stripe's code review and live-coding rounds assume. The candidate already ships JavaScript, TypeScript, React and Node.js; this phase raises them to payments-grade rigour: strictly typed domain models, a real test pyramid, and an automated lint/type/test gate that every later phase builds on.

tasks.title: Payments-Grade TypeScript Domain Model
tasks.description: Take an existing feature and rebuild its domain layer in strict TypeScript (strict, noImplicitAny, exactOptionalPropertyTypes). Model Money as a branded amount + currency pair instead of a number, model transaction states as a discriminated union so illegal states are unrepresentable, and share DTO interfaces between the Express API and the React client through a workspace types package. Replace every `any` and `as` cast with a narrowed type or a Zod schema parsed at the boundary.
tasks.deliverable: Shared types package (Money branded type, TransactionState discriminated union, request/response DTOs) consumed by both API and React app, `tsc --noEmit` clean at strict settings, plus type-level tests (expectTypeOf) proving the invalid states do not compile.

tasks.title: Repository Quality Gate: Lint, Format, Types, Conventional Commits
tasks.description: Make quality non-optional and identical locally and in CI. Configure ESLint (typescript-eslint + react-hooks + jsx-a11y), Prettier, and commitlint, then wire Husky + lint-staged so staged files are formatted, linted and type-checked before commit. Expose lint, typecheck, format and test as npm scripts that run unchanged inside Docker and in the pipeline.
tasks.deliverable: ESLint/Prettier/commitlint configs, Husky pre-commit and commit-msg hooks, a single `pnpm quality` script chain, and a demo showing a non-conventional commit and a lint error both blocked locally.

tasks.title: Backend Test Pyramid against Real Postgres and Redis
tasks.description: Build the testing discipline the role requires. Add unit tests for pricing/validation logic, integration tests for Express routes using Supertest against a Testcontainers Postgres and Redis, and contract tests that assert response shapes match the shared DTOs. Cover one happy path, one validation failure, one auth/permission denial and one idempotent-retry case per resource, and enforce a coverage threshold in the test config.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest + Supertest suite with Testcontainers Postgres/Redis, 80%+ line coverage on the API layer enforced by a threshold, and a coverage report committed as a build artifact.

tasks.title: React + TypeScript Frontend Quality Pass
tasks.description: Apply the same rigour to the React surface. Refactor a dashboard view into typed function components with hooks, extract data fetching into a small typed client layer with explicit loading/error/empty states, add error boundaries and memoisation where a profiler shows wasted renders, and make the accessibility lint rules pass on every component.
tasks.deliverable: Typed React data layer with loading/error states, component tests with React Testing Library (Vitest), jsx-a11y clean, and a React DevTools profiler screenshot showing reduced re-renders after memoisation.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Close the two hard gaps that suppress the candidate's level: Kubernetes (the deployment model behind the role's stack) and Python (Stripe's primary scripting and service language). Docker is already strong, so Kubernetes is a continuation rather than a restart; Python is a second-language build on top of the existing Node.js backend experience.

tasks.title: Kubernetes Fundamentals on a Local Cluster
tasks.description: Run the existing Dockerized stack on a local kind cluster. Write raw manifests for Deployments (frontend, API, worker), ClusterIP Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps and Secrets, resource requests/limits, and liveness/readiness/startup probes with a real readiness endpoint. Prove self-healing by deleting a pod and rolling out a bad image to watch the readiness probe hold traffic back.
tasks.deliverable: Versioned `k8s/` manifests that boot the full stack on a kind cluster with `kind create cluster && kubectl apply -k k8s/dev`; a demo log of a pod deletion self-healing and a failed-readiness rollout being caught.

tasks.title: Helm Chart with Dev/Staging/Prod Overlays
tasks.description: Turn the raw manifests into a reusable Helm chart parameterised by values files (image tag, replica count, resource limits, env, ingress host) with dev/staging/prod values overlays, and a Kustomize alternative for comparison. Add a `helm template` diff check so a values change can be reviewed before it ships, and template the database/Redis connection settings from environment values rather than hardcoding them.
tasks.deliverable: Helm chart (`helm lint` clean, `helm template` renders for three environments), values-dev/staging/prod files, a documented Kustomize-vs-Helm comparison, and a rendered-manifest diff committed to the repo.

tasks.title: Kubernetes Operations: Scaling, Rollouts, State, Network Policy, RBAC
tasks.description: Operate the cluster like production. Configure HorizontalPodAutoscaler on CPU and custom metrics, exercise rolling update and `kubectl rollout undo` for zero-downtime releases, run Postgres and Redis as StatefulSets with PersistentVolumeClaims and a headless Service (or connect to managed equivalents), enforce a default-deny NetworkPolicy that only allows app-to-database and app-to-cache traffic, add a scoped ServiceAccount with RBAC and a PodDisruptionBudget. Write the failure runbook for CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled and Pending pods.
tasks.deliverable: HPA, StatefulSets with PVCs, default-deny NetworkPolicies with explicit allows, namespaced RBAC role/service account, PodDisruptionBudget, and a Kubernetes incident runbook with four reproduced-and-diagnosed failures.

tasks.title: Python Service Layer and Stripe Integration
tasks.description: Build a real Python service, not a script: a FastAPI (or Flask) internal service with type hints throughout, Pydantic models for request validation, async I/O for outbound calls, structured logging, pytest unit and integration tests, and Ruff/Black/mypy in the quality gate. Integrate the official Stripe Python SDK for create-payment-intent and refund flows, sending an idempotency key on every mutating call and verifying webhook signatures before processing an event.
tasks.deliverable: Python service with typed routes and Pydantic models, pytest suite at 80%+ coverage, mypy strict clean, a Dockerfile shared with the Phase 1 image, and a working Stripe test-mode payment + signature-verified webhook handler with an idempotency-key replay test.

tasks.title: CI/CD Level-Up: Reusable Pipeline with Scanning and Rollback
tasks.description: Convert partial pipeline knowledge into ownership. Extract reusable workflows (workflow_call) and composite actions for setup/lint/test/build, add path filters and concurrency groups, run dependency and container scanning (Trivy, npm audit) failing on HIGH/CRITICAL, build multi-arch images with buildx layer caching, and add a deployment job with a post-deploy smoke test and an automatic rollback path. Track lead time, deploy frequency and change-failure rate across at least three real deploys.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable GitHub Actions workflows + composite actions used by CI, scan gates blocking merges, buildx cached image build, a deploy workflow with smoke test and rollback job, and a DORA metrics table from three real deploys.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Take the containerized, chart-packaged stack onto AWS and run Kubernetes there as a managed service. The gap is not conceptual - the candidate already thinks in services, queues and caches - it is the AWS API and operational model itself (IAM, VPC, EKS, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, CloudWatch) expressed as code so it is reproducible and reviewable.

tasks.title: AWS Foundation as Code: IAM, Networking, Budgets, Remote State
tasks.description: Set up a clean AWS account baseline with Terraform: a versioned S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking, a least-privilege deployment role (no long-lived root or admin keys), an MFA-protected operator identity, budget alarms, and a VPC with public/private subnets across two AZs, route tables, NAT gateway and security groups. Include a teardown path so the environment can be destroyed without orphaned resources.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning VPC/networking, IAM roles and policies, budget alarms and an S3+DynamoDB state backend; least-privilege deployment policy documented; `terraform destroy` verified clean; AWS billing screenshot showing the active budget alarm.

tasks.title: Deploy the Full Stack to EKS with ALB Ingress and IRSA
tasks.description: Push images to Amazon ECR and run the Phase 2 Helm chart on a managed EKS cluster. Provision node groups across private subnets, install the AWS Load Balancer Controller and point the Ingress at an ALB with target-group health checks, and use IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) so pods get scoped AWS permissions instead of node-level credentials. Deploy the frontend, API, worker and Python service as separate workloads.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned ECR and EKS with managed node groups, AWS Load Balancer Controller, IRSA-scoped service accounts, the full stack reachable on a public HTTPS URL via ALB, and an architecture diagram of the deployed topology.

tasks.title: Managed Data and Secrets: RDS, ElastiCache, S3, Secrets Manager
tasks.description: Move the stateful tier off in-cluster containers. Provision RDS Postgres in private subnets with a security group that only accepts traffic from the EKS node/service security group, run migrations against it, provision ElastiCache Redis and repoint the cache/rate-limit/session code at it, create a versioned encrypted S3 bucket for uploads with least-privilege policies and pre-signed URLs, and store credentials in Secrets Manager injected via External Secrets Operator or CSI driver rather than in a Kubernetes Secret.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS + ElastiCache + S3 + Secrets Manager with security-group chaining and encryption enabled; migration run against RDS; proof of a pre-signed S3 upload; app screenshot of a cache hit served from ElastiCache; no plaintext credentials in the repo.

tasks.title: Keyless Delivery to AWS with Blue/Green and Rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery from GitHub to EKS with no static AWS keys: configure GitHub OIDC federation to a narrowly-trusted IAM role, then extend the pipeline to build and push to ECR, update the Helm release, and perform a blue/green or canary rollout (Argo Rollouts) that waits for health metrics before shifting traffic. Add a protected production environment with manual approval, a tested one-command rollback, and alerting on failed deploys.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-authenticated deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> Helm/Argo Rollouts canary -> promote), IAM trust policy JSON, GitHub Environment approval gate, and logs proving both a successful progressive rollout and a successful rollback.

tasks.title: Async and Distributed Patterns: Queue Workers, Retries, Dead Letters
tasks.description: Model a real distributed workflow - payment confirmation to receipt email, ledger entry and analytics event. Put the slow and failure-prone work on an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue, idempotent consumers keyed on an event id, exponential backoff with jitter, and visibility-timeout handling. Run the worker as its own EKS Deployment scaled on queue depth (KEDA), and document the at-least-once delivery semantics and where exactly-once is simulated by idempotency.
tasks.deliverable: SQS + DLQ Terraform, idempotent worker Deployment scaled on queue depth, poison-message replay script for the DLQ, and a written note on delivery semantics and idempotency boundaries with a test proving duplicate events are processed once.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it is trustworthy under load and audit'. This phase closes Security Compliance and levels up System Design: hardening the platform against the OWASP Top 10 and Stripe's compliance expectations (PCI DSS scope, SOC 2 controls, PII handling), then proving scalability with observability, SLOs and load tests, and finally writing the architecture documents that turn implementation into interview language.

tasks.title: Compliance Control Matrix for a Payments Product
tasks.description: Build a defensible compliance posture instead of reading about it. Map the platform to the relevant PCI DSS v4.0 requirements for a SAQ-A/SAQ-D-merchant boundary (never storing card data, tokenising through Stripe, TLS everywhere, key management, logging and monitoring, access control, vulnerability management, change control) and to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (security, availability, confidentiality). Record which controls are implemented by the code and which by AWS, and identify the gaps with a remediation task each.
tasks.deliverable: Compliance control matrix (control -> requirement -> implementation -> evidence -> gap -> remediation), a documented card-data-flow diagram showing where PCI scope ends, and an encryption/at-rest-and-in-transit inventory covering RDS, S3, ElastiCache and secrets.

tasks.title: OWASP Top 10 Hardening and Threat Model
tasks.description: Threat-model the system with STRIDE and then fix what the model finds. Enforce parameterised queries and least-privilege DB roles, add input validation at every boundary with Zod/Pydantic, configure helmet with a strict CSP and secure cookie flags, implement short-lived JWTs with refresh rotation and RBAC checks on every route, add a Redis token-bucket rate limiter on auth and payment endpoints, verify Stripe webhook signatures, scrub PII from logs, and add SAST (CodeQL) plus dependency and container scanning to the pipeline with a documented vulnerability triage and patching SLA.
tasks.deliverable: STRIDE threat model with mitigations, hardened API (helmet/CSP, RBAC, validation, rate limiting, webhook verification, log redaction), SAST + dependency + container scanning gates in CI, and an automated security test suite including auth-bypass and injection attempts.

tasks.title: Observability, SLOs and On-Call Alerting
tasks.description: Make the system explain itself. Emit structured JSON logs with correlation/request IDs, expose Prometheus metrics (request rate, latency histograms, error rate, queue depth, cache hit ratio, DB pool saturation) and ship them to Grafana, and add OpenTelemetry tracing across ALB -> API -> queue -> worker with context propagation. Define SLOs for availability and p95 latency with error budgets, then build Grafana alerts and CloudWatch alarms tied to them plus a runbook for each alert.
tasks.deliverable: Grafana dashboard, Prometheus metrics endpoint, OTel traces of a request spanning the frontend, API and worker, a written SLO document with error budgets, and three or more alert rules each linked to a runbook entry.

tasks.title: Load Testing and Autoscaling to a Defined SLO
tasks.description: Prove the platform scales and find the real ceiling. Write k6 scenarios (smoke, average load, spike, soak) against the deployed payment flow, capture p95/p99 latency, throughput and error rate, and tune Kubernetes HPA/KEDA targets, node-group scaling and connection-pool sizes until the stated SLO holds under the average-load scenario. Identify and document the first bottleneck (typically DB connections or cache stampede) with the fix applied and re-measured.
tasks.deliverable: k6 scenario scripts and a load-test report with before/after charts showing scale-out holding the SLO, tuned HPA/KEDA and node-group config, and a bottleneck analysis with the applied fix and new measurements.

tasks.title: System Design Documents for Payments-Scale Problems
tasks.description: Write three design documents in the shape of an interview answer and a real RFC: (1) a high-throughput, idempotent payments/ledger API with exactly-once semantics and double-entry bookkeeping; (2) a multi-tenant SaaS backend with tenant isolation, RBAC and per-tenant rate limiting; (3) a webhook/notification delivery system with retries, ordering, backpressure and DLQ handling. Each must cover API contracts, data model and indexes, caching and invalidation, queueing and consistency tradeoffs, hosting topology on AWS/EKS, capacity estimates, and failure modes with circuit breakers and timeouts.
tasks.deliverable: Three design docs with boxes-and-arrows diagrams, capacity/SLO math, SQL-vs-cache-vs-queue tradeoff tables per read/write path, failure-mode matrices, and a self-critique list of where an interviewer would push back.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the phases into interview performance for the Full Stack Engineer loop at Stripe: practical coding in TypeScript and Python, Kubernetes/AWS/security deep dives, system design, and behavioural stories grounded in measured outcomes. Every artifact becomes a diagram, a metric and a defensible decision.

tasks.title: Timed System Design and Architecture Drills
tasks.description: Turn the Phase 4 documents into spoken fluency. Run six timed 35-40 minute prompts (URL shortener with analytics, idempotent payment processing, a high-throughput ledger, a rate-limited public API, a multi-tenant SaaS backend, a webhook delivery pipeline) and two recorded mock sessions. For each: clarify requirements, estimate scale, sketch the diagram, choose the data model, place caching and queues, name the bottleneck and the failure mode, then write the answers to the three hardest follow-ups.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, tradeoffs, follow-up answers) and two recorded mocks with a reviewed list of recurring weaknesses.

tasks.title: Practical Coding Drills in TypeScript and Python
tasks.description: Rehearse the format Stripe actually uses: read an unfamiliar repo, extend a running service, and write tests - not just algorithm puzzles. Complete 20 timed algorithm problems (arrays, hashing, graphs, concurrency) in TypeScript, then 10 more in Python for the second-language round, and run three 45-minute practical drills: add a paginated, validated endpoint with tests to the Phase 1 API, add a background job with a retry policy, and debug a failing concurrency test. Write a short retrospective after each on time management and communicated tradeoffs.
tasks.deliverable: 30 solved problems with notes, three completed practical drill repos with passing tests, and a drill retrospective log listing recurring mistakes and how each was corrected.

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Architecture Case Study and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate the code, Helm charts, Terraform, CI/CD workflows, tests, scan reports, dashboards, load-test results, compliance matrix and runbooks into one clean public repository whose README reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, one-command local quickstart, AWS/EKS deployment guide, observability screenshots, security and compliance posture, load-test numbers and the rollback runbook. Then write RESUME.md mapping each feature to a resume bullet and rewrite the current Full Stack Developer role to surface the new depth (Kubernetes, AWS, compliance, Python) alongside the existing microservices and test-coverage work.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repo with architecture diagram, local + AWS quickstarts, dashboards/screenshots, load-test and cost numbers, a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping, and a rewritten resume section reviewed against the Full Stack Engineer job description.

tasks.title: Chart-Consolidated Kubernetes and AWS Deep Dives
tasks.description: Compress hands-on experience into interview-ready precision. Build one-page cheat sheets for the Kubernetes objects actually used (Deployment, Service, Ingress, HPA, StatefulSet, PVC, NetworkPolicy, RBAC, probes, resource limits) and for core AWS services (IAM, VPC, EKS, ECR, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SQS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch), each paired with the exact thing built with it in Phases 2-4. Then sit a timed practice exam or equivalent scenario set (CKAD-style object tasks and AWS SAA-C03 domains) and review every miss to a service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: Cheat sheets for 12+ Kubernetes objects and 10+ AWS services each linked to a project artifact, one timed practice exam score report per topic, and a wrong-answer review log targeting consistent 80%+.

tasks.title: Mock Interviews and a Metrics-Backed STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop: a live coding round, a Kubernetes/AWS deep dive, a security and compliance discussion, a system design round and a behavioural pass. Build a STAR bank of 8+ stories with real numbers from this plan - 'cut p95 latency by X% with a Redis cache-aside layer', 'held the SLO through a k6 spike by tuning HPA on EKS', 'closed 12 PCI DSS control gaps with evidence', 'shipped a keyless OIDC pipeline with automatic rollback' - plus one story framing the candidate's front-to-back range as an advantage in a payments codebase. Log every question asked and tighten the answer.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (coding and system design), a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist covering TypeScript, React, Node.js, Python, Kubernetes, AWS, CI/CD, security compliance and system design.

careerPlans.summary: A 10-week roadmap for a Full Stack Developer (2023-present, scalable components and microservices with high test coverage) targeting Full Stack Engineer at Stripe, built around the four priority gaps - Kubernetes, AWS, Security Compliance and Python - and the two partial skills that need leveling up, CI/CD and System Design. The plan deliberately starts from strength: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Node.js/Express, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Redis and Docker are already on the profile, so Phase 1 spends only 1-2 weeks raising them to payments-grade rigour (branded Money and discriminated-union domain models, a Testcontainers-backed test pyramid, an enforced lint/type/test gate). Phase 2 is the hard-skill deep dive: Kubernetes from raw manifests through Helm overlays to HPA, StatefulSets, NetworkPolicy and RBAC on a local kind cluster, plus a real typed Python service integrating the Stripe SDK with idempotency keys and webhook signature verification, and a CI/CD pipeline upgraded to reusable workflows with scanning gates and rollback. Phase 3 puts that stack on AWS as code - Terraform VPC/IAM, EKS with ALB Ingress and IRSA, RDS and ElastiCache and S3 and Secrets Manager, keyless OIDC blue/green delivery, and SQS-based async workers with dead-letter and idempotency handling. Phase 4 makes it production-trustworthy: a PCI DSS and SOC 2 control matrix with evidence, STRIDE threat modelling plus OWASP Top 10 hardening and SAST/DAST scanning, observability with Prometheus/Grafana and OpenTelemetry against defined SLOs, k6 load testing that tunes autoscaling to hold those SLOs, and three written system design documents. Phase 5 converts everything into interview output: timed design drills, practical coding in TypeScript and Python, a public portfolio repo written as a case study with resume mapping, consolidated Kubernetes/AWS cheat sheets, and a metric-backed STAR story bank. No task is generic - each names the gap it closes, reuses the candidate's existing full-stack experience as the starting point, and produces an inspectable deliverable whose numbers become interview evidence.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: The candidate already ships React, TypeScript, Node/Express, PostgreSQL, Redis and Docker with high test coverage - so this phase is not about learning the stack, it is about raising it to Stripe's production bar.
