Objective: turn a working app into a typed, contract-driven, fully containerized system whose quality gates (strict types, lint, layered API, integration tests) run identically on a laptop and in CI. This gives every later phase a reproducible build-test-ship loop.

tasks.title: Strict TypeScript Architecture with a Shared Contract Package
tasks.description: Retrofit the reference full-stack app so TypeScript is enforced end to end instead of being used loosely. Enable `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`; convert the repo to project references with three packages: `web` (React), `api` (Express) and a shared `contracts` package that owns every request/response DTO, union and branded ID type. Replace all `any` with `unknown` plus narrowing, add Zod schemas for runtime validation at the API boundary, and derive the static types from those schemas with `z.infer` so validation and types can never drift. Add a `tsc --noEmit` gate that fails on any error or implicit any.
tasks.deliverable: Monorepo with strict `tsconfig` project references, a published `@app/contracts` package of DTOs/Zod schemas consumed by both web and api, zero `any` in application code, and a passing `tsc --noEmit` run documented in the README.

tasks.title: React Frontend Quality Baseline: Component Architecture and Test Coverage
tasks.description: Consolidate the React side into a defensible architecture: split presentational components from data-fetching containers, centralize server state in a query layer (TanStack Query or RTK Query) with typed hooks over the `contracts` package, and implement loading, empty, error and optimistic-update states for every list and detail view. Add route-level code splitting with React.lazy and Suspense, memoize expensive renders, and enforce accessibility with eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y plus keyboard-navigable components. Cover the create/edit flow with React Testing Library and MSW so tests exercise real network contracts rather than mocked internals.
tasks.deliverable: Refactored React app with typed data-fetching hooks, full loading/error/empty states, code-split routes, an axe or Lighthouse accessibility report, and an RTL + MSW suite covering the primary CRUD journey at 80%+ component coverage.

tasks.title: Express API Refactor to OpenAPI-First Layered Design
tasks.description: Restructure the Express API into explicit layers (routes -> controllers -> services -> repositories) so business logic is testable without an HTTP server. Add a typed error-handling middleware with a consistent error envelope and correlation IDs, request validation driven by the shared Zod schemas, cursor-based pagination, idempotency keys on write endpoints, and a generated OpenAPI 3.1 document served at `/openapi.json`. Generate a typed client from that spec and use it in the React app so a contract break fails CI instead of production.
tasks.deliverable: Layered Express API with centralized error middleware, validated inputs, pagination and idempotency keys, an auto-generated OpenAPI 3.1 spec with a generated typed client, and integration tests against a real Postgres via Testcontainers.

tasks.title: One-Command Containerized Development Environment
tasks.description: Make the whole system boot reproducibly from a clean clone. Write multi-stage Dockerfiles for `web` (build stage -> nginx or node runtime), `api` and a background worker, all running as a non-root user with pinned base images and a correct `.dockerignore`. Add a `docker-compose.yml` that wires the three services to Postgres and Redis on isolated networks with named volumes, healthchecks, `depends_on` conditions and environment-driven configuration, plus bind mounts for hot reload in a dev override file. Provide a Makefile with `make setup`, `make dev`, `make test` so no step is tribal knowledge.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfiles for web/api/worker, `docker-compose.yml` plus a dev override with healthchecks and volume persistence, and a documented `make setup && make dev` boot from a clean machine.

tasks.title: First CI Quality Gate: Lint, Typecheck and Test Matrix
tasks.description: Level up from ad-hoc local checks to an enforced pipeline. Add a GitHub Actions workflow triggered on pull requests that caches dependencies, runs ESLint/Prettier check, `tsc --noEmit`, the unit and integration suites and a build of all three Docker images (no push), using a matrix over the supported Node versions and a Postgres/Redis service container for integration tests. Upload coverage and JUnit artifacts, add `concurrency` groups to cancel superseded runs, and enable branch protection so a red check blocks merge.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions CI workflow with lint/typecheck/test matrix, service containers, cached dependencies, uploaded coverage artifacts, concurrency cancellation and branch protection - demonstrated by a screenshot of a green PR run.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Objective: attack the three priority gaps that are not solved simply by 'deploying to a cloud' - Kubernetes, Security Compliance and Python. The candidate runs containers with Docker but has never scheduled them on a cluster, has no compliance or threat-modelling vocabulary despite targeting a payments company, and has no polyglot backend experience. Each task produces an artifact that Phase 3 then lifts into AWS and Phase 5 turns into interview material.

tasks.title: Kubernetes Fundamentals: Run the Full Stack on a Local Cluster
tasks.description: Move the Compose stack onto Kubernetes using `kind` (multi-node) or minikube. Deploy api, web and worker as Deployments with liveness, readiness and startup probes, Services and an Ingress; externalize configuration into ConfigMaps and credentials into Secrets; set CPU/memory requests and limits, a ResourceQuota and LimitRange, and a HorizontalPodAutoscaler. Run Postgres and Redis as in-cluster dependencies first, then migrate them out of the cluster once Phase 3 introduces managed services. Practice the operational loop: `kubectl logs -f`, `describe`, `exec`, `events`, `rollout status` and `rollout undo`, and deliberately reproduce a CrashLoopBackOff, an ImagePullBackOff and a failed readiness probe to document the diagnosis path.
tasks.deliverable: `k8s/` manifests or a Helm chart deploying the full stack to kind, a documented `kubectl` troubleshooting runbook with three reproduced failure scenarios, and a screenshot of a successful rollout plus HPA scaling under load.

tasks.title: Packaging, Progressive Rollouts and Cluster Network Policy
tasks.description: Turn the raw manifests into a reusable deployment artifact. Parameterize with Helm (values.schema.json, `values-dev.yaml` and `values-prod.yaml`) or Kustomize overlays for dev/staging/prod, and add the production-safety objects a reviewer will look for: rolling-update strategy with `maxSurge`/`maxUnavailable`, PodDisruptionBudget, topology spread constraints across zones, default-deny NetworkPolicies that allow only web -> api -> data traffic, ServiceAccounts with least-privilege RBAC, Pod Security Admission at the `restricted` level, persistent volumes with a StorageClass, and a pre-install migration Job. Validate every overlay with `helm template` in CI.
tasks.deliverable: Parameterized Helm chart (or Kustomize overlays) for three environments including rolling-update strategy, PDB, topology spread, default-deny NetworkPolicies, RBAC ServiceAccounts, PSA `restricted` compliance and a migration Job, all rendered and linted in CI.

tasks.title: Python for Backend Engineers: Typed Service with API Parity
tasks.description: Close the Python gap by building a real, typed service rather than reading tutorials. Create a FastAPI microservice (for example a reporting/aggregation service or a transactional notification worker) with Pydantic v2 models, SQLAlchemy 2.0 async access to the same PostgreSQL database, dependency-injected settings, structured logging and OpenAPI output. Enforce quality with `mypy --strict`, Ruff, Black and a pytest suite (unit + integration with a containerized database), and use `uv` for reproducible dependency locking. The service must satisfy the same shared OpenAPI contract as the Node API so the React client can call either backend interchangeably, and it must be containerized and deployed alongside the existing services.
tasks.deliverable: Containerized, `mypy --strict`-clean FastAPI service with Pydantic schemas, async SQLAlchemy access, pytest unit/integration suite, pinned dependencies, generated OpenAPI spec matching the shared contract, and a README note on the Node/Python interoperability decision.

tasks.title: Security Compliance Engineering: From Threat Model to Auditable Controls
tasks.description: Build the compliance literacy Stripe interviews for. Write a STRIDE threat model for the whole system (browser, API, worker, database, CI, cloud account) and derive concrete controls from it: full OWASP Top 10 and API Security Top 10 remediation on the Express/FastAPI services (parameterized queries, output encoding, SSRF allow-lists, safe deserialization, security headers with Helmet, CORS and CSP tightening, brute-force and request-size limits); secrets removed from source and loaded from a secret store with rotation; TLS everywhere and encryption at rest; PII classification with field-level redaction in logs; immutable audit logging for money-moving and permission-changing actions; and a documented data-retention policy. Automate the evidence: SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep), dependency and container scanning (Trivy, Dependabot), secret scanning with gitleaks, and DAST (OWASP ZAP) against the staging deployment, all gating merges on HIGH/CRITICAL findings. Produce a PCI-DSS v4.0 and SOC 2 control-mapping matrix that links each applicable requirement to the implementation and the CI job that proves it.
tasks.deliverable: STRIDE threat model, remediated OWASP/ASVS checklist, secrets-management and audit-logging implementation, CI jobs for SAST/SCA/secret scanning/DAST that fail on HIGH findings, an incident-response runbook for a leaked credential, and a PCI-DSS/SOC 2 control matrix mapping controls to code, pipeline jobs and evidence.

tasks.title: Identity, Authorization and Tenant Isolation Hardening
tasks.description: Harden the access path of the application itself. Replace hand-rolled session logic with standards-based authentication (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC via a provider such as Auth0 or Keycloak, or a reviewed implementation) covering PKCE authorization-code flow, short-lived access tokens with refresh-token rotation, secure cookie flags, CSRF protection and session revocation. Implement role- and attribute-based authorization middleware with a policy table, then enforce multi-tenant isolation at the database layer using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security with a per-request tenant context, verifying it cannot be bypassed through the API. Add automated authorization tests that assert a user from tenant A receives 404/403 for tenant B resources, and run a self-directed penetration-test checklist (IDOR, privilege escalation, JWT confusion, rate-limit bypass) with every finding fixed and retested.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based auth with rotating refresh tokens, RBAC/ABAC policy middleware, PostgreSQL RLS tenant isolation, a cross-tenant authorization test suite proving denial, and a penetration-test report with all findings remediated and retested.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Objective: close the AWS gap by deploying the Phase 1-2 artifacts to real managed infrastructure using Kubernetes as the control plane - EKS, ALB, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, Secrets Manager and ECR, all provisioned as Terraform code and delivered by an OIDC-authenticated pipeline. Docker familiarity and the Phase 2 cluster work transfer directly; the new material is AWS's IAM, networking and managed-service semantics plus infrastructure as code and progressive delivery.

tasks.title: AWS Foundation as Code: Accounts, IAM, Networking and Remote State
tasks.description: Stand up a production-shaped AWS baseline with Terraform. Structure the repo into `bootstrap`, `modules` and per-environment roots, store state in an S3 backend with DynamoDB locking and state encryption, and define a least-privilege IAM model: no root usage, MFA-enforced admin, a separate CI deploy role, and permission boundaries. Build the VPC from scratch - two or more Availability Zones, public and private subnets, internet and NAT gateways, route tables, NACLs, VPC endpoints for ECR/S3/Secrets Manager so traffic never leaves the AWS network, and VPC flow logs. Add AWS Budgets with alerts, CloudTrail with log-file validation, GuardDuty and a default-encryption KMS key. Enforce `terraform fmt`, `validate`, `plan` in CI and forbid console-only changes.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo with modular VPC (multi-AZ, NAT, VPC endpoints, flow logs), least-privilege IAM roles and policies, budget alarms, KMS key, CloudTrail and GuardDuty enabled, S3+DynamoDB remote state, and a committed plan output for review.

tasks.title: Deploy the Helm Chart to Amazon EKS behind an ALB
tasks.description: Provision an EKS cluster in Terraform (managed node groups plus a Fargate profile for the worker) and deploy the Phase 2 Helm chart unchanged across at least two Availability Zones. Install the AWS Load Balancer Controller and expose the API through an ALB Ingress with TLS via ACM and cert-manager, health checks and target-group stickiness. Wire pod-level IAM with IRSA so the API reads S3 and Secrets Manager through a scoped role rather than node credentials, configure Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter, and turn on control-plane audit logs to CloudWatch. Document the differences between the local kind cluster and EKS (storage classes, ingress, IAM, node lifecycle) explicitly.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned EKS with node groups and Fargate profile, Helm release running on 2+ AZs, ALB Ingress with TLS and health checks, IRSA role for the API, Karpenter or Cluster Autoscaler configured, control-plane logs shipped, and a live HTTPS URL plus an architecture diagram.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Caching and Secrets on AWS
tasks.description: Replace every in-cluster stateful dependency with a managed, secured service. Provision RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ in private subnets with automated backups, parameter groups tuned for the workload and a security group that accepts traffic only from the EKS node/pod security group; ElastiCache Redis in a cluster mode with encryption in transit and at rest; an S3 bucket for user uploads with versioning, lifecycle rules, Block Public Access and a least-privilege bucket policy; and Secrets Manager entries with automatic rotation delivered into the cluster by the External Secrets Operator. Run the real migrations against RDS, point the API and worker at the managed endpoints through ConfigMaps, and prove the Redis cache is serving hits from ElastiCache rather than a pod.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Multi-AZ, ElastiCache Redis, S3 and Secrets Manager with automatic rotation; security-group chaining documented; External Secrets Operator syncing into the cluster; executed migrations, a verified S3 upload, and evidence of an ElastiCache cache hit.

tasks.title: Keyless CI/CD to EKS with Canary Delivery and Automated Rollback
tasks.description: Turn the Phase 1 pipeline into a real delivery system. Configure GitHub OIDC federation to a scoped IAM role so no static AWS keys exist anywhere; build the images once, tag them with the commit SHA, push to ECR with immutable tags and sign them (cosign/Sigstore). Deploy with Helm, then add progressive delivery using Argo Rollouts or Flagger: a canary step to 10%/25%/50% gated on Prometheus analysis of error rate and latency, automatic promotion on success and automatic rollback on metric breach. Add a manual approval environment gate for production, post-deploy smoke tests against the live URL, database migration ordering guarantees, and DORA metrics captured from each release.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-authenticated workflow (build -> ECR -> Helm -> canary analysis -> promote/rollback), cosign-signed images, GitHub Environment approval gate, logs of one successful canary promotion and one automatic rollback, and a DORA metrics table from at least three releases.

tasks.title: Infrastructure as Code Discipline: Modules, Policy Checks and Drift Detection
tasks.description: Make the AWS estate maintainable and defensible. Refactor duplicated Terraform into versioned modules with documented inputs/outputs, split dev/staging/prod through var-files or workspaces with environment-specific sizing, and make the same pipeline promote an identical artifact across all three. Add policy-as-code gates (OPA/Conftest, Checkov or tfsec) that block non-compliant plans - public buckets, unencrypted volumes, wildcard IAM, missing tags - plus `terraform plan` on every PR and a scheduled drift-detection job that fails when the console diverges from code. Publish a cost report and apply at least three concrete optimizations.
tasks.deliverable: Versioned Terraform modules with three environments deployed from one pipeline, policy-as-code gates blocking non-compliant plans, scheduled drift detection, a tagging standard applied via `default_tags`, and a cost report with three applied optimizations and their dollar deltas.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Objective: move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives peak traffic'. This is where the two partial skills are closed for real - System Design becomes measurable through observability, autoscaling and load tests, and CI/CD matures into reliability engineering. Redis is deepened from basic caching into rate limiting, queues and hot-key handling, and the Python service from Phase 2 is scaled alongside the Node API.

tasks.title: End-to-End Observability with SLOs and Error Budgets
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed system so architectural claims can be measured. Emit structured JSON logs with correlation and tenant IDs from both the Express and FastAPI services, expose RED metrics (rate, errors, duration) and USE metrics, and propagate OpenTelemetry traces through browser -> ALB -> API -> worker -> database. Stand up Prometheus and Grafana (or CloudWatch dashboards if on managed services) with dashboards for p50/p95/p99 latency, error ratio, saturation, DB connection-pool usage and cache hit rate. Define SLOs with error budgets for the two most important user journeys, add multi-window burn-rate alerts plus a runbook per alert, and prove the alert fires by injecting a fault.
tasks.deliverable: OTel tracing across services, structured logging with correlation IDs, Grafana/CloudWatch dashboards, documented SLOs with error budgets, burn-rate alerts each linked to a runbook, and a recorded fault injection where the alert fires correctly.

tasks.title: Redis at Scale: Caching, Rate Limiting and Async Pipelines
tasks.description: Take Redis from a single tutorial cache-aside call to three production-grade uses, all measured. First, a cache-aside layer on the hottest read paths with explicit key-naming and TTL policy, versioned keys, negative caching, stampede protection via locks or probabilistic early expiry, and a documented invalidation strategy on write; report hit rate and p95 change. Second, a distributed token-bucket rate limiter in Redis (Lua script for atomicity) applied per API key and per tenant, returning 429 with `Retry-After`, with a test proving it holds under parallel load. Third, asynchronous work: move slow operations (email, PDF/report generation, webhook fan-out) to an SQS or Kafka queue consumed by the worker, with idempotent handlers keyed by message ID, retry with exponential backoff, a dead-letter queue and an outbox pattern so a database write and its event are never split.
tasks.deliverable: Cache-aside layer with measured hit-rate and latency improvement, atomic Redis rate limiter with load-proven 429 behaviour, and an SQS/Kafka-backed worker with DLQ, retries, idempotency keys and transactional outbox - each with a before/after benchmark.

tasks.title: Load Testing and Autoscaling to a Stated SLO
tasks.description: Prove the system scales and find where it breaks. Write k6 (or Locust) scenarios covering a read-heavy browsing path, a write-heavy transactional path and a spike/stress profile, then run them against the EKS deployment while capturing p95/p99 latency, throughput and error rate. Configure Kubernetes autoscaling on the right signals - HPA on CPU and custom request-rate metrics, KEDA for queue depth on the worker, VPA recommendations for right-sizing - and tune target values, stabilization windows and min/max replicas to hold the SLO during the spike. Reduce database pressure with PgBouncer or RDS Proxy and connection-pool tuning, then document the first real bottleneck (usually the connection pool or a missing index), the fix and the measured improvement.
tasks.deliverable: k6/Locust scenarios for read, write and spike profiles, a load-test report with before/after p95 and throughput showing scale-out, autoscaling policies for HPA/KEDA/VPA, database-pool tuning, and a written bottleneck analysis with the applied fix.

tasks.title: System Design Fluency: Three Written Design Docs with Tradeoff Analysis
tasks.description: Convert hands-on implementation into design language. Write three full design documents - a high-throughput payments/ledger API with exactly-once semantics and idempotency keys, a multi-tenant SaaS backend with noisy-neighbour isolation, and a user-upload and media-processing pipeline - each covering requirements and non-goals, back-of-envelope capacity math, API contracts, data model with indexes and partitioning, caching strategy and invalidation, queueing, backpressure and flow control, consistency and isolation tradeoffs, deployment topology on EKS/AWS, failure modes with timeout/retry/circuit-breaker policy, and cost at scale. Every decision must cite an artifact from Phases 2-4 ('chose Redis cache-aside with versioned TTLs because we measured 85% hit rate'), and each doc ends with the three hardest questions an interviewer would ask plus the answers.
tasks.deliverable: Three design docs with diagrams, capacity estimates, tradeoff tables (SQL vs Redis vs queue per read/write path), failure-mode matrices, cost models, and a self-critique section of likely interviewer pushback with prepared answers.

tasks.title: Reliability, Disaster Recovery and Cost Engineering
tasks.description: Finish the production story with the operational discipline a payments platform requires. Define and test RTO/RPO: automated RDS snapshots with a verified point-in-time restore into a separate environment, S3 cross-region replication, and a documented backup-restore runbook with the measured recovery time. Extend the pipeline to blue/green or canary with automatic verification and one-click rollback for both application and migration, and rehearse a rollback under load. Run chaos experiments (kill a pod, drain a node, break a dependency, saturate Redis) and record system behaviour against the error budget. Then produce a FinOps review: cost per request, rightsizing Fargate/node groups, RDS instance class, savings plans, S3 lifecycle to cheaper storage tiers and cache-driven database load reduction, with actual dollar deltas.
tasks.deliverable: Tested backup/restore and DR runbook with measured RTO/RPO, blue/green and rollback rehearsal notes, a chaos-experiment log with observed behaviour, and a FinOps report with cost-per-request and three applied optimizations showing dollar savings.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Objective: turn every Phase 1-4 artifact into interview performance for the Full Stack Engineer loop at Stripe. The candidate's strongest asset is genuine end-to-end shipping experience across React, TypeScript, Node and Postgres - this phase makes that evidence legible, closes the remaining vocabulary gaps (Kubernetes, AWS, security compliance), and rehearses the rounds under time pressure.

tasks.title: Timed System Design and Architecture Drills
tasks.description: Convert the Phase 4 design docs into verbal fluency under a clock. Run at least six 35-45 minute mock prompts - a payment/ledger service with idempotency and exactly-once processing, a rate-limited public API, a multi-tenant SaaS backend, a notification/feed fan-out system, an analytics ingestion pipeline, and a URL shortener for warm-up - twice each on video, using a whiteboard to clarify requirements, estimate scale, draw boxes and arrows, choose data models and indexes, place caches and queues, name the bottleneck and state the failure mode. Record and review, then write the answers you would give to the three hardest follow-ups per prompt. Focus deliberate repetition on the gaps the candidate is weakest in: consistency tradeoffs, backpressure and multi-region failover.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design drill packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, decisions, follow-up answers), two recorded mock sessions, and a reviewed list of recurring weak points with targeted notes.

tasks.title: Coding Interview Drills in the Candidate's Real Stack
tasks.description: Practise the live-coding round in the technologies the role actually uses. Do timed drills in a containerized repo: add a tested Express endpoint backed by Postgres with validation and pagination; implement a React component with loading/error states, a custom hook and a test; solve a set of TypeScript/algorithm problems under a 30-minute timer while narrating; refactor a deliberately messy function into clean typed code with the reviewer's constraints. Practise reading and extending an unfamiliar codebase in under ten minutes, writing a failing test before the fix, and explaining complexity and tradeoffs out loud. Run at least two pairing sessions with a peer or recorded self-review.
tasks.deliverable: A drill log of 10+ timed problems with times and mistakes noted, a repository of completed live-coding exercises with tests, two recorded mock coding rounds with reviewed feedback, and a personal checklist for the first five minutes of any coding round.

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Case Study Writeup and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate everything into one inspectable public artifact. Assemble the monorepo - React/TypeScript app, Express API, FastAPI service, Terraform, Helm chart, Kubernetes manifests, CI/CD workflows, tests, threat model, load-test reports and runbooks - and write a README that reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack and rationale, `docker compose up` quickstart, EKS deployment guide, observability screenshots, measured latency/throughput numbers, security controls, cost notes and the rollback runbook. Add short `docs/` writeups for the three hardest decisions (multi-stage builds, canary delivery, tenant isolation) and then write RESUME.md mapping each feature to a resume bullet, rewriting the current 'scalable components and microservices with high test coverage' line into quantified, verified claims.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub monorepo with architecture diagram, containerized quickstart, EKS deploy and rollback guides, dashboards, benchmarks and security evidence; `docs/` decision records; and a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping with rewritten resume lines for the Full Stack Engineer target.

tasks.title: Kubernetes, AWS and Security Knowledge Consolidation
tasks.description: Turn practical experience into interview-grade fluency. Build one-page cheat sheets for the services and objects actually used - Pod/Deployment/Service/Ingress/ConfigMap/Secret/PDB/HPA/NetworkPolicy/RBAC on the Kubernetes side, and IAM, VPC, EKS, ECR, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SQS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch and KMS on the AWS side - each paired with the artifact the candidate built and the failure mode they debugged. Work through the CKAD/CKA and SAA-C03 objective domains, sit at least three timed practice exams, and review every wrong answer back to a service-level explanation. Prepare crisp answers for the security-compliance questions a payments company asks: API key handling, PCI scope reduction, secret rotation, audit logging and least privilege.
tasks.deliverable: Cheat sheets for 15+ Kubernetes/AWS services each linked to a project artifact, three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log targeting 80%+, and a prepared answer bank for six security-compliance interview questions.

tasks.title: Full-Loop Mock Interviews and a Metrics-Backed STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the complete loop and make the narrative quantitative. Run mock rounds covering live coding, a TypeScript/React deep dive, an API/database design round, a Kubernetes/AWS infrastructure deep dive, a security scenario, and behavioural questions about conflict, ambiguity and failure. Build a STAR bank of 8+ stories drawn from real Phase 1-4 work with hard numbers - 'cut API p95 from 480ms to 140ms with cache-aside at 87% hit rate', 'moved the stack to EKS and took deploy time from 20 minutes to 6 with canary rollout', 'found and fixed a cross-tenant IDOR and proved it with an automated regression test', 'reduced monthly AWS spend 32% by rightsizing' - plus one story on a genuine production incident, its root cause and the preventive control added. Log every question asked and tighten the weakest answers.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded full-loop mock interviews with feedback, a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist covering React, TypeScript, Node, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, CI/CD, system design and security.

careerPlans.summary: A 12-week, evidence-first roadmap for an experienced full-stack developer (JavaScript/TypeScript, React, Node/Express, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, high test coverage) targeting Full Stack Engineer at Stripe, focused on five named gaps: Kubernetes, AWS, Security Compliance and Python as priority misses, and CI/CD and System Design as partial skills needing senior-level depth. Phase 1 raises the existing stack to production bar - strict TypeScript with a shared contract package, a layered OpenAPI-first Express API, a tested React data layer, a one-command containerized environment - and installs the first enforced CI gate. Phase 2 deep-dives the three non-cloud gaps: a real Kubernetes workload with Helm, RBAC, network policy and progressive rollouts; a typed FastAPI service sharing the same OpenAPI contract; and a security-compliance program that starts from a STRIDE threat model and ends with automated SAST/SCA/secret/DAST gates, tenant isolation via RLS and a PCI-DSS/SOC 2 control matrix. Phase 3 deploys that workload to AWS as code - modular Terraform VPC and IAM, EKS with ALB and IRSA, RDS Multi-AZ, ElastiCache, S3 and Secrets Manager - delivered keylessly through GitHub OIDC with canary promotion and automatic rollback. Phase 4 makes it survivable and measurable: OTel observability with SLOs, Redis as cache plus atomic rate limiter plus queue-backed async pipelines with an outbox and DLQ, k6 load testing with HPA/KEDA autoscaling and pool tuning, three defended system design documents, and tested DR, chaos and FinOps work. Phase 5 converts all of it into interview performance: timed design and coding drills, a case-study portfolio repository, Kubernetes/AWS/security cheat sheets tied to real artifacts, and a metrics-backed STAR bank. Every task names the specific gap it closes and produces an inspectable deliverable - no filler, and each phase consumes the artifacts of the one before it.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Turn the candidate's working JavaScript/TypeScript/React/Node/Express/PostgreSQL/Redis/Docker stack into a hardened, payments-grade reference service with an owned CI quality gate. Stripe assumes a Full Stack Engineer can already ship code that is reviewable, tested and defensible; this phase converts the flagged partial CI/CD gap and the Security Compliance gap into a working build-test-scan loop that every later phase (Kubernetes, AWS, distributed payments flows) deploys through. Deliverable-level outcome: one repository that any Stripe interviewer could clone and see lint, typecheck, tests, secret scanning and container image scans all passing on a pull request.

tasks.title: Threat-Model and Harden the Existing Express/Node API
tasks.description: Take the production Node/Express + React service the candidate already maintains and make it defensible under a payments-grade review. Write a STRIDE threat model for the request path (browser -> Express -> PostgreSQL/Redis), then close the gaps you find: strict TypeScript with no `any` in the request/response layer, zod schema validation on every router input, helmet security headers, CORS allow-list instead of `*`, per-route and per-IP rate limits backed by Redis, bcrypt/argon2 password hashing, parameterized queries with a lint rule banning string-built SQL, and a hard rule that no PAN, CVV or full auth token is ever logged (redacting pino serializer plus a unit test asserting it). Move every credential out of `.env` behind a sealed config module and remove them from git history.
tasks.deliverable: SECURITY.md containing the STRIDE threat model and control-to-code mapping, hardened Express router layer with zod validation and Redis-backed rate limiting, redacted structured logging with a test proving no sensitive field leaks, and `gitleaks` + `semgrep --config p/nodejs` passing clean on the repository.

tasks.title: Build the First Owned CI Quality Gate with GitHub Actions
tasks.description: The candidate has consumed pipelines; now they must own one. Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs on every pull request and blocks merge: install with lockfile-frozen commands, run ESLint + `tsc --noEmit`, spin up PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7 as service containers, run unit and integration tests with a coverage threshold (fail under 80% on changed lines), and upload the coverage report plus JUnit results as artifacts. Add a Node 20/22 matrix, dependency and pnpm store caching keyed on the lockfile, `concurrency` cancellation for superseded runs, and a separate `changes` job so docs-only PRs skip the heavy matrix. Protect `main` with required status checks and linear history.
tasks.deliverable: Committed `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with a job matrix, service-container Postgres/Redis, coverage gate and artifacts, reproducible locally via `pnpm ci:local` (act or docker compose), plus branch-protection settings captured as code in the README.

tasks.title: Add Application Security Testing to the Pipeline (SAST, DAST, Dependency Audit)
tasks.description: Extend the CI gate with automated security testing and make the PCI DSS scope explicit. Add a Semgrep job (custom rules for secrets, unsafe SQL and disabled TLS verification), GitHub CodeQL with the `security-extended` query suite, `pnpm audit`/`osv-scanner` failing on high severity with a documented exception file, and an OWASP ZAP baseline scan against the API booted with compose in the same workflow. Modify the payments path so raw card data never reaches the service: card fields are tokenized by the provider and the service stores only the token plus last-4, then draw the cardholder-data-environment (CDE) boundary diagram and map each of the 12 PCI DSS requirements to the control that satisfies it, marking which are inherited from Stripe versus owned by the application.
tasks.deliverable: Security jobs in CI emitting SARIF to the GitHub Security tab, ZAP baseline report artifact, a `security/` folder with `pci-scope.md` (CDE boundary diagram + 12-requirement control matrix), and a tokenization change so no card data is persisted or logged.

tasks.title: Produce Signed, Scanned, Reproducible Container Images
tasks.description: Level up the candidate's existing Docker skills to supply-chain standards. Rewrite the API and web Dockerfiles as multi-stage builds (deps -> build -> runtime) on distroless or alpine base images, run as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem, and pin base images by digest. Add Trivy image scanning that fails on fixable HIGH/CRITICAL CVEs, generate a CycloneDX SBOM with syft, and sign the pushed image with cosign keyless signing. Tag images with the git SHA and a semver from semantic-release, and keep the whole flow reproducible from a clean clone.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened multi-stage Dockerfiles per service, a `release.yml` workflow that builds once, scans, generates an SBOM, signs with cosign and pushes immutable SHA+semver tags to a registry, plus a documented image-tagging policy.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: This is where the three Priority Gaps get closed head-on: Kubernetes, AWS and Python. The candidate already containerizes with Docker, so the goal is to move from 'it runs on my machine in compose' to 'it runs on a cluster and in a cloud account they provisioned themselves'. Python is treated as a first-class second language, not a tutorial detour: it is re-implemented against the same contracts the TypeScript service already exposes, so the candidate proves they can be productive in Stripe's polyglot codebase and in data/reconciliation tooling. Every task ends with an artifact deployed to a real, destroyable environment.

tasks.title: Deploy the Full Stack to a Local Kubernetes Cluster (kind)
tasks.description: Convert the compose topology into Kubernetes objects. Create a `k8s/` manifest set (or a Helm chart) with Deployments for web and API, ClusterIP Services, an Ingress, ConfigMaps for non-secret config, Secrets kept out of git, and dependency wiring to Postgres and Redis. Add readiness, liveness and startup probes tuned per service, resource requests/limits, a HorizontalPodAutoscaler on CPU plus a custom metric, rolling-update strategy with `maxSurge`/`maxUnavailable`, and a `make kind-up` target that creates the cluster and applies everything. Practice the operational loop deliberately: `kubectl rollout restart`, `kubectl describe pod` on a CrashLoopBackOff, `kubectl port-forward`, `kubectl top pods`, and reading events to debug a failing probe.
tasks.deliverable: A `k8s/` (or Helm chart) directory deploying web, API, Postgres and Redis to kind with probes, resources, HPA and Ingress, a one-command `make kind-up` bootstrap, and a `docs/kubectl-runbook.md` capturing the debugging sessions with real command output.

tasks.title: Run Stateful Workloads, Migrations and Network Isolation in Kubernetes
tasks.description: Move past stateless Deployments into the parts of Kubernetes that break in production. Replace the in-cluster database with a StatefulSet plus headless Service and PersistentVolumeClaims (or wire to an external managed instance and justify the choice), run PostgreSQL migrations as a Kubernetes Job gated on an initContainer waiting for the DB, and schedule the ledger reconciliation job as a CronJob with concurrency policy and backoff limits. Add NetworkPolicies so only the API can reach the database and only the web tier can reach the API, a PodDisruptionBudget per workload, a dedicated namespace per environment with ResourceQuota and LimitRange, and secrets sourced through External Secrets Operator from a real secret store rather than committed manifests. Verify by applying a policy and proving the blocked flow with `kubectl exec` + `nc`.
tasks.deliverable: StatefulSet or external-DB manifests, a migration Job, a reconciliation CronJob, NetworkPolicy set with a documented allow/deny test transcript, PDBs, namespace quotas, and External Secrets integration.

tasks.title: Provision an AWS Landing Zone with Terraform and Run the App on EKS
tasks.description: Own the cloud account end-to-end with infrastructure as code. Using Terraform modules, build a VPC across three AZs with public/private subnets, NAT gateways, route tables and security groups; an EKS cluster with a managed node group and IRSA roles scoped per service account so pods assume least-privilege IAM roles with no static keys; ECR for images; an ALB via the AWS Load Balancer Controller; RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ with automated backups and a parameter group; ElastiCache Redis with encryption in transit; S3 with versioning and block-public-access for exports; and CloudWatch log groups. Deploy the Phase 1 images to the cluster and expose the app through the ALB with TLS from ACM. Keep state in a remote S3 backend with DynamoDB locking, and add `terraform plan` output to the PR as a sticky comment. Tear down nightly to control cost and record the apply/destroy timing.
tasks.deliverable: A tagged, modular Terraform repository (network, eks, data, app modules) with remote state, a `terraform apply` that stands up the full environment, the Phase 1 application reachable over HTTPS on an ALB DNS name, and an `architecture.md` with a cost-annotated diagram.

tasks.title: Instrument the AWS Deployment: Observability, Alarms and Autoscaling
tasks.description: Make the deployed system explainable under load. Add OpenTelemetry tracing (ADOT) across the React client, Express API and Python service with correlated trace IDs, emit RED metrics (rate, errors, duration) plus queue and pool saturation, and build CloudWatch dashboards as code via Terraform. Define SLOs (e.g. p99 API latency < 300 ms, error rate < 0.1%, webhook delivery success > 99.9%) with error-budget alerts, wire alarms to an SNS topic with a real notification path, and configure cluster autoscaling: HPA on request rate and Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter with node-pool constraints. Prove it with a k6 load test that pushes the API past its capacity and captures the scale-out/scale-in curve.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-defined dashboards, SLOs and multi-condition CloudWatch alarms on an SNS topic, a k6 load-test script with a results report showing autoscaling kicking in, and an on-call runbook mapping each alarm to a diagnosis and first action.

tasks.title: Build and Deploy a Typed Python Service Against the Shared Contract
tasks.description: Close the Python gap by shipping something real rather than doing exercises. Build a FastAPI internal service - a ledger reconciliation and daily reporting API - that consumes the same OpenAPI contract and database as the TypeScript service. Use uv for dependencies and packaging, Pydantic v2 models generated from the shared schema, SQLAlchemy 2.0 with Alembic migrations, and pandas for the reconciliation report (match settled charges against ledger entries, surface unmatched items as CSV/S3 exports). Enforce quality with mypy `--strict`, Ruff, pytest with fixtures against a containerized Postgres, and 85% coverage; containerize with the same hardened multi-stage pattern and deploy it to the EKS cluster alongside the Node services. Practice idiomatic Python explicitly: type hints, dataclasses vs Pydantic, context managers, comprehensions, `asyncio` basics, and the GIL tradeoffs worth mentioning in an interview.
tasks.deliverable: A `services/reconciliation` FastAPI service (uv-managed, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2.0 + Alembic, pandas report writer) with mypy-strict-clean code, pytest suite at 85%+ coverage, hardened Dockerfile, and a Helm/manifest deployment running in the same EKS cluster with its own CI job.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Now that the app can run in Kubernetes on AWS, this phase makes delivery automatic and the money-moving paths correct under failure. The two partial skills are pushed to interview depth: CI/CD becomes a full OIDC-authenticated pipeline from pull request to progressive rollout with automated rollback, and System Design becomes hands-on work on the payment primitives Stripe interviews probe hardest - idempotency, transactional outbox, signed webhook delivery with retries, and dead-letter handling. Security Compliance continues in parallel by hardening data protection, audit logging and key management in the deployed environment.

tasks.title: Automate Pull-Request-to-Production Delivery with GitHub Actions and Terraform
tasks.description: Turn the manual deploy into one pipeline with environment promotion. Use GitHub OIDC to assume a deploy role in AWS (no long-lived access keys anywhere), then chain: build and scan images -> push to ECR with immutable tags -> `terraform plan` on PR (posted as a comment) -> `terraform apply` on merge to main for dev -> Helm upgrade of the new image digest -> automated smoke tests against the ALB -> promotion to staging and production behind GitHub Environments with required reviewers. Implement automatic rollback on failed smoke tests or errored canary (Helm `--atomic` plus Argo Rollouts), and make every deploy traceable by writing the commit SHA, image digest and actor into a release record. Add a `deploy` CLI/label to re-run a specific commit.
tasks.deliverable: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` with OIDC-based AWS auth, Terraform plan/apply stages, Helm deploys using image digests, smoke-test gate, environment approvals and automatic rollback, plus `docs/delivery.md` with the promotion path and the rollback runbook exercised at least once on a deliberately broken release.

tasks.title: Make the Payments API Idempotent and Exactly-Once on Money Movements
tasks.description: Implement the payment primitive interviewers use to separate senior from mid-level candidates. Add POST /charges (and /refunds) with an `Idempotency-Key` header: the key, a hash of the request body, and the stored response are persisted in PostgreSQL with a unique constraint, concurrent duplicates are blocked with an advisory lock or `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT`, and a conflicting body under the same key returns a 409 exactly as Stripe's API does. Store amounts as integer minor units (never floats), attach a state machine to each payment (requires_capture -> succeeded -> refunded) with legal-transition enforcement, and use the transactional outbox pattern - write the domain event in the same transaction as the state change, then relay it asynchronously - so a crash can never lose or double-emit an event. Prove correctness with failure-injection tests: kill the process between commit and publish, replay the same idempotency key 100x concurrently, and assert exactly one charge and one event.
tasks.deliverable: Idempotent charges/refunds endpoints with PostgreSQL-backed key store and conflict handling, integer-minor-unit money types, an enforced payment state machine, an outbox table plus relay worker, and a test suite (including concurrency and crash-injection cases) proving exactly-once semantics.

tasks.title: Build a Signed, Retrying, Dead-Letter-Backed Webhook System
tasks.description: Design and ship the outbound event fan-out Stripe is famous for. Merchants register endpoints with a signing secret; every delivery is signed with an HMAC over timestamp + payload (Stripe-style `t=`/`v1=` header), includes a delivery ID for merchant-side dedupe, and is retried on non-2xx with exponential backoff and jitter over a documented schedule. Move delivery off the request path through SQS (or Kafka) with a worker pool, a per-endpoint circuit breaker so one slow merchant cannot stall the fleet, and a dead-letter queue after max attempts with a replay command. Add ordering guarantees per merchant, at-least-once semantics called out explicitly in the docs, webhook delivery metrics (attempts, success rate, p95 latency, DLQ depth) and a test endpoint/CLI so the whole loop is demonstrable. Also build the inbound side: verify an incoming signed webhook, reject replayed timestamps, and dedupe by event ID.
tasks.deliverable: Webhook dispatcher service with HMAC signing, registered endpoints and secrets, retry schedule with jitter, DLQ plus a `replay` CLI, a signature-verification middleware for inbound webhooks with replay protection, and an integration test suite that simulates slow, failing and duplicate-receiving merchants.

tasks.title: Prove Resilience in Kubernetes Under Failure and Load
tasks.description: Break the system on purpose and document what happens. Run a k6 or Artillery scenario at 2-5x expected peak against the EKS deployment and capture HPA scale-out, node provisioning latency and p50/p95/p99 latency plus error rate. Then run a planned failure drill set: kill a pod mid-charge and verify no lost or duplicated payment, drain a node and confirm PDBs keep the service available, delete the Redis pod and verify graceful degradation or failover, simulate an AZ outage by cordoning one zone's nodes, and exhaust the database connection pool to observe and then fix the saturation behaviour (PgBouncer or pool tuning). Add pod-level chaos via Chaos Mesh or `kubectl` scripts, and confirm the alerts from Phase 2 actually fire during each drill.
tasks.deliverable: A `chaos/` directory of reproducible drill scripts, a load-test report with capacity numbers and the scaling curve, a failure-drill log recording symptom -> alert -> diagnosis -> fix for each scenario, and the code/config changes made in response (pool limits, timeouts, retry budgets, PDB tuning).

tasks.title: Harden Data Protection, Key Management and Audit Logging in Production
tasks.description: Apply compliance thinking to the live environment rather than to a document. Encrypt everything at rest with KMS customer-managed keys (RDS, EBS, S3, ElastiCache) and enforce TLS in transit inside the cluster and to every dependency; enable automatic secret rotation for database credentials and provider keys through Secrets Manager plus External Secrets, and prove rotation works without downtime. Build an append-only audit log service that records who did what to which payment object (actor, action, resource, before/after, request ID), ships to S3 with Object Lock and CloudTrail for control-plane events, and is queryable for an incident review. Then write an incident-response runbook (detect, contain, eradicate, recover, post-mortem) and map every implemented control to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and the relevant PCI DSS requirements in one traceable matrix.
tasks.deliverable: KMS-backed encryption at rest and TLS enforcement across all data stores, working zero-downtime secret rotation demo, an append-only audit-log service with Object Lock retention and a query interface, an incident-response runbook, and a control matrix mapping implemented controls to SOC 2 TSC and PCI DSS clauses.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: The final build phase scales the system to numbers a payments company actually cares about and pushes the candidate's System Design skill from 'can build it' to 'can defend the tradeoffs at a staff-level review'. The work is concentrated on the read/write paths of a ledger at tens of thousands of transactions per second, correctness of money under concurrency, multi-region disaster recovery with measured RTO/RPO, and platform-level GitOps and policy enforcement. Security Compliance closes out with audit evidence and adversarial validation, so the candidate can speak fluently about running regulated infrastructure, not just coding against it.

tasks.title: Scale the Read Path: Partitioning, Replicas and a Capacity Model
tasks.description: Take the ledger from thousands to tens of thousands of writes per second on paper and then partially in code. Write a capacity model (arrival rate, average and p99 latency, payload size, retention, replication factor, growth over 24 months) and derive storage, IOPS, connection and instance requirements. Then implement the read-scaling pieces: partition the transactions/events tables by month (declarative partitioning) with an archival/rollup job, add PostgreSQL read replicas with a read/write split in the data layer (and document the replication-lag tradeoff), put PgBouncer in transaction pooling mode with measured connection counts, and design the caching hierarchy (in-process LRU -> Redis -> Postgres) with explicit invalidation rules and a stampede guard. Benchmark each change with pgbench or a k6-backed read mix and record before/after numbers, including a soak test of at least one hour.
tasks.deliverable: A written capacity model with assumptions and a 24-month projection, partitioned tables plus archive/rollup job, read-replica routing in the data layer, PgBouncer deployed and tuned, a documented cache hierarchy with invalidation rules, and a benchmark report showing the throughput/latency improvement at each step.

tasks.title: Implement a Double-Entry Ledger with Reconciliation and Invariant Tests
tasks.description: Design money storage the way a payments company does. Replace the ad-hoc balance columns with an immutable, append-only double-entry ledger: every movement writes balanced debit/credit entries in a single transaction, balances are derived (with snapshots for performance), and a database-level constraint or trigger rejects any unbalanced journal. Handle distributed correctness with sagas: an authorize -> capture -> transfer flow across the ledger and the provider, with compensating actions for each failure point, and an idempotent reconciliation job that compares provider settlement files against ledger entries and produces an exceptions queue. Write invariant tests that assert debits equal credits globally and per journal, that no balance can go negative where the product forbids it, that replayed events are no-ops, and that a randomized saga fuzz run never loses or creates value. Document the consistency tradeoffs (strong consistency on writes vs eventual consistency on reporting) you chose and why.
tasks.deliverable: Append-only double-entry ledger schema with balance-derivation queries and an imbalance-rejecting constraint, saga orchestration for authorize/capture/transfer with compensations, an idempotent reconciliation job with an exceptions queue and CSV/S3 report, and a test suite (including a randomized saga fuzz test) proving the money invariants hold.

tasks.title: Design and Drill Multi-Region Disaster Recovery on AWS
tasks.description: Define and then actually test recovery. Specify RTO and RPO targets per system from business impact, then implement the matching architecture in Terraform: a warm-standby or pilot-light second region with cross-region RDS read replica (and a documented promotion procedure), S3 cross-region replication, ECR image replication, Route 53 health checks with failover routing, and the same EKS stack stood up from the same modules. Automate the failover drill with a script, run it during business-like load, and measure actual RTO/RPO against target - then write the post-drill findings and fix what missed. In parallel, run a cost review: right-size node pools and databases from real utilization, add Savings Plans or reserved capacity where justified, set S3 lifecycle rules, and produce a tagged cost-allocation dashboard; the goal is a documented reduction in monthly run-rate without hurting the SLOs from Phase 2.
tasks.deliverable: Documented RTO/RPO targets per system, second-region infrastructure as Terraform modules with replication and Route 53 failover, an automated failover drill script plus a report comparing measured versus target RTO/RPO, and a cost report with right-sizing/Savings Plan decisions and a before/after monthly run-rate on a tagged dashboard.

tasks.title: Run the Platform as a GitOps Product with Progressive Delivery and Policy as Code
tasks.description: Move the cluster from imperative `kubectl apply` deploys to a declarative platform. Stand up Argo CD pointing at an environment repository so cluster state is reconciled from git (drift detection plus self-heal), split dev/staging/prod with Kustomize overlays or Helm value files, and replace the plain rollout with Argo Rollouts canary or blue-green using analysis templates that query Prometheus SLIs and abort automatically on error-rate or latency regression. Add policy enforcement with Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper: require resource limits, disallow `latest` tags and privileged containers, require non-root and read-only filesystems, and block workloads missing an owner label. Enforce least privilege with per-namespace service accounts and audit RBAC bindings, and demonstrate the whole loop by shipping a canary release that auto-promotes on green metrics and auto-rolls-back when a deliberately injected error metric fires.
tasks.deliverable: A GitOps environment repository reconciled by Argo CD with per-environment overlays and drift self-heal, an Argo Rollouts canary/blue-green strategy with Prometheus analysis and automated rollback demonstrated once, a Kyverno/Gatekeeper policy set with a test suite of compliant and non-compliant manifests, and an RBAC/service-account audit.

tasks.title: Close the Compliance Loop: Evidence, Pen-Test Remediation and a Game Day
tasks.description: Prove the system is auditable and adversarially tested, which is what a regulated employer will ask for. Assemble an audit-evidence pack for the controls implemented across Phases 1-4: architecture and data-flow diagrams, the PCI DSS and SOC 2 control matrices with named owners and evidence links, encryption and key-rotation records, vulnerability-management SLAs (how fast CRITICAL/HIGH are triaged and fixed, with the SBOM and scan history as proof), access-review records and change-management history from the GitOps repo. Run an external-style penetration test on a staging environment (a paid assessment or a structured OWASP WSTG checklist pass with Burp/ZAP), triage and remediate every finding, and re-test. Finish with an incident-response game day: a tabletop plus a live drill injecting a simulated credential leak or card-data exposure, exercising detection, containment, customer/regulator notification decisions and the post-mortem template.
tasks.deliverable: An audit-evidence pack (diagrams, control matrices with owners and evidence, encryption/rotation records, vulnerability SLAs, access reviews, change history), a penetration-test report with all HIGH/CRITICAL findings remediated and re-tested, and a game-day report with the post-mortem, timeline and follow-up action list.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Everything built in Phases 1-4 becomes interview material here. The candidate converts an artefact-rich body of work into repeatable, high-signal narratives: system-design rounds on payments problems, coding rounds in both TypeScript and Python, deep-dives on the Kubernetes and AWS decisions they actually made, and behavioural stories anchored in real incidents and tradeoffs. The phase ends with an honest final gap scorecard and a portfolio that makes the work inspectable in a take-home or design round.

tasks.title: Run Payments System-Design Mock Rounds and Write the Design Docs
tasks.description: Turn the built system into rehearsal-ready design documents and practice delivering them out loud under time pressure. Write four 2-3 page design docs in the style of a Stripe design review - (1) a payment intents API with idempotency, (2) a webhook delivery system at 1M events/day, (3) a double-entry ledger with reconciliation, (4) a read-heavy reporting API - each covering requirements, capacity estimates, data model, API surface, failure modes, and rejected alternatives with reasons. Then run at least three timed mock interviews (peers, Pramp/Interviewing.io or recorded solo) where you whiteboard for 35 minutes, and capture where you lost structure. Drill the recurring questions: how you would shard the ledger, why you chose the outbox over 2PC, how you'd migrate a hot table with zero downtime, and how you'd diagnose a p99 latency regression in production. Re-answer each weak point until the tradeoff explanation is crisp in under two minutes.
tasks.deliverable: Four committed design documents in `docs/design/` with capacity estimates, failure modes and rejected alternatives, plus a mock-interview log with recordings or notes, scored rubrics per round and a written list of corrected weak points.

tasks.title: Reach Interview Fluency in Python Alongside TypeScript
tasks.description: Make Python a language you can be interviewed in, not just build with. Work through 60 problems spanning arrays/strings, hash maps, two pointers, sliding window, trees/graphs (BFS/DFS), heaps, and dynamic programming - solved in Python with the same set re-solved in TypeScript so you can switch on request - and log time and pattern per problem to find weak spots. Add the Python-specific depth interviewers probe: when a list vs tuple vs set wins, generators and laziness for streaming a large settlement file, `asyncio` versus threads for I/O-bound webhook fan-out, the GIL and when multiprocessing matters, decorators/context managers, and packaging with uv plus dependency pinning. Practice reading and extending the FastAPI reconciliation service from Phase 2 live, since interviewers test navigating unfamiliar code, and keep a one-page Python cheat sheet of idioms and standard-library modules you actually used.
tasks.deliverable: A `interview-prep/` repository with 60 problems solved in both Python and TypeScript (solution, complexity, pattern, timing log), a written comparison of Python concurrency options exercised in your own service, and a one-page Python idiom cheat sheet derived from real code written in this plan.

tasks.title: Rehearse Kubernetes and AWS Deep-Dives from Your Own Systems
tasks.description: Prepare to defend the infrastructure decisions instead of reciting documentation. Build a 'walk me through what you built' deck covering the EKS architecture (VPC layout, IRSA, node pools, ingress/TLS), how rolling and canary deployments work and what you saw fail during the drills, the resource-request and HPA tuning reasoning behind your capacity numbers, NetworkPolicy and secret-management choices, and the cost/RTO tradeoffs from Phase 4. Then rehearse live troubleshooting: in a fresh cluster, break something realistic (bad image tag, missing ConfigMap, probe misconfiguration, exhausted node memory) and narrate the diagnosis from `kubectl get events`/`describe`/`logs` to fix within ten minutes. Prepare crisp answers for the classic probes: requests vs limits, ConfigMap vs Secret vs External Secret, StatefulSet vs Deployment, what happens on node drain, and how to safely run a database migration during a deploy.
tasks.deliverable: An architecture walkthrough deck (or recorded screen-share) drawn entirely from the candidate's own cluster and Terraform, a done-for-you troubleshooting playbook with five narrated break/fix scenarios and their real transcripts, and a written Q&A sheet of the twelve most likely Kubernetes/AWS interview probes with answers grounded in the built system.

tasks.title: Own the Compliance and Payments-Domain Story
tasks.description: Be the candidate who can talk about risk, money and regulation without hand-waving. Build a payments-domain glossary and concept map tied to the system built in this plan: authorization/capture/void/refund, partial refunds and disputes/chargebacks, 3-D Secure and SCA, interchange and network fees, settlement and payout timing, PCI DSS scope reduction via tokenization, idempotency and exactly-once in money movement, and reconciliation/exception handling. Then prepare behavioural and values-based stories anchored in real work from these phases using STAR: a security finding you triaged and fixed under SLA, a rollout you rolled back, a capacity problem you diagnosed, a disagreement about a design tradeoff and how it resolved, and a moment you pushed back on shipping risk. Refresh the security fundamentals that come up in interviews - OWASP Top 10 with concrete examples from your own code, symmetric vs asymmetric crypto, hashing versus encryption, HMAC signing, JWT pitfalls, and how secrets rotation works in your deployment.
tasks.deliverable: A payments-domain glossary and concept map cross-referenced to the built system, ten to fifteen written STAR stories each tied to a specific artefact from Phases 1-4, and a security-fundamentals Q&A sheet where every answer cites code, a config or an incident from this project.

tasks.title: Ship the Portfolio, Score the Gaps and Set the Next 90 Days
tasks.description: Make the ten weeks inspectable and close the loop on the original gap analysis. Consolidate everything into one public-facing repository: a top-level README with the architecture diagram, one-command local bootstrap (`make dev`), a services/skills map, links to the design docs, load-test and DR reports, and the security control matrices; a five-minute recorded walkthrough of the system running (request trace through the API, a canary release, a webhook retry, a chaos drill); and a portfolio page section that tells the story in Stripe-relevant terms. Then re-score every original gap - Kubernetes, AWS, Security Compliance, Python, CI/CD, System Design - with evidence from a specific artefact and a confidence 1-5, mark what remains partial, and write the next 90-day plan for the weakest one or two, including the reading or certification path (CKA, AWS Solutions Architect Associate) only if it genuinely helps. Do a final resume pass mapping each portfolio artefact to a bullet with measurable impact.
tasks.deliverable: A consolidated portfolio repository with architecture README, one-command bootstrap, linked design/security/test reports and a recorded system walkthrough; a gap scorecard re-scoring all six flagged skills with evidence links and confidence ratings; a written next-90-days plan for the remaining weak areas; and a revised resume section with metric-backed bullets mapped to specific artefacts.

careerPlans.summary: A custom 5-phase, roughly 10-week preparation plan for a Full Stack Engineer role at Stripe, built strictly from this candidate's gap analysis rather than a generic curriculum. The candidate already has a strong, shipping full-stack foundation (JavaScript, TypeScript, React, HTML5/CSS3, Node.js, Express, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker) plus current experience building scalable, well-tested components and microservices at a San Francisco technology firm, so nothing in this plan is remedial: each task converts an existing strength into a payments-grade artefact while systematically closing the three Priority Gaps (Kubernetes, AWS, Security Compliance) and the two partial skills (CI/CD, System Design). Phase 1 hardens the existing Node/Express/React service with a threat model, an owned GitHub Actions quality and security gate, and signed, scanned container images. Phase 2 deep-dives Kubernetes (kind to EKS with StatefulSets, migrations, NetworkPolicies), AWS (a Terraform-provisioned three-AZ EKS landing zone with RDS and ElastiCache and real observability) and Python (a typed FastAPI reconciliation service deployed next to the TypeScript services). Phase 3 automates delivery with OIDC-authenticated pipelines and proves distributed correctness through idempotent charges, a transactional outbox, signed retrying webhooks with dead-letter handling, chaos drills and production key management and audit logging. Phase 4 scales the ledger to tens of thousands of transactions per second with partitioning, read replicas, caching, a double-entry ledger with reconciliation and invariant tests, multi-region DR with measured RTO/RPO, GitOps with progressive delivery and policy as code, and an audit-evidence pack with a penetration test and game day. Phase 5 converts all of it into interview evidence: payments system-design round documents, Python and TypeScript interview fluency, Kubernetes/AWS deep-dive rehearsals, compliance and payments-domain storytelling, and a consolidated portfolio with an evidence-backed gap scorecard and a next-90-days plan. Every task names a concrete deliverable, so progress is inspectable rather than self-reported.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Lock in the full-stack baseline the Docker and AWS work will be built on: get one real app running reproducibly on a machine, wired with tests, linting, and CI so every later phase has a stable artifact to containerize and deploy. Docker fundamentals start here as the first missing skill.

tasks.title: Stand up a repeatable local full-stack app
tasks.description: Build or adopt a non-trivial full-stack app (React/Next.js frontend + Node/Express or FastAPI backend + PostgreSQL) with real auth and CRUD, so it has multiple services worth containerizing. Document exact install/run steps and required environment variables in the repo README.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub repository with frontend + backend + database, a README quickstart, and a .env.example listing every required variable

tasks.title: Write the first production-grade Dockerfile for the backend
tasks.description: Containerize the backend with a multi-stage build (builder + runtime), pin the base image to an exact Node/Python version, install dependencies from a lockfile, run as a non-root user, and add a HEALTHCHECK plus a .dockerignore. Compare image size against a naive single-stage build.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile with build/runtime stages, non-root user, HEALTHCHECK, .dockerignore, and a before/after image size note in the README

tasks.title: Run the stack with docker-compose and wire environment parity
tasks.description: Author a docker-compose.yml that brings up frontend, backend, and Postgres together with healthchecks and depends_on conditions, injects configuration via env_file, and persists database data in a named volume. Prove the whole stack comes up from a clean `docker compose up`.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml with three services, healthchecks, named volume, and a verified one-command cold start documented in the README

tasks.title: Add automated lint and test gates for the repo
tasks.description: Add ESLint/Prettier, unit tests for core API endpoints, and a pre-commit hook. Make the backend tests runnable inside the Docker image so the same command works locally and in CI.
tasks.deliverable: Lint + unit test setup with a pre-commit hook and a `docker run` command that executes the backend test suite green

tasks.title: Create a GitHub Actions CI pipeline that builds the Docker image
tasks.description: Write a GitHub Actions workflow that runs lint and tests on a pull request, builds the backend Docker image on push to main, and fails the build if the image cannot build. Use buildx layer caching to keep runs fast.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow file (.github/workflows/ci.yml) with lint, test matrix, and docker build jobs plus a green run link in the README

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Go deep on Docker as the first priority gap - multi-service orchestration, networking, image security, registries, and how containers behave beyond a single laptop. Everything here exists to make the app deployable to a cloud runtime in Phase 3.

tasks.title: Build a multi-service docker-compose with cache and message broker
tasks.description: Extend the compose stack with Redis for caching and a queue worker service (BullMQ/Celery) that shares the backend image but runs a different command. Configure service-to-service DNS names, restart policies, and resource limits.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml with five services (frontend, api, worker, postgres, redis), resource limits, and an async job demonstrated end to end

tasks.title: Master Docker networking, volumes, and troubleshooting
tasks.description: Produce and verify a network/volume topology for the compose stack: custom bridge network, published vs internal-only ports, bind mount for local development versus named volume for data. Deliberately break the stack (wrong port, missing env, DNS typo) and record how each failure is diagnosed with docker logs, inspect, and exec.
tasks.deliverable: Network and volume topology diagram plus a troubleshooting playbook of five reproducible failures with their fix and diagnostic command

tasks.title: Harden the container image and scan it for vulnerabilities
tasks.description: Reduce the runtime image to a minimal base (distroless or alpine-slim), remove build tooling from the final stage, add a read-only root filesystem and dropped capabilities, and scan the image with Trivy. Fix or explicitly accept every HIGH/CRITICAL finding.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened Dockerfile, Trivy scan report, and a short security notes file listing accepted risks and their justification

tasks.title: Publish images to Amazon ECR from CI with a real tagging strategy
tasks.description: Create a private ECR repository, authenticate via OIDC in GitHub Actions (no long-lived keys), and push images tagged with both the git SHA and a semantic version. Add a lifecycle policy to expire untagged images.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions release workflow pushing SHA and semver tags to ECR, IAM OIDC role definition, and an ECR lifecycle policy

tasks.title: Write a Docker interview drill: 40 questions answered from experience
tasks.description: Work through the questions that actually get asked (build cache layering, COPY vs ADD, CMD vs ENTRYPOINT, image vs container, layer caching in CI, compose vs swarm vs k8s, volume drivers) and answer each one using your own project as the example, not a definition.
tasks.deliverable: Docker question bank with 40 answers, each anchored to a concrete decision made in your own project

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the containerized stack to real AWS infrastructure. Work from identity and network foundations upward to a running HTTPS application with managed database, object storage, and CDN.

tasks.title: Set up AWS account guardrails and least-privilege IAM
tasks.description: Enable MFA on the root account, create a deploy user/role for CI and a separate read-only role for diagnostics, and write narrowly scoped policies for ECR, ECS, S3, CloudWatch, and Secrets Manager. Enable CloudTrail in a dedicated logging bucket.
tasks.deliverable: IAM policy JSON files (deploy role, read-only role), MFA-enabled root, and CloudTrail logging verified with one captured audit event

tasks.title: Build the VPC and network layer as infrastructure as code
tasks.description: Define a VPC across two availability zones using Terraform or CDK: public subnets for load balancing, private subnets for compute and data, an internet gateway, NAT gateway, and security groups that allow only the ports the app needs. Never hand-click this - the same code must create the stack again.
tasks.deliverable: IaC VPC module (subnets, IGW, NAT, route tables, security groups) that provisions the network cleanly after a destroy

tasks.title: Deploy the backend to ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer
tasks.description: Create an ECS cluster, task definition, and service running the ECR image in private subnets, fronted by an ALB with health-check routing and a target group. Wire application logs to CloudWatch and confirm a rolling deployment replaces tasks without downtime.
tasks.deliverable: ECS Fargate service definition, ALB with target group and health check, and a live URL serving the backend API

tasks.title: Add managed PostgreSQL and keep secrets out of the image
tasks.description: Provision RDS PostgreSQL in private subnets reachable only from the app security group, run migrations against it, and move all credentials into Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store injected into the ECS task. Prove no secret exists in the image or the repo.
tasks.deliverable: RDS instance with restricted security group, migration output, and ECS task definition referencing Secrets Manager instead of plaintext environment variables

tasks.title: Host the frontend on S3 + CloudFront with HTTPS
tasks.description: Build the frontend, publish it to a private S3 bucket served through CloudFront with Origin Access Control, request an ACM certificate for a custom domain, and add a deploy script that invalidates the cache on release.
tasks.deliverable: CloudFront distribution serving the built frontend over HTTPS on a custom domain, with a cache-invalidating deploy script

tasks.title: Codify the whole environment in one reproducible stack
tasks.description: Refactor the VPC, ECS, ALB, RDS, S3, and CloudFront resources into a single parameterized IaC stack with separate dev and prod variable files, then destroy and re-apply it to prove reproducibility.
tasks.deliverable: One IaC stack applied to a second environment from variables alone, with a recorded destroy-and-recreate run

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Turn the deployed app into a production-grade system: fully automated delivery with rollback, observability and alerting, autoscaling under real load, database scaling, and a defensible cost and security posture.

tasks.title: Automate the full CI/CD path from commit to ECS rollout
tasks.description: Chain the pipeline end to end: lint and test, build and push the image to ECR, render the new task definition, deploy to ECS, and wait for service stability. Add automatic rollback on failed health checks and a manual approval gate for production.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions deploy workflow with ECS rollout, health-check wait, automatic rollback, and a rollback runbook

tasks.title: Instrument the app and build CloudWatch dashboards and alarms
tasks.description: Emit structured JSON logs with request IDs, add a /health and /metrics endpoint, and create CloudWatch dashboards plus alarms for 5xx rate, p95 latency, ALB unhealthy hosts, ECS CPU/memory, and RDS connections. Route alarms to a notification target.
tasks.deliverable: Structured logging in the API, a CloudWatch dashboard JSON, and alarm definitions with a notification channel wired up

tasks.title: Load test the service and configure autoscaling on real signals
tasks.description: Write a k6 or Artillery script that ramps to realistic concurrency, run it against the ALB, and capture latency and error curves. Set ECS service autoscaling on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target, then re-run the test to show tasks scaling out and back in.
tasks.deliverable: Load test script, before/after performance report, and ECS autoscaling policies with evidence of scale-out under load

tasks.title: Scale the data layer safely with zero-downtime migrations
tasks.description: Enable RDS Multi-AZ, add a read replica for reporting queries, and place RDS Proxy or a connection pooler in front of the app so task scaling does not exhaust connections. Script a backward-compatible migration and prove the app stays up while it runs.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-AZ RDS with a read replica, connection pooling in the task definition, and a zero-downtime migration script with a runbook

tasks.title: Harden the production edge and document the architecture
tasks.description: Attach AWS WAF managed rules to CloudFront or the ALB, enforce HTTPS-only and security headers, verify S3 buckets block public access, and re-review IAM for unused permissions. Capture the whole system as a labeled architecture diagram covering request path, data stores, and deploy pipeline.
tasks.deliverable: WAF and HTTPS configuration, security-header check output, and a one-page architecture diagram with the request and deployment paths annotated

tasks.title: Produce a running cost and reliability review
