tasks.description: Use the AWS pricing calculator and Cost Explorer to estimate monthly cost, identify the three largest line items, and propose one concrete optimization (e.g. Fargate Spot, S3 lifecycle, right-sized tasks). State the single points of failure and what happens if each AZ fails.
tasks.deliverable: Cost estimate with the top three drivers and one applied optimization, plus a failure-mode table listing each single point of failure and its mitigation

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the Docker and AWS work into interview evidence. Rehearse the system designs, questions, and stories that come up for Full Stack Engineer roles, using your own deployed project as the reference architecture.

tasks.title: Rehearse container and AWS system design under time pressure
tasks.description: Practice three timed whiteboard designs - a URL shortener, a multi-tenant SaaS API, and a file upload/processing pipeline - and for each one explain the container topology, compute choice, data stores, scaling strategy, and deployment path on AWS. Timebox to 45 minutes each and record the gaps.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design documents with diagrams and a gap log of concepts you could not explain fluently

tasks.title: Drill the AWS question set that Full Stack interviews actually ask
tasks.description: Answer 40 AWS interview questions grounded in your deployed stack: VPC and subnet design, security groups vs NACLs, IAM roles vs users, ECS vs Lambda vs EC2, ALB vs NLB, RDS Multi-AZ vs read replicas, and S3 storage classes. Also be able to explain how Docker images reach and run on ECS.
tasks.deliverable: AWS question bank with 40 answers, each referencing the specific resource you built and why you chose it

tasks.title: Write STAR stories from the Docker and AWS migration work
tasks.description: Draft six STAR stories drawn from this roadmap: reducing image size, debugging a broken compose network, adding CI/CD with rollback, handling a load-test bottleneck, tightening IAM permissions, and a cost optimization. Each story needs a measurable result.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with six stories, each with a quantified outcome and a 90-second spoken version

tasks.title: Publish a portfolio repo that proves the skills end to end
tasks.description: Create a public, well-documented repository containing the app, Dockerfiles, IaC, CI/CD workflows, architecture diagram, and a case-study README walking a reviewer through the deployment from commit to running service. Include the live demo URL.
tasks.deliverable: Public portfolio repository with architecture diagram, IaC, CI/CD workflows, case-study README, and a live demo link

tasks.title: Run mock interviews and close the remaining gaps
tasks.description: Do at least two full mock interviews (one system design, one technical plus behavioral) with a peer, mentor, or recorded self-review. Log every stumble, patch the underlying note, and re-answer the question until it is fluent.
tasks.deliverable: Mock interview feedback log with at least ten corrected answers and revised resume bullets quantified with Docker and AWS outcomes

careerPlans.summary: A 5-phase, roughly 11-16 week plan built specifically around this candidate's two priority gaps - Docker and AWS - for a Full Stack Engineer role. Phase 1 establishes a reproducible local full-stack app, its first multi-stage Dockerfile, a compose stack, and CI so there is a real artifact to work with. Phase 2 goes deep on Docker: multi-service orchestration, networking and volumes, image hardening with vulnerability scanning, and pushing images to Amazon ECR from CI. Phase 3 closes the AWS gap from the ground up - IAM least privilege, a two-AZ VPC as code, ECS Fargate behind an ALB, managed RDS with secrets out of the image, and S3 plus CloudFront serving the frontend over HTTPS. Phase 4 makes it production-grade: end-to-end CI/CD with automatic rollback, CloudWatch dashboards and alarms, load testing with ECS autoscaling, Multi-AZ and read-replica database scaling, WAF and architecture documentation, and a cost and failure-mode review. Phase 5 converts all of it into interview evidence through system design rehearsals, an AWS question drill, STAR stories, a public portfolio repo, and mock interviews. Every task produces a concrete artifact - a Dockerfile, a compose stack, an IaC module, a workflow, a dashboard, or a report - so progress is inspectable rather than assumed.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Establish the one artifact every later phase depends on: a full-stack app (React + TypeScript frontend, Node/Express or FastAPI API, Postgres, Redis) that boots reproducibly and whose tests and quality checks run identically on a laptop, in a container and in CI. The two target gaps (Docker, AWS) are attacked here at their root - Docker is learned as the definition of the environment itself, not as an afterthought, so Phases 3-4 have a portable image to deploy.

tasks.title: Define the Whole Dev Environment in Docker, Not in a README
tasks.description: Build the reference full-stack app and make containers the only supported way to run it. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile for the frontend and one for the API (deps -> build -> runtime), then a docker-compose.yml that wires frontend, API, Postgres and Redis onto one named network with named volumes, .env-driven configuration and a Postgres healthcheck the API waits on. Add bind mounts plus the right dev command (nodemon/vite) for hot reload, and delete every 'works on my machine' prerequisite from the README.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile per service plus docker-compose.yml that boots the entire stack with `docker compose up` on a clean machine and gives a working UI -> API -> Postgres -> Redis round trip; README with the one-command quickstart and a container-network diagram (ports, network, volumes).

tasks.title: Container-Executed Quality Gate (lint, typecheck, format, tests)
tasks.description: Make code quality reproducible rather than machine-dependent. Configure ESLint + Prettier, TypeScript in strict mode, and a Husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook, then expose lint, typecheck, format and test as npm scripts that are invoked the same way everywhere - locally through `docker compose run --rm api pnpm <script>` and in CI inside the built image. Prove the gate is environment-independent by running it from a fresh container with no host Node install.
tasks.deliverable: Strict tsconfig, ESLint/Prettier/Husky configs and a script list that runs unchanged on host and in-container; screenshot/log of the full gate passing inside a clean container, plus a blocked non-conventional commit and a blocked lint error.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Test Suite with Testcontainers
tasks.description: Prove the app is testable in isolation the way a pipeline will test it. Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests for the API against a real Postgres and Redis spun up by Testcontainers (no pre-started database, no shared fixtures). Cover a happy path, a validation failure, an auth/permission denial and an idempotent-retry case for the core resource, and enforce a coverage threshold in the test config.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest/Jest + Supertest (or Pytest) suite with Testcontainers-managed Postgres and Redis, a single `test` script that needs no external services, 60%+ coverage on the API layer enforced by threshold, and a committed coverage report.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take Docker from 'it runs' to the production bar a Full Stack Engineer is expected to defend in review: images that are small, non-root and scanned; a multi-service topology that mirrors production; CI that builds images rather than just linting source; and the operational reflexes to debug a container instead of rebuilding it. This is the phase that converts Docker from a listed gap into a demonstrated capability.

tasks.title: Production Image Hardening and Supply-Chain Scanning
tasks.description: Rebuild both images for production: slim/alpine or distroless base on a pinned digest, a non-root user, only compiled artifacts copied into the runtime stage, a proper .dockerignore, OCI labels and multi-arch (amd64/arm64) builds. Order the Dockerfile so dependency layers are cached across code-only changes (lockfile copied before source). Scan with Trivy, generate an SBOM with Syft, remove any baked-in secrets, and measure the before/after with `docker image ls` and `dive`.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfile producing a runtime image under 300MB running as non-root on a pinned digest; .dockerignore; Trivy scan report at zero HIGH/CRITICAL; generated SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX); and a dev-vs-prod size and layer comparison table.

tasks.title: Multi-Service Orchestration with Dev/Prod Compose Overrides
tasks.description: Model a realistic distributed system locally: frontend, API, background worker, Postgres, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy. Use a base compose file plus dev and prod override files, custom networks that isolate the data tier from the public tier, healthcheck-based `depends_on`, per-service resource limits, restart policies and JSON-file log rotation. Seed the database and prove state survives a full `down`/`up` cycle.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml plus dev/prod override files orchestrating six services with tier network isolation, healthchecks, resource limits, restart policies and log rotation; a scripted volume-persistence test proving data survives `down`/`up`; and a service-topology diagram.

tasks.title: Image-Building CI with Layer Caching and a Registry
tasks.description: Make the pipeline build and publish the artifact, not just check the source. Add a GitHub Actions workflow that builds both images with docker/build-push-action and buildx, caches layers via cache-from/cache-to (gha or registry) so warm builds are fast, builds multi-arch, tags by commit SHA and `latest`, and pushes to GHCR on merge to main. Add a Trivy image-scan job that fails the build on HIGH/CRITICAL and a matrix job that runs the Phase 1 test suite inside the built image.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow building, scanning and pushing multi-arch images to GHCR with verified layer caching (cold vs warm build time), commit-SHA and latest tags, and a green PR pipeline plus a published image visible in the registry.

tasks.title: Container Debugging and Runtime Operations Runbook
tasks.description: Learn to operate containers, not just build them. Deliberately reproduce five incidents - crash loop from a bad entrypoint, OOM kill under a memory limit, port conflict, network DNS failure between services, and a volume permission error from running as non-root - and diagnose each with `docker logs`, `exec`, `stats`, `inspect`, `events` and `docker compose ps`. Handle SIGTERM for graceful shutdown and record before/after `docker stats` under applied CPU/memory limits.
tasks.deliverable: Container debugging runbook documenting five reproduced incidents (symptom, diagnostic command, root cause, fix), a SIGTERM graceful-shutdown demo, and a resource-limit before/after stats report showing the OOM diagnosis.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the Phase 2 containers onto managed infrastructure provisioned entirely as code. Everything is Terraform-first, least-privilege by default, and built in a real VPC with private subnets so that the networking concepts a Full Stack Engineer is questioned on (subnets, route tables, security groups, IAM) are things this candidate has actually built rather than read about.

tasks.title: AWS Foundation as Code: Least-Privilege IAM, Budgets, Remote State
tasks.description: Stand up a clean AWS account baseline. Create a non-root admin identity with MFA, a scoped deployment role used only by the pipeline, AWS CLI v2 profiles per environment, and a budget alarm with an SNS notification. Provision the foundation with Terraform in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking and state encryption. Write the least-privilege deployment policy explicitly (no wildcard actions on production resources) and document what each statement is for.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles/policies, a budget alarm and the S3 + DynamoDB remote-state backend; a documented least-privilege deployment policy; a screenshot of the active budget alarm and a `terraform state list` proving the backend is remote.

tasks.title: Deploy the Containers to ECS Fargate behind an ALB in Private Subnets
tasks.description: Push the hardened images to Amazon ECR and run them on ECS Fargate across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks. Define the VPC, public/private subnets, route tables, internet gateway and NAT gateway in Terraform; place tasks in private subnets with no public IP; expose only the ALB through a security group that the task security group accepts traffic from. Add CloudWatch log groups for the task logs and pass configuration through task-definition environment variables and secrets.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned VPC (2 AZs, public/private subnets, IGW, NAT, route tables), ECR repository, ECS Fargate service with desired count 2 behind an ALB with HTTP health checks; a publicly reachable URL serving the app plus a deployed-architecture diagram and a `curl` proof of the health endpoint.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Secrets and ElastiCache on AWS
tasks.description: Replace the local containers with managed services. Provision RDS Postgres in private subnets whose security group accepts traffic only from the ECS service security group, a versioned and encrypted S3 bucket for uploads with a least-privilege bucket policy and pre-signed URLs, Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store) entries for database credentials injected at task start, and an ElastiCache Redis cluster in the data subnet tier. Rewire the app's Redis client to ElastiCache and run the migrations against RDS. Security-group-to-security-group referencing is the core lesson here.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Postgres + versioned S3 + Secrets Manager/SSM + ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining; a migration run against RDS; proof of a pre-signed upload and retrieval; app screenshot showing a cache hit served from ElastiCache; and a note on which resources are deliberately not public.

tasks.title: Keyless CI/CD to AWS with OIDC, Rolling and Blue/Green Deploys
tasks.description: Automate delivery to AWS without storing static keys: configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role whose trust policy scopes the `sub` claim to this repository and branch, then extend the Phase 2 workflow to build and push to ECR, render a new ECS task definition with the new image tag, wait for service stability, and deploy. Progress from an ECS rolling deployment to a CodeDeploy blue/green deployment with an ALB test listener, add a manual approval gate (GitHub Environment) for production, and implement and test a rollback to the previous task revision.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-federated deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS rolling, then blue/green), IAM trust policy with a scoped subject, GitHub Environment approval gate, and logs proving both a successful zero-downtime deploy and a successful rollback to the prior revision.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives'. Observability, autoscaling under measured load, multi-environment infrastructure, cost control and disaster recovery are all exercised on the AWS stack built in Phase 3, while container concerns at scale (image supply chain, registry lifecycle, runtime failure modes) are closed out on the Docker side. By the end there is measured evidence of behaviour under load and failure, not just an opinion.

tasks.title: Observability: Structured Logs, Metrics, Alarms and Tracing
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end. Emit structured JSON logs carrying a request ID and trace ID, ship them to CloudWatch Logs with a defined retention, and publish custom latency and business metrics via the CloudWatch SDK or embedded metric format. Build a CloudWatch dashboard (request rate, p95 latency, 5xx rate, ECS CPU/memory, ALB target health) with alarms on error-rate and latency thresholds that notify SNS, and add AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry tracing across ALB -> API -> RDS/Redis so a slow request can be broken down by segment.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard with the five key panels, three or more CloudWatch alarms wired to SNS, one completed X-Ray/OTel trace showing the API-to-database segment, and a short note on the metric each alarm protects.

tasks.title: Autoscaling and Load Testing to a Defined SLO
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it with numbers. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target-tracking policies on CPU and on ALB request-count-per-target, set sensible min/max and cooldowns, then drive load with k6 (or Locust) against the deployed endpoint. Capture p95 latency, throughput and error rate before and after scale-out, define an explicit SLO, and add an RDS connection-pooling or bottleneck fix when the database becomes the limit - then re-run the test to show the improvement.
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies for CPU and request count with tuned min/max/cooldown, a k6 load-test script and report showing scale-out from 2 to N tasks, a stated SLO with pass/fail, and a bottleneck-analysis note with the applied fix and re-test result.

tasks.title: Multi-Environment Terraform, Cost Control and Disaster Recovery
tasks.description: Make the infrastructure repeatable and affordable. Parameterize Terraform into dev/staging/prod workspaces or var-files with environment-specific sizing (Fargate CPU/memory, RDS instance class, ElastiCache node type, desired counts), stand up a staging environment end to end from the same modules, and confirm the pipeline promotes the same image through it. Produce a Cost Explorer analysis with three applied optimizations and their dollar deltas, and write plus test an RTO/RPO backup-and-restore runbook covering RDS snapshots/PITR and S3 versioning.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-environment Terraform (dev/staging/prod) with a successfully deployed staging stack, a cost analysis with three applied optimizations and actual dollar deltas, and a DR runbook with a completed restore rehearsal and the measured recovery time.

tasks.title: Container Supply Chain and Runtime Failure Modes at Scale
tasks.description: Close the Docker gap at the operations end. Implement ECR image lifecycle policies and tag immutability, and make deployments reference immutable digests instead of floating tags. Set up scheduled rebuilding of base images so CVE fixes land without code changes, verify signature/provenance (cosign or ECR signing) and make the pipeline refuse unsigned images. Then reproduce and diagnose two production-shaped container failures on ECS - an image-pull failure from a missing/bad tag and a container exit from an unhealthy probe or an unhandled SIGTERM - using ECS events, CloudWatch logs and `docker inspect` locally.
tasks.deliverable: ECR lifecycle + tag-immutability policy, digest-pinned deployments, a scheduled base-image rebuild workflow, image signing enforced in the pipeline, and a failure-mode writeup covering the two reproduced ECS container incidents with the exact diagnostic path to root cause.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert Phases 1-4 into interview performance. Every artifact (compose stack, hardened images, Terraform, pipelines, dashboards, load-test numbers, DR runbook) becomes a story, a diagram and a defensible decision, and the Docker and AWS knowledge is drilled to the point of being explainable under pressure at the depth a Full Stack Engineer loop probes.

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Architecture Writeup and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate the code, Dockerfiles, compose files, Terraform, CI/CD workflows, tests, SBOM/scan reports, dashboards and runbooks into one clean public repository with a README written as an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment and rollback guide, observability screenshots, load-test numbers and cost notes. Then write RESUME.md mapping each project feature to a resume bullet ('multi-stage images hardened to <300MB non-root; ECS Fargate across 2 AZs behind an ALB; OIDC keyless deploys with blue/green rollback').
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, container quickstart, AWS deploy + rollback guides, dashboard and load-test evidence, cost notes, a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping, and a rewritten resume section targeting Full Stack Engineer.

tasks.title: Docker and AWS Deep-Dive Question Bank with Written Answers
tasks.description: Prepare for the technical deep dive by writing out answers to the questions this stack invites - Docker: image vs container, layer caching and build context, multi-stage builds, COPY vs ADD, CMD vs ENTRYPOINT, why non-root, how networking and DNS work between compose services, volumes vs bind mounts, how to debug a crashing container, image slimming; AWS: IAM roles vs users vs policies, VPC and subnet design, security groups vs NACLs, ALB vs NLB, ECS Fargate vs EC2 vs Lambda, RDS in private subnets, secrets injection, blue/green vs rolling deploys, autoscaling policy choice, CloudWatch alarms and cost drivers. Answer each with the concrete artifact built in this plan rather than a definition.
tasks.deliverable: A question-and-answer bank of 30+ Docker and AWS questions, each answer citing a specific artifact from Phases 1-4 (e.g. 'non-root because our runtime image runs as uid 1001 and we hit a volume-permission error fixing it'), plus a list of the five questions still weakest and a plan to close them.

tasks.title: Timed Mock Interviews: Live Coding, Deep Dive and System Design
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop: a live coding round (add a tested endpoint to the running containerized app and rebuild the image), a Docker/AWS deep dive round, and a system design round where the candidate designs a URL shortener and a multi-tenant SaaS API, choosing data models, caching, queues, deployment topology on AWS, scaling limits and failure modes. Run at least two sessions recorded or with a peer, then review and log every recurring weak point with the corrected answer.
tasks.deliverable: Two recorded mock interview sessions (one live coding, one system design) with a written debrief, two completed system design packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, tradeoffs, failure modes), and a recurring-weak-point log with corrected answers.

tasks.title: AWS Fluency Consolidation and Final Readiness Checklist
tasks.description: Turn practical AWS experience into interview-grade fluency across the core domains - IAM, VPC/networking, ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, CloudWatch and cost models - by condensing each service into a one-page cheat sheet that pairs the service with the thing actually built with it and the tradeoff it represents. Sit at least three timed AWS practice exams (SAA-C03 style), review every wrong answer to a service-level explanation, and finish with a readiness checklist covering Docker, AWS, deployment and observability, plus a 60-second and 3-minute narrative for 'walk me through your architecture'.
tasks.deliverable: Cheat sheets for 10+ AWS services each linked to a project artifact, three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log targeting a consistent 80%+, and a final readiness checklist with a rehearsed 60-second and 3-minute architecture narrative.

careerPlans.summary: A 10-week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a candidate targeting Full Stack Engineer, built entirely around the two priority gaps identified for this role: Docker and AWS. It is sequenced so each phase feeds the next. Phase 1 makes containers the single definition of the environment and moves lint/typecheck/test execution inside them, so the artifact is portable from day one. Phase 2 takes Docker to a production bar: hardened non-root images under 300MB with SBOM and Trivy scanning, a six-service compose topology with tier isolation and dev/prod overrides, CI that builds and publishes multi-arch images with verified layer caching, and a container incident-debugging runbook. Phase 3 closes AWS by deploying those images as infrastructure-as-code - least-privilege IAM and remote state, a two-AZ VPC with private subnets, ECS Fargate behind an ALB, RDS/S3/Secrets Manager/ElastiCache with security-group chaining, and keyless OIDC-driven rolling and blue/green delivery with a tested rollback. Phase 4 adds production depth: CloudWatch and X-Ray observability with alarms, ECS autoscaling proven under k6 load against a stated SLO, multi-environment Terraform with cost optimization and a rehearsed disaster-recovery restore, and container supply-chain controls with digest pinning and signing. Phase 5 converts every artifact into interview performance through a documented portfolio repository, a 30+ question Docker/AWS answer bank, timed mock interviews and AWS exam-level fluency. No task is generic: each names the specific gap it closes and produces an inspectable deliverable with measurable evidence.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Build the daily loop a Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer at Datadog is assumed to own: a reproducible containerized environment, version-controlled infrastructure with linting and tests, and a first automated pipeline. Docker is the candidate's highest-priority missing skill, so it anchors this phase; CI/CD and system-level fundamentals are reinforced alongside it so every later phase deploys onto a working build-test-ship foundation.

tasks.title: Containerize a Multi-Service Reference Stack
tasks.description: Stand up a small reference app (Go or Node/Python API + Postgres + Redis) and define the whole stack in containers. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile per service (build stage -> minimal runtime stage), a docker-compose.yml wiring API, Postgres and Redis on one user-defined bridge network with named volumes, env-file config and healthchecks, plus a .dockerignore. Verify a cold `docker compose up` works from a clean machine and that Redis is reachable only from the API container.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile per service, docker-compose.yml with healthchecks and named volumes, .dockerignore, and a README with the one-command quickstart and a container-network diagram.

tasks.title: Make Infrastructure a First-Class Codebase (lint + validate + pre-commit)
tasks.description: Treat config as code: add shellcheck for scripts, hadolint for Dockerfiles, yamllint for YAML, and tflint/terraform validate for any IaC. Wire them into a pre-commit hook and identical `make lint` targets so the same quality gate runs locally, in the container build, and in CI. Enable Go/Node strict settings (gofmt/vet or eslint --max-warnings=0) for the API service.
tasks.deliverable: Committed .pre-commit-config.yaml, hadolint/yamllint/tflint configs, a Makefile with lint/format/test targets, and proof the hook blocks a deliberately malformed Dockerfile.

tasks.title: Automated Tests Against Real Containers
tasks.description: Prove the stack is testable in isolation the way a pipeline will test it. Add unit tests for API logic and integration tests that boot real Postgres and Redis via Testcontainers, covering a happy path, a validation failure, a cache hit vs miss, and an auth/permission case. Ensure `make test` needs no pre-started services and emits a coverage report.
tasks.deliverable: Testcontainers-backed integration suite with unit tests, a coverage report (>=60% on the API layer), and a `make test` target that provisions its own dependencies.

tasks.title: First CI Pipeline: Lint + Test Matrix + Image Build
tasks.description: Close the CI/CD gap with the smallest useful pipeline. A GitHub Actions workflow runs on every PR: dependency caching, the lint target, the test suite, and a Docker image build (no push). Add a version matrix, upload coverage as an artifact, and enable branch protection requiring the checks to pass before merge.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with cached lint/test matrix and an image-build job, branch protection enabled, and a screenshot or link to a green PR run.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take Docker, AWS and Redis from 'it runs' to production bar. Images become small, non-root and scanned; the stack gains a real AWS footprint (IAM, VPC, S3, a managed compute service); and Redis is understood as a cache, a queue and a distributed data store with eviction, persistence and clustering trade-offs. These are the three missing skills on the candidate's profile and the ones a Datadog interview panel will probe hardest.

tasks.title: Harden Production Images and Scan the Supply Chain
tasks.description: Rebuild images for production: distroless/slim bases pinned by digest, non-root user, only build artifacts in the runtime stage, OCI labels, layer ordering for cache reuse, and multi-arch (amd64/arm64) builds. Scan with Trivy, generate an SBOM with Syft, remove any baked-in secrets, and measure before/after size and layer count with `docker history` and dive.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened Dockerfile producing a non-root runtime image under 300MB on a pinned digest, generated SBOM, Trivy scan report, and a dev-vs-prod size/layer comparison.

tasks.title: Provision a Real AWS Landing Zone with Terraform
tasks.description: Stand up the AWS foundation the missing AWS skill demands: a Terraform module creating a VPC with public/private subnets, route tables, NAT, security groups, an S3 bucket with versioning and encryption, and least-privilege IAM roles/policies. Use remote state in S3 with DynamoDB locking, tag everything, and keep variables per environment. Destroy and recreate the stack to prove it is fully reproducible.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable Terraform module + dev/prod tfvars creating VPC, subnets, NAT, S3 and scoped IAM roles, remote state config, and `terraform plan` output plus a clean destroy/recreate log.

tasks.title: Deploy the Container on Managed AWS Compute
tasks.description: Run the Phase 1 app on AWS: push images to ECR, then deploy via ECS Fargate (or EKS with a managed node group) behind an Application Load Balancer, with task-level IAM roles, Secrets Manager for credentials, CloudWatch logs/metrics, and target-tracking autoscaling on CPU and request count. Capture a rolling deployment and a manual rollback.
tasks.deliverable: ECS/EKS service definition running the API + Redis (ElastiCache) behind an ALB, ECR repo with a immutable-tagged image, autoscaling policy, CloudWatch dashboard, and a recorded rollback of a bad release.

tasks.title: Redis Deep Dive: Cache, Queue and Eviction Behavior
tasks.description: Move past 'it stores keys'. Implement cache-aside with TTLs and stampede protection, a rate limiter with atomic Lua or INCR/EXPIRE, a pub/sub or Streams-based job queue, and a leaderboard using sorted sets. Measure hit ratio with INFO stats, deliberately trigger maxmemory-policy eviction (allkeys-lru vs allkeys-lfu) and observe the difference, and compare RDB vs AOF persistence and durability implications.
tasks.deliverable: Documented Redis patterns (cache-aside, rate limiter, Streams queue, sorted-set leaderboard) in the app, a benchmark + INFO stats report showing hit ratio and eviction policy behavior, and a persistence trade-off write-up.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Turn the deployment from a manual exercise into a documented, automated, distributed system. Terraform and the delivery pipeline mature into environment-aware, repeatable releases; Redis runs as a clustered, replicated managed service; and continuous delivery adds migrations, smoke tests and rollback. This is the cloud-platform core of the target role.

tasks.title: Full Delivery Pipeline: Build -> Scan -> Deploy with Rollback
tasks.description: Extend Phase 1's workflow into real CD: build and tag images by commit SHA, scan with Trivy (fail on HIGH/CRITICAL), push to ECR, run `terraform plan` on PR and `terraform apply` on merge to main, deploy to ECS/EKS with OIDC-based AWS auth (no long-lived keys), then run post-deploy smoke tests against the ALB endpoint. Add automatic rollback to the previous task definition on failed smoke tests and group jobs to keep the pipeline fast.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage GitHub Actions pipeline with image scan gate, Terraform plan/apply, OIDC AWS auth, and post-deploy smoke tests that trigger automatic rollback; documented in a pipeline README with a time-to-deploy figure.

tasks.title: Redis in Production: Replication, Failover and Clustering
tasks.description: Run Redis the way a platform team must: ElastiCache (or self-managed) in cluster mode with replicas across availability zones, automatic failover, and encryption in transit/at rest. Handle MOVED/ASK redirects and multi-key operations across hash slots in the app, and validate failover behavior by failing over a replica and confirming the client reconnects. Set up a backup/snapshot plan and document recovery.
tasks.deliverable: Cluster-mode Redis with multi-AZ replicas and failover configured via Terraform, app code handling slot redirects, a failover test log showing reconnection, and a snapshot/restore runbook.

tasks.title: Observability Pipeline on the Datadog Model
tasks.description: Instrument the stack the way the target company's own product expects: structured JSON logs, RED/USE metrics for the API and Redis, distributed tracing across the ALB -> service -> Redis path, and a Datadog Agent sidecar or DaemonSet shipping logs and metrics with unified service tagging. Build a dashboard and two monitors (latency p99 and error-rate SLO burn) that page on breach.
tasks.deliverable: Instrumented app with structured logs, metrics and traces; Datadog Agent deployment config; a dashboard plus two alerting monitors, with a screenshot of a triggered alert.

tasks.title: Kubernetes Fundamentals: Deploy the Stack to EKS
tasks.description: Translate the container work into Kubernetes, the substrate for most platform roles: create an EKS cluster via Terraform, then deploy the API with a Deployment, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap/Secret, resource requests/limits and liveness/readiness probes. Do a rolling update and a rollback with kubectl, scale with an HPA, and run a StatefulSet-based or externalized Redis. Compare the ECS and EKS deployments in a short write-up.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned EKS cluster plus manifests/Helm chart deploying the API and Redis with probes, HPA and ingress; a recorded rolling update and rollback; and an ECS-vs-EKS comparison note.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Shift from 'the system runs' to 'the system survives'. The candidate designs and loads a scalable architecture, removes single points of failure, and reasons explicitly about load balancing, caching, queues, consistency and failure modes - the system-design depth the role's 'partial' rating demands and the core of a Datadog interview loop.

tasks.title: Write and Defend a Scalability Design Doc
tasks.description: Produce a design doc for a high-throughput ingestion pipeline (the shape Datadog operates): read path vs write path, stateless API behind the ALB, Redis caching layer, a queue to absorb bursts, Postgres/ElastiCache read replicas, partitioning/sharding strategy, backpressure and idempotency, and an explicit failure-mode table (node loss, AZ loss, Redis failover, cache stampede) with mitigations. State the CAP/PACELC trade-off chosen and why.
tasks.deliverable: A 4-6 page design doc with architecture diagram, capacity estimates (RPS, storage, cost), failure-mode table, and a documented rationale for consistency and caching choices.

tasks.title: Load, Stress and Failover Testing
tasks.description: Validate the design under pressure with k6 or Locust: baseline throughput and p50/p95/p99 latency, find the knee where latency or error rate climbs, verify HPA scales out and back in, then run a chaos-style failover - kill a task/pod, fail over a Redis replica, and saturate the CPU - and record how the system degrades and recovers. Feed findings back into the doc.
tasks.deliverable: k6/Locust load-test scripts, a results report with throughput/latency charts and the identified knee, an autoscaling timeline, and a chaos/failover test log with recovery times.

tasks.title: Reliability Engineering: SLOs, Error Budgets and Runbooks
tasks.description: Define SLIs and SLOs (availability, latency, freshness) for the API and cache, compute an error budget, and map each monitor to an SLO burn-rate alert. Write two operational runbooks - Redis memory saturation/failover and a bad-deploy rollback - each with detection, diagnosis, mitigation, and verification steps. Run one postmortem on a failure you induced in Phase 4.2.
tasks.deliverable: SLO/error-budget sheet, burn-rate alert rules tied to the Datadog dashboard, two runbooks, and a blameless postmortem of an induced incident.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert built artifacts into interview evidence. Rehearse the system-design and cloud/DevOps loops, package the repositories into a portfolio with measurable outcomes, and close the gaps exposed by mock interviews. Everything here points at proven, defensible work rather than unverifiable claims.

tasks.title: System-Design Mock Interviews with Self-Scoring
tasks.description: Run at least four timed 45-minute whiteboard mocks on designs adjacent to the target company (high-volume metrics ingestion, a config-delivery service, a log pipeline, a multi-tenant caching layer). Record them, score against a rubric (requirements, estimation, API/schema, data model, scaling, failure handling, trade-offs), and keep a running gap list that feeds targeted study on the weakest two areas.
tasks.deliverable: Four recorded mock sessions, a completed rubric per session, an architecture diagram for each design, and a written gap list with the fixes you studied.

tasks.title: DevOps/Cloud Rapid-Fire Drill Deck
tasks.description: Build an Anki-style deck of 80-120 cards drawn only from what you actually built: Docker layer caching and multi-stage trade-offs, IAM least privilege and OIDC federation, VPC/subnet/NAT routing, ECS vs EKS, ALB vs NLB, Terraform state/locking/modules, Redis eviction policies and persistence, CI/CD rollback strategies, and Linux process/network troubleshooting commands. Review until you can answer each card aloud in under 60 seconds.
tasks.deliverable: A flashcard deck of 80-120 self-authored cards with answers, and a log of two full review passes with the weakest cards revisited.

tasks.title: Portfolio Package with Measurable Outcomes
tasks.description: Consolidate Phases 1-4 into a public, well-documented monorepo: the hardened containerized app, Terraform modules, the full CI/CD pipeline, the EKS/ECS deployment, the observability setup, load-test reports, and the design doc. Each README states the problem, the approach, the measured result (image size, deploy time, p99 latency, cost) and how to reproduce it. Add architecture diagrams and a one-page summary mapped to the target job's requirements.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub monorepo with per-module READMEs, architecture diagrams, a metrics table (image size, deploy time, p99 latency, throughput, cost), and a requirements-to-evidence mapping page.

careerPlans.summary: This 12-16 week plan is built around the candidate's exact profile for the Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer role at Datadog: zero Docker/AWS/Redis and only partial CI/CD and system design. It starts by making containerization and an automated quality gate the daily habit (Phase 1), then deep-dives the three missing skills to production bar - hardened images, a Terraform-provisioned AWS landing zone with managed compute, and Redis as cache/queue/cluster (Phase 2). Phase 3 automates the delivery pipeline and adds observability on the Datadog model plus Kubernetes, Phase 4 forces scalability and reliability thinking through a design doc, load testing and SLOs, and Phase 5 converts the work into interview-ready artifacts. Every task targets a named gap and ends in a concrete, inspectable deliverable rather than a generic study item.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Rebuild the engineering substrate this role assumes: strong Go/Python, Linux internals, shell automation, Git workflow, and automated testing/linting. Everything here is written so it can be containerized and shipped in later phases, so no task is throwaway.

tasks.title: Build a Go + Python Linux host-inventory CLI with strict typing and tests
tasks.description: Write a CLI that reads /proc and /sys (CPU, memory, disk, network interfaces, listening ports) and emits JSON. Implement it twice: once in Go with a cmd/ + internal/ layout and cobra flags, once in Python 3.12 with a pyproject/uv setup and argparse. Cover both with unit tests plus table-driven tests in Go; target >85% coverage. Every package must pass go vet, staticcheck, ruff, and mypy in strict mode.
tasks.deliverable: Public repo host-inventory with two implementations, CI-ready Makefile, and a README documenting Go vs Python tradeoffs for platform tooling

tasks.title: Master Linux process, cgroup, and networking troubleshooting drills
tasks.description: Work through a documented lab: force a CPU-bound process into a cgroup v2 memory limit and observe OOM-kill behaviour, trace a slow syscall with strace, inspect socket state with ss/netstat, resolve an MTU and DNS failure inside a network namespace, and reproduce a file-descriptor leak. Record exact commands and the signal you used to diagnose each fault.
tasks.deliverable: linux-troubleshooting-runbook.md with 8 fault scenarios, the diagnostic command sequence for each, and the fix applied

tasks.title: Automate a repeatable dev environment with Bash/Python tooling and pre-commit
tasks.description: Replace manual setup with idempotent bash scripts (set -euo pipefail, shellcheck-clean) that install toolchains, configure git hooks, and bootstrap the repo. Wire pre-commit with shellcheck, gofmt, ruff, gitleaks secret scanning, and conventional-commit message linting, and document a trunk-based branching model with signed commits.
tasks.deliverable: bootstrap.sh plus .pre-commit-config.yaml and CONTRIBUTING.md defining the branch, review, and commit conventions

tasks.title: Practice structured code review on concurrency and error handling
tasks.description: Review a deliberately flawed Go service (unbounded goroutines, ignored errors, context not propagated, data race under -race) and a Python service with blocking calls in async handlers. Produce line-level review comments, then rewrite both with context cancellation, error wrapping, bounded worker pools, and graceful shutdown on SIGTERM.
tasks.deliverable: review-report.md with 15+ annotated findings and the corrected Go and Python sources alongside the originals

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Close the two runtime gaps that block the role most directly: Docker (containerization from image layers to Compose orchestration) and Redis (caching, data structures, and operational behaviour). Both are drilled to an operational, production-aware depth rather than tutorial level.

tasks.title: Produce a hardened multi-stage Dockerfile for a Go service
tasks.description: Containerize the Phase 1 host-inventory service from scratch. Use a build stage with cached dependency layers, then a distroless/scratch runtime stage; run as a non-root UID, copy a CA bundle, set HEALTHCHECK and ENTRYPOINT in exec form, pin base images by digest, and add OCI labels. Measure the size and layer count before and after, and rebuild layer caches to prove cache invalidation behaves as intended. Reproduce and then eliminate a common failure: a glibc-vs-musl binary mismatch and a missing CA certificate causing TLS errors.
tasks.deliverable: Optimized multi-stage Dockerfile (image <20MB, non-root, digest-pinned), .dockerignore, and a build-comparison table of image size before/after each optimization

tasks.title: Orchestrate a local stack with docker-compose and validate a service mesh of dependencies
tasks.description: Write a docker-compose.yml running the app, Postgres, and Redis with named volumes, a custom bridge network, environment/secret separation via env_file, healthcheck-gated depends_on (condition: service_healthy), restart policies, and resource limits. Add an override file for local development with bind-mounted hot reload. Break it deliberately by removing a healthcheck and document the resulting startup race.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml plus docker-compose.override.yml, .env.example, and a notes file showing the failed-startup reproduction and its fix

tasks.title: Master Redis data structures, caching patterns, and eviction behaviour
tasks.description: Instrument the inventory service with Redis across five patterns: cache-aside with TTL jitter and negative caching, a sorted-set leaderboard/latency ranking, a stream-based event buffer, a distributed lock (SET NX PX with a safe release script), and a token-bucket rate limiter. Use redis-py or go-redis with connection pooling, pipelining, and explicit timeouts. Then force failure modes: fill memory under noeviction vs allkeys-lru, simulate cache stampede on a hot key, and reproduce a stale-cache bug after a write. The service must degrade gracefully when Redis is unavailable.
tasks.deliverable: redis-cache-layer branch with benchmark data for cache-hit vs cache-miss latency, eviction policy note, and a stampede-mitigation write-up using a lock or single-flight

tasks.title: Operate Redis like production: persistence, replication, and key hygiene
tasks.description: Configure a primary-replica pair in Compose with AOF + RDB persistence, authentication, and a non-default port. Test a failover by killing the primary, inspect replication offsets with INFO replication, run MEMORY USAGE and SCAN-based key audits, and script a safe key-namespace migration (SCAN + batched writes, never KEYS). Set maxmemory-policy deliberately and justify the choice.
tasks.deliverable: redis.conf set with primary/replica roles, a failover test transcript, and a key-naming and TTL convention document for the team

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Move the containerized stack into AWS and make delivery continuous. AWS depth (compute, networking, IAM, managed data) pairs with an upgraded CI/CD practice that matches a platform team's expectations: reproducible, gated, and automatically deployed pipelines with rollback.

tasks.title: Provision AWS networking and compute from scratch with Terraform
tasks.description: Build a VPC with public/private subnets across two AZs, an internet gateway, NAT gateway, route tables, security groups, and an Application Load Balancer fronting an ECS Fargate service running the Phase 2 image. Add an ECR repository with lifecycle policies, IAM task roles with least privilege, CloudWatch log groups, and a Secrets Manager-held Redis credential. Push the image to ECR and reach the service through the ALB over HTTPS. Everything in modules with remote state in S3 + DynamoDB locking.
tasks.deliverable: terraform/ repo (modules for vpc, ecs, alb, ecr, iam) that stands up the full stack, plus terraform state backend config and an architecture diagram of the deployed topology

tasks.title: Attach a managed Redis and object store to the AWS stack
tasks.description: Migrate the service from local Redis to ElastiCache (replication group in private subnets, encryption in transit, parameter group tuned) and store static artifacts in S3 with a bucket policy that blocks public access and enforces TLS. Update application config to read endpoints from environment/Secrets Manager, and verify the cache-hit path and a cold-start path both work from ECS.
tasks.deliverable: ElastiCache + S3 Terraform modules, an app config change set pointing at managed endpoints, and a verification log showing cache hits from inside ECS

tasks.title: Level up CI/CD to a gated, multi-environment delivery pipeline
tasks.description: Upgrade the basic workflow into a GitHub Actions pipeline with a lint/unit/integration test matrix (Go 1.22 on Linux + macOS, Python 3.11/3.12), an integration stage that spins up Redis and Postgres as service containers, OIDC-based AWS authentication with no long-lived keys, Docker buildx multi-arch image builds with layer caching to ECR, and staged promotion dev to staging to prod with required reviewers. Include a rollback job that reverts to the previous ECS task definition revision.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflows (ci.yml, deploy.yml, rollback.yml) with a lint-and-test matrix, OIDC role assumption, multi-arch builds, and documented rollback rehearsal

tasks.title: Add infrastructure validation, policy, and drift detection to the pipeline
tasks.description: Gate infrastructure changes automatically: run terraform fmt, validate, tflint, and a plan against the real backend; add static analysis with checkov or tfsec and fail the build on high-severity findings; deploy via a plan-artifact-then-apply job so the applied plan is exactly the reviewed one. Schedule a nightly drift-detection job that fails loudly when the live stack diverges from state.
tasks.deliverable: iac-validate workflow, .tflint.hcl, checkov baseline with documented exceptions, and a scheduled drift-detection workflow with a sample alert

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Turn a working deployment into a system you could defend in an on-call review: high availability, observability with Datadog, autoscaling, load and failure testing, and the system-design reasoning behind each tradeoff. This is also where the partial System Design skill is strengthened with real measurements instead of diagrams alone.

tasks.title: Instrument the platform end-to-end with Datadog
tasks.description: Wire the Datadog Agent into ECS as a sidecar and adopt the dd-trace SDK for distributed tracing across the ALB, service, and Redis calls. Ship structured JSON logs with trace correlation, build a dashboard covering golden signals (latency p50/p95/p99, traffic, errors, saturation), and create monitors with thresholds that would actually page: error rate, p99 latency, ECS task restarts, Redis evictions, and ALB 5xx. Add a synthetic API test.
tasks.deliverable: Live Datadog dashboard JSON export, monitor definitions as code, trace screenshots showing a full request path, and a runbook mapping each alert to a first diagnostic step

tasks.title: Design and load-test a horizontally scalable, caching-fronted architecture
tasks.description: Write a design doc for the service at 10x traffic: stateless app tier behind the ALB, Redis as a shared cache with consistent key strategy, read replicas or a queue to absorb write bursts, and an explicit answer on cache coherence and thundering herd. Then autoscale ECS on a custom Datadog/CloudWatch metric (requests per target or Redis latency), and run k6 or Locust at baseline, 5x, and 10x load to find the knee. Document where it breaks first and why.
tasks.deliverable: architecture-design-doc.md with capacity math and tradeoff table, plus load-test scripts and a results report showing throughput, p99 latency, and the identified bottleneck at each load tier

tasks.title: Run a chaos and failure-injection exercise on the live stack
tasks.description: Break things deliberately in a staging environment and verify the system behaves: kill ECS tasks mid-request to confirm graceful drain, saturate Redis to trigger eviction and confirm degradation is graceful rather than fatal, inject a 3-second latency into a dependency, and trigger an AZ failure by removing one subnet's resources. Confirm alerts fire within their target window and that recovery is automatic.
tasks.deliverable: chaos-experiment-report.md documenting four injected failures, the observed blast radius, alert latency, recovery time, and the concrete code or config fix applied for each

tasks.title: Codify reliability targets, cost, and operations as code
tasks.description: Define SLOs for availability and latency with an error budget policy, then implement the burn-rate alerts behind them. Cost-model the stack (Fargate, ElastiCache, ALB, NAT, logs) and apply at least two optimizations such as savings plans, log retention tiering, or right-sized tasks, quantifying the saving. Add a disaster-recovery procedure covering Redis snapshot restore, Terraform redeploy from state, and a measured recovery time.
tasks.deliverable: slo-and-error-budget.md, a cost breakdown with before/after figures, and a tested disaster-recovery runbook with a recorded restore drill

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the built portfolio into interview performance: rehearsed system-design narratives, hands-on troubleshooting under time pressure, a polished DSA/tooling baseline, and a story bank grounded in the actual projects above rather than generic answers.

tasks.title: Rehearse timed system-design interviews on the built architecture
tasks.description: Run six 45-minute mock design sessions out loud, whiteboard-first: a metrics ingestion pipeline at high write volume, a multi-tenant platform control plane, a CI/CD system that deploys thousands of services, a globally distributed cache, a log-search backend, and an autoscaling scheduler. Use your real AWS and Redis work as the evidence base. Each session ends with estimated numbers: QPS, storage, instance counts, and a stated bottleneck.
tasks.deliverable: Six whiteboard designs with capacity estimates, plus a self-scored rubric sheet tracking requirement gathering, API design, data model, scaling, and tradeoff articulation

tasks.title: Drill Docker, AWS, and Redis troubleshooting as live scenario prompts
tasks.description: Prepare 20 interview-style scenarios and a decisive answer for each: an image that runs locally but crashes with exec format error in ECS, a container OOM-killed at 512MB, a task stuck in PENDING due to IAM or subnet issues, a NAT gateway cost spike, Redis latency spikes from a slow command, cache stampede after a deploy, and a pipeline that deploys but never becomes healthy. Practise diagnosing each from logs and metrics without seeing the code.
tasks.deliverable: troubleshooting-interview-bank.md with 20 scenarios, each containing the first three diagnostic commands, the likely root cause, and the fix

tasks.title: Sharpen coding rounds with container and concurrency-aware problems
tasks.description: Solve 60 curated problems with emphasis on LRU cache, rate limiter, task scheduler, log parser, token bucket, and connection-pool style design questions, since these mirror real platform work. Practise Go/Python implementations under a 35-minute timer, then re-solve every missed problem from scratch a week later. Include at least 10 problems requiring concurrency primitives and correct shutdown.
tasks.deliverable: Annotated solutions repo organised by pattern, with a spaced-repetition tracker showing first-attempt and review-pass rates

tasks.title: Package the portfolio and rehearse the behavioural story bank
tasks.description: Write a README-first portfolio landing page linking the Terraform modules, Compose stack, CI/CD pipelines, Datadog dashboards, and load-test and chaos reports, each with a one-paragraph problem/approach/outcome framing and measured numbers. Draft eight STAR stories mapped to platform-team values (ownership of production, incident response, automation mindset, collaboration with developers), and dry-run a 5-minute walkthrough of the flagship project on video.
tasks.deliverable: Public portfolio repo with architecture diagrams and result metrics, a STAR story bank of eight entries, and a recorded 5-minute project walkthrough

careerPlans.summary: A tailored 15-19 week roadmap for a Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer role (Datadog). The candidate enters with an empty verified skill baseline, so Phase 1 rebuilds the Go/Python, Linux, and code-quality substrate that everything else depends on. Phase 2 attacks the two highest-priority runtime gaps head-on - Docker to a hardened, multi-stage, distroless standard and Redis through cache-aside, locking, rate limiting, eviction, and replication - because both are load-bearing in a platform role. Phase 3 lifts the stack into AWS (VPC, ECS Fargate, ALB, IAM, ElastiCache, S3) with Terraform and upgrades the partial CI/CD skill into a gated, OIDC-authenticated, multi-environment pipeline with rollback and IaC drift detection. Phase 4 raises the partial System Design skill to interview grade through real evidence: Datadog golden-signal dashboards and monitors, load testing to 10x to locate the actual bottleneck, chaos and AZ-failure experiments, SLOs with error budgets, and cost modelling. Phase 5 converts the artifacts into interview performance via timed design mocks, a 20-scenario troubleshooting bank drawn from the candidate's own builds, container-aware coding drills, and a measured, README-first portfolio. Every task produces a concrete artifact, and later phases deliberately reuse the code and infrastructure built earlier so the effort compounds into one defensible production system rather than disconnected exercises.

phases.title: Phase 1: Foundations & Architecture Alignment
phases.description: Refine core code quality, type safety, and architectural modularity.

tasks.title: Harden Core Architecture Architecture & Data Contracts
tasks.description: Define strict DTO boundaries and interface validation for Core Architecture.
tasks.deliverable: Typed contract schema and validation tests

tasks.title: Implement Structured Error Handling & Logging Middleware
tasks.description: Build centralized HTTP error classes and correlation ID tracing.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable error handler pipeline

phases.title: Phase 2: Closing Priority Gaps (Docker, AWS)
phases.description: Address core missing requirements needed for technical evaluation.

tasks.title: Build Hands-On Working Proof of Concept with Docker
tasks.description: Implement and configure a production-ready module featuring Docker.
tasks.deliverable: Tested implementation repository using Docker

tasks.title: Integrate AWS into CI Pipeline
tasks.description: Automate build verification and lint checks on push.
tasks.deliverable: Automated CI/CD configuration file

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud & Infrastructure (Redis)
phases.description: Demonstrate real-world deployment and scalability readiness.

tasks.title: Deploy Service to Cloud Environment with Redis
tasks.description: Configure security groups, DNS, environment secrets, and monitoring.
tasks.deliverable: Live HTTPS deployment URL and runbook

tasks.title: Performance Benchmark & Caching Layer with Redis
tasks.description: Measure latency before and after caching optimization.
tasks.deliverable: Benchmark report showing response latency reduction

phases.title: Phase 4: High-Scale System Design & Production Readiness
phases.description: Master architectural trade-offs expected in senior interviews.

tasks.title: Design Distributed Architecture for Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer
tasks.description: Map out architecture for high availability, fault tolerance, and data partitioning.
tasks.deliverable: Architectural diagram and trade-off whitepaper

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Model Answers
phases.description: Practice context-aware technical screening questions.

tasks.title: Complete Mock Technical Screening on Docker
tasks.description: Answer deep-dive questions and review 4-pillar evaluation scores.
tasks.deliverable: Interview session scoring >= 80% across all pillars

careerPlans.summary: Structured roadmap to bridge 3 critical gaps and prepare for Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Build the daily loop a Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer is assumed to already own: containers you can build, run and debug, a local multi-service stack, and a single quality gate that behaves identically on a laptop and in CI. Docker is a zero-level gap and CI/CD is only partial, so this phase creates the reproducible build-test-run foundation that every later phase deploys.

tasks.title: Container Mechanics from Zero: Build, Run, Inspect, Debug
tasks.description: Start at the atomic level with no Docker experience assumed. Write a first Dockerfile for a small HTTP service (Go or Python/FastAPI), then deliberately practise the daily verbs: docker build with and without cache, docker run with port and env mapping, docker exec, docker logs -f, docker inspect to read IPs/mounts/health, docker stats, docker image ls, docker system df, and docker history to see why a layer was invalidated. Add a .dockerignore, an ENTRYPOINT/CMD split, and a HEALTHCHECK, then break the image on purpose (wrong WORKDIR, missing env var, bad EXPOSE) and fix each one by reading container state rather than guessing.
tasks.deliverable: A single-service Dockerfile plus a CONTAINERS.md cheat sheet recording the exact command that revealed each of four deliberately broken builds, and a `docker history` comparison showing one cache-hit and one cache-miss rebuild.

tasks.title: Multi-Service Local Stack with Compose: App + Postgres + Redis + Worker
tasks.description: Model the shape of a real platform in one command. Write docker-compose.yml running the API, a background worker, Postgres and Redis on one user-defined bridge network with named volumes, .env-driven configuration, healthcheck-based depends_on, restart policies and stdout log rotation. Prove the wiring end to end: the API writes to Postgres, the worker consumes a job from Redis, and both survive `docker compose down` / `up` with the volume intact. Log the container-to-container DNS names you used, because that naming is exactly what breaks first when the stack moves to Kubernetes or ECS.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml booting four services with `docker compose up` from a clean machine, a seed script, a verified volume-persistence test, a service-topology diagram, and a one-command smoke test that proves the API-to-worker round trip through Redis.

tasks.title: One Quality Gate for Laptop and Container: Makefile + Lint + Typecheck + Tests
tasks.description: CI/CD is only partial, so remove the ambiguity before automating it. Define a Makefile (or task runner) with the targets `lint`, `format`, `typecheck`, `test` and `build`, make every one of them runnable both on the host and inside the container, and pin tool versions so the two agree. Add a pre-commit hook running formatting and lint on staged files, strict type checking, and a conventional-commit check. The rule to enforce: anything a pipeline later runs must exist as a single scripted target first, never as inline YAML.
tasks.deliverable: Makefile with five CI-parity targets, pinned lint/format/typecheck tooling, a pre-commit hook config, and a short note showing identical output from `make test` on the host and `docker compose run app make test`.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Test Suite the Pipeline Can Trust
tasks.description: Make correctness reproducible before scaling anything. Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests that run against a real Postgres and a real Redis started by Testcontainers (or by Compose service definitions), not mocks. Cover one happy path, one validation failure, one authentication/authorization failure, and one Redis-backed cache-hit-then-miss case. Produce a coverage report and confirm the whole suite runs with no pre-started dependencies, which is the property every CI runner depends on.
tasks.deliverable: Unit plus Testcontainers-backed integration suite covering four cases, a coverage report at 60%+ on the API layer, and a `make test` target that spins its own Postgres and Redis containers and needs no manual setup.

tasks.title: First GitHub Actions Pipeline: Lint, Typecheck, Test Matrix, Image Build
tasks.description: Take CI/CD from partial to demonstrable. Create a GitHub Actions workflow triggered on pull request that caches dependencies, runs the Makefile targets in order (lint, typecheck, test), builds the Docker images without pushing, uploads the coverage report as an artifact, and uses a small version matrix for the language runtime. Turn on branch protection so the checks must pass before merge, then open a deliberately failing PR to prove the gate actually blocks.
tasks.deliverable: Committed .github/workflows/ci.yml with caching, a runtime matrix, artifact upload and an image-build job; branch protection enabled; a screenshot of one green run and one run that blocked a broken PR.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Move Docker from 'it runs' to 'a platform team would ship it', and meet Redis properly for the first time. Images get small, non-root, pinned and scanned; the pipeline becomes reusable rather than copy-pasted; and Redis is learned as a data store with eviction, persistence and failure behaviour instead of as a cache library. Both are named priority gaps for this target role.

tasks.title: Production Image Hardening and Supply-Chain Scanning
tasks.description: Rebuild the images to production bar: multi-stage builds (deps, build, runtime), distroless or slim runtime bases, a non-root user with a fixed UID, only compiled artifacts copied forward, OCI labels, pinned base-image digests, and BuildKit cache mounts so dependency layers survive code changes. Generate an SBOM with Syft, scan with Trivy and fix or document every HIGH/CRITICAL finding, strip secrets from image history, and measure before/after with `docker image ls` and `dive`. Finish with a multi-arch buildx build for amd64 and arm64, because the target role runs mixed architecture.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened multi-stage Dockerfile producing a runtime image under 200MB running as non-root on a pinned digest, multi-arch buildx output, generated SBOM, Trivy report with a fix log, and a before/after size and layer-count table.

tasks.title: Image Registry Workflow: Tagging, Immutability, Provenance, Signing
tasks.description: Learn the registry as an operational system, not a push destination. Create a private registry repository (GHCR now, ECR later), define a tagging strategy (immutable semantic tags plus a git-SHA tag, never a moving `latest` in production), enable image immutability and retention policy, and add digest-pinned deployment. Sign images with cosign and verify the signature at pull time, then simulate the two failures that matter operationally: a tag that was overwritten, and a pull of an unsigned or non-existent digest.
tasks.deliverable: Registry repository with immutability and retention configured, documented tagging and digest-pinning strategy, a cosign signing plus verification step, and an incident note for both simulated failures with the exact error output.

tasks.title: Redis Fundamentals: Data Structures, Eviction, Persistence, Replication
tasks.description: Learn Redis as infrastructure. In a container, exercise strings, hashes, sorted sets, lists and streams with redis-cli, then reason about memory: maxmemory-policy options (noeviction, allkeys-lru, volatile-ttl), key expiry, big-key and hot-key risk, and why `KEYS` is banned in production. Configure and compare RDB snapshots against AOF (everysec versus always) by loading data, killing the container mid-write, restarting and measuring what survived. Turn on a replica, force a failover, and record the data loss window. Map each experiment to the question an interviewer asks: what happens to this data on restart, and at what cost in latency.
tasks.deliverable: An experiments log with redis-cli transcripts for five data structures, a memory/eviction configuration table, a measured RDB versus AOF durability comparison after a forced crash, and a documented replica failover with the observed data-loss window.

tasks.title: Reusable Parameterized CI/CD with Scanning Gates and Environment Controls
tasks.description: Replace duplicated YAML with a system. Extract the build, test and image steps into a `workflow_call` reusable workflow plus composite actions, add path filters and concurrency groups that cancel superseded PR runs, cache Docker layers through buildx, and insert Trivy image scanning and dependency audit jobs that fail the build on HIGH/CRITICAL. Add a short-lived preview environment per pull request and a protected environment with required reviewers for anything that deploys. Document the .github/ structure as a diagram so the pattern is explainable, which is precisely the 'how do you scale pipelines across teams' question this role asks.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable workflow plus composite actions used by both PR and release pipelines, concurrency groups, buildx layer caching, scanning jobs that gate merges, a per-PR preview environment, and a documented .github/ architecture diagram.

tasks.title: Container Runtime Debugging and Operations Runbook
tasks.description: Deliberately reproduce and diagnose the six failures that make up real container on-call: crash loop from a bad entrypoint, OOM-kill under a memory limit, port conflict, container-network DNS resolution failure, permission error from running as non-root against a mounted volume, and a container that ignores SIGTERM and is SIGKILLed after the grace period. For each, capture the symptom, the diagnostic commands (`docker logs`, `inspect`, `events`, `stats`, `exec`, `compose ps`), the root cause and the fix. Add correct SIGTERM handling with a preStop-style drain and record CPU/memory behaviour under applied limits.
tasks.deliverable: Container troubleshooting runbook covering six reproduced incidents with real command output, a graceful-shutdown demo showing a clean SIGTERM exit code 0, and a `docker stats` before/after report under CPU and memory limits.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the hardened Phase 2 containers onto managed infrastructure that is provisioned entirely as code. The emphasis is on the parts of AWS a platform engineer is actually asked about: least-privilege IAM, VPC and subnet design, ALB-fronted container services, managed data and secrets, and an event-ingestion path built for throughput. Everything here is Terraform, reviewed in a pull request, not clicked in a console.

tasks.title: AWS Account Baseline as Code: Identity, Guardrails, Budgets, Remote State
tasks.description: Start AWS correctly instead of dangerously. Create a non-root admin identity with MFA, a least-privilege deployment role, and AWS CLI v2 profiles. Provision with Terraform in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking and state encryption. Add a budget with alerts, CloudTrail logging, default encryption on storage, tagging standards enforced by policy, and a written note on how to avoid the classic first-month mistakes (open security groups, long-lived access keys, unencrypted volumes).
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles and policies, an S3 plus DynamoDB remote-state backend, a budget with an active alert, CloudTrail enabled, a least-privilege deployment policy document, and a screenshot of the budget alarm.

tasks.title: Deploy Containers to ECS Fargate behind an ALB in Private Subnets
tasks.description: Run the Phase 2 images on managed compute. In Terraform define a VPC with public and private subnets across two Availability Zones, route tables, an internet gateway, a NAT gateway for egress, and security groups where only the ALB is publicly reachable and tasks accept traffic solely from the ALB security group. Push images to ECR, create an ECS cluster and Fargate service with a task definition pulling secrets at start, and front it with an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks and a rolling deployment configuration. Verify by draining and replacing a task without dropping requests.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned VPC (2 AZs, public/private subnets, NAT), ECR repository, ECS Fargate service with an ALB health-checked target group, a reachable public URL, and a deployed-architecture diagram plus a log excerpt of a rolling replacement with zero failed requests.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Secrets and ElastiCache: RDS, S3, Secrets Manager, Redis
tasks.description: Replace every local dependency with a managed one and prove it. Provision RDS Postgres in private subnets whose security group accepts connections only from the ECS service, a versioned and lifecycle-managed S3 bucket, Secrets Manager entries injected into the task at startup so no credential lives in an image or a repo, and an ElastiCache Redis cluster in a private subnet group. Point the application's Redis client at ElastiCache and demonstrate a real cache hit served from the cloud, not from a local container. Document the security-group-chaining model, which is the single most common AWS interview probe for this role.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Postgres, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining, a completed database migration against RDS, proof of an S3 object upload and lifecycle rule, and an application log line showing a cache hit served by ElastiCache.

tasks.title: Event Ingestion Path: SQS, Kinesis and a Scaled Consumer
tasks.description: Build the ingestion shape this role actually operates. Create an ingestion endpoint that publishes events to SQS with a dead-letter queue and redrive policy, and a second path that streams to Kinesis for ordered replay. Run the consumer as its own ECS service scaled on queue depth, and make handlers idempotent with deduplication keys so redelivery is safe. Deliberately poison a message to exercise the DLQ, then replay the DLQ and confirm no duplicate side effects. Note the throughput, batch size and visibility-timeout tradeoffs you chose.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for SQS with DLQ and redrive, a Kinesis stream and a queue-depth-scaled consumer service, idempotent handlers with a dedupe store in Redis, and a demo log showing a poisoned message land in the DLQ, be replayed, and produce exactly one side effect.

tasks.title: Keyless Delivery: GitHub OIDC to AWS, Blue/Green Deploy, Tested Rollback
tasks.description: Finish the partial CI/CD gap cloud-side. Configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a tightly scoped trust policy so no static access keys exist anywhere, then extend the Phase 2 release workflow to build, push to ECR, render a new ECS task definition and roll out. Add a production environment with a manual approval gate, post-deploy smoke tests against the live URL, and a rollback job that redeploys the previous task-definition revision. Publish lead time, deploy frequency, change-failure rate and MTTR from at least three real deploys.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based deploy workflow (build, ECR push, ECS rollout), committed IAM trust policy, GitHub Environment approval gate, smoke-test step, a rollback job, and a DORA metrics table from three real deploys including one rollback.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Turn 'it deploys' into 'it survives load'. Redis is taken from fundamentals to three production patterns (cache-aside, rate limiting, streams-based queues) with measured numbers; observability is built with the DogStatsD and OpenTelemetry tooling this employer is known for; autoscaling and load testing establish an actual SLO; and system design documentation converts implemented decisions into interview language.

tasks.title: Production Cache-Aside with Redis: TTLs, Versioned Keys, Stampede Control
tasks.description: Implement caching the way a platform team does. Add a cache-aside layer in front of the hottest read endpoint on ElastiCache with explicit per-key TTLs, namespaced and versioned key names so a deploy can invalidate wholesale, negative caching for misses, and stampede protection via a short-lived lock or single-flight so a cold key cannot fan out onto the database. Instrument hit rate, miss latency and eviction counts, then run a before/after benchmark and tune TTLs from the measured data rather than a guess. Document the invalidation strategy and the consistency window it accepts.
tasks.deliverable: Cache-aside implementation with TTL policy, versioned key scheme and stampede protection, a measured before/after latency and database-load benchmark, a cache hit-rate metric on a dashboard, and a written invalidation and consistency note.

tasks.title: Redis for Rate Limiting, Queues and Failover: Sorted Sets, Streams, Sentinel
tasks.description: Cover the second and third pattern. Build a distributed token-bucket or sliding-window rate limiter on a sorted set applied to the public API, with tests proving 429 responses under burst and correct behaviour when the limit window rolls over. Move slow work onto Redis Streams with consumer groups, pending-entry tracking, retries and a dead-letter stream, and make consumers idempotent. Then test resilience: force an ElastiCache failover with a Multi-AZ replica and record how the application behaves during the promotion window, and state clearly which operations lose data in that window and why that is or is not acceptable.
tasks.deliverable: Sorted-set rate limiter with 429 proving tests, a Redis Streams pipeline with consumer groups, retry and dead-letter stream, and a failover test report with measured recovery time and an explicit statement of accepted data loss.

tasks.title: Observability with DogStatsD, OpenTelemetry and Datadog-Style Dashboards
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end, using the tooling this team builds. Emit custom metrics through DogStatsD with tags and check cardinality cost deliberately, export an OpenTelemetry trace spanning ALB to API to worker to Redis, and ship structured JSON logs with request IDs and a correlation ID that links a log line to a trace. Build a dashboard covering request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, saturation and cache hit rate, define two SLOs with error budgets, and create alert monitors that fire on symptoms rather than causes. Include one high-cardinality experiment and its cost implication, because that is the tradeoff this employer lives with.
tasks.deliverable: DogStatsD custom metrics plus one OpenTelemetry trace across four hops, structured-logging middleware with correlated request IDs, an SLO dashboard with error budgets, two symptom-based alert monitors, and a cardinality-cost note with a measured example.

tasks.title: Load Testing and Autoscaling to a Stated SLO
tasks.description: Prove the platform scales and find where it stops.
