Write a k6 (or Locust) scenario mixing read-heavy and write traffic against the deployed endpoint, then configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target with sensible min, max and cooldown values. Capture throughput, p95 latency and error rate before and after scale-out, tune the target values to hold a stated SLO, and identify the first bottleneck the load reveals, which is almost always the database connection pool or a cache cold-start, and fix it.
tasks.deliverable: k6/Locust load-test script and report showing scale-out with before/after throughput, p95 and error rate against the SLO, tuned autoscaling policies with documented target values, and a bottleneck analysis with the applied fix and its measured effect.

tasks.title: System Design Documents: Metrics Ingest, Log Search, Multi-Region Control Plane
tasks.description: Turn implementation into design language, aimed squarely at this employer's domain. Write three design documents: a high-volume metric ingestion and aggregation pipeline (agent to queue to aggregator to time-series store, with batching, backpressure, cardinality limits and sharding); a log ingestion and search path (buffering, partitioning, indexing, retention tiers); and a multi-region control plane with consistent configuration rollout and failure isolation. Each must state API contracts, data model and partition keys, capacity estimates with real math, caching and queueing decisions, idempotency, failure modes and a tradeoff table. Every choice must cite something you built in Phases 2-4 rather than a generic best practice.
tasks.deliverable: Three design documents with architecture diagrams, capacity and sizing math, partition-key rationale, tradeoff tables, a failure-mode table (retry, timeout, circuit breaker, backpressure), and a self-critique list of where an interviewer would push back.

tasks.title: Multi-Environment Terraform, Cost Control and Disaster Recovery
tasks.description: Make the platform repeatable and affordable. Refactor Terraform into reusable modules consumed by dev, staging and prod with environment-specific sizing via var-files or workspaces, stand up a second full environment and prove the pipeline promotes between them. Use Cost Explorer to find and apply three real optimizations (Fargate sizing, RDS instance class, right-sized ElastiCache node type, or log retention), recording the dollar delta. Then write and actually execute a backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3, measuring recovery time and stating RTO and RPO.
tasks.deliverable: Modular multi-environment Terraform with a deployed staging stack and pipeline promotion between environments, a cost analysis with three applied optimizations and actual dollar deltas, and an executed backup/restore runbook with measured recovery time and stated RTO/RPO.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert Phases 1-4 into interview performance for a Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer loop: timed distributed-systems design drills in the metrics and logging domain, rapid-fire depth on containers and Redis internals, exam-grade AWS consolidation, a portfolio repository that reads as a case study, and metric-backed stories that survive follow-up questions.

tasks.title: Timed Distributed-Systems Design Drills with Diagrams and Capacity Math
tasks.description: Run at least six timed 35-40 minute drills, solo, with two recorded for review: a metrics ingestion pipeline at millions of samples per second, a log aggregation and search system, a rate limiter for a public API, a multi-tenant configuration rollout system, an idempotent job-processing queue, and a high-availability cache tier with invalidation. For each, clarify requirements, estimate scale on paper, sketch the architecture, choose partition keys and storage, place queues and caches, name the bottleneck and the failure mode, then write out answers to the three hardest follow-ups. Reuse the Phase 4 documents so the reasoning is yours, not memorized.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, decisions, follow-up answers) and two recorded mock design sessions with a written list of recurring weak points and how each was addressed.

tasks.title: Container and Platform Deep-Dive Question Bank
tasks.description: Convert hands-on Docker work into the fast, precise answers a platform interview expects. Build a 60+ question bank you can answer in under a minute each: image layers and the cache invalidation rules, union filesystems, namespaces and cgroups, what the OCI spec standardizes, Docker versus containerd versus runc, bridge versus host versus overlay networking, DNS resolution between containers, how limits become kernel controls, why a PID 1 that ignores SIGTERM breaks rollouts, image pull policy, how a registry-backed platform serves thousands of nodes, and what a container runtime must guarantee during a node drain. Answer from your Phase 2 experiments and cite the command output that proves each one.
tasks.deliverable: A 60+ question container and platform answer bank with one paragraph plus a reproduced command or config per answer, and a list of the ten questions you could not answer fluently with a remediation date for each.

tasks.title: Redis and Data-Store Troubleshooting Drills
tasks.description: Prepare for the operational data-store questions. Work through twelve scenario drills live: unexpected memory growth and eviction storms, latency spikes from a big key, a hot key on one shard, a replica that lags or fails over and loses writes, a cache stampede after mass eviction, a rate limiter that double-counts across instances, a stream consumer group with growing pending entries, and a poisoned payload looping in a dead-letter path. For each, state the detection signal, the diagnostic command, the likely root cause, the mitigation and the permanent fix, then compare Redis to the alternatives (Memcached, DynamoDB, Postgres queues, Kafka) with a decision table.
tasks.deliverable: Twelve written scenario drills each with detection signal, diagnostic commands and fix, plus a data-store selection decision table comparing Redis, Memcached, DynamoDB, Postgres and Kafka across durability, latency, ordering and operational cost.

tasks.title: AWS Knowledge Consolidation and Timed Practice Exams
tasks.description: Turn practical AWS work into interview-ready fluency across the domains this role probes: IAM and cross-account trust, VPC design and connectivity, ECS, ECR and Fargate versus EKS, RDS and ElastiCache, S3 and lifecycle, SQS, SNS and Kinesis, CloudWatch and EventBridge, autoscaling, and cost models. Condense each service into a one-page sheet that pairs the service with the specific artifact you built with it. Sit at least three timed practice exams and turn every wrong answer into a written service-level explanation, targeting 80%+ before scheduling the real exam.
tasks.deliverable: One-page cheat sheets for 12+ AWS services each linked to a project artifact, three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log, and a 80%+ consistent baseline before booking the exam.

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Architecture Writeup and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate the code, Dockerfiles, Terraform modules, workflows, runbooks, scan reports and dashboards into one public repository whose README reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, local quickstart, cloud deployment and rollback guide, observability screenshots, load-test numbers, cost findings and the incident runbook. Then write RESUME.md mapping each project capability to a resume bullet with a number attached, and rewrite prior roles to foreground the transferable core: pipeline ownership, infrastructure as code, least privilege, change control and incident response, alongside the newly proven Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD and design work.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, container quickstart, Terraform and deploy guides, dashboard screenshots, load-test results and rollback runbook, plus a RESUME.md capability-to-bullet mapping and a rewritten resume section for the Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer target.

tasks.title: Mock Interview Loop and Metric-Backed STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the whole loop and make every story defensible. Run a live coding round (add a tested endpoint plus a Redis-backed change to the running containerized service), a Docker and AWS deep dive, a Redis troubleshooting round, and a system design round, recording two of them. Build a STAR bank of 8+ stories drawn from Phases 1-4 with hard numbers: 'reduced the runtime image from 1.1GB to 180MB and cut cold-start time', 'diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop from task-level metrics', 'raised cache hit rate to 85% and cut p95 latency by 60%', 'took delivery from manual to OIDC-federated pipelines with a tested rollback', 'designed a metric pipeline sized for millions of samples per second'. Log every question asked and tighten each answer. Finish with a readiness checklist across Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD and system design.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank of 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (one coding, one system design), a question log with revised answers and timings, and a final readiness checklist scoring Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD and system design.

careerPlans.summary: A 10-week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a candidate targeting Cloud Platform & DevOps Engineer, sequenced to close three missing skills (Docker, AWS, Redis) and lift two partial ones (CI/CD, System Design) with no generic filler. Phase 1 assumes zero Docker and builds a reproducible loop: container mechanics, a four-service Compose stack, one quality gate shared by laptop and CI, container-aware tests, and a first GitHub Actions pipeline with branch protection. Phase 2 deepens the priority gaps: hardened multi-arch images under 200MB with SBOM and scan gates, a registry workflow with immutability, signing and digest pinning, Redis fundamentals including measured RDB versus AOF durability and a forced failover, a reusable parameterized pipeline with scanning gates and preview environments, and a six-incident container on-call runbook. Phase 3 closes AWS entirely in Terraform: a least-privilege account baseline with remote state and budgets, a two-AZ VPC with ECS Fargate behind an ALB, managed RDS, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining, an SQS and Kinesis ingestion path with a DLQ and idempotent consumers, and keyless OIDC delivery with blue/green rollout and a tested rollback. Phase 4 makes it production-grade and measurable: production cache-aside with TTL, key versioning and stampede control, sorted-set rate limiting plus Redis Streams consumer groups and a failover test, DogStatsD and OpenTelemetry observability with SLOs and alert monitors, k6 load testing against autoscaling to a stated SLO, three distributed-systems design documents in the metric and log ingestion domain, and modular multi-environment Terraform with cost optimization and an executed DR runbook. Phase 5 converts all of it into interview performance: six timed design drills, a 60+ question container depth bank, twelve Redis troubleshooting scenarios with a data-store decision table, AWS consolidation to 80%+ on practice exams, a public case-study portfolio with resume mapping, and eight metric-backed STAR stories with recorded mocks and a final readiness checklist. Every task names the specific gap it closes and produces an inspectable artifact an interviewer can review.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Establish the engineering baseline a Stripe-level full stack team expects before touching infrastructure: a reproducible containerized dev environment, automated lint/type/test gates, and written architecture decisions. Foundation for the Docker and CI/CD gaps.

tasks.title: Containerize the full stack dev environment with Docker
tasks.description: Take your existing full stack project (React/TypeScript frontend + API backend) and make it run with one command. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile (deps -> build -> minimal runtime), use a non-root user, add HEALTHCHECK, and a .dockerignore. Compose API, Postgres and Redis with named volumes, healthchecks and depends_on conditions, and run the frontend in a containerized dev mode too.
tasks.deliverable: Optimized multi-stage Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml bringing up API, Postgres and Redis with healthchecks; README section 'docker compose up runs the stack in <2 min'

tasks.title: Build a lint, typecheck and test CI matrix
tasks.description: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every PR: install with a lockfile, run ESLint/Prettier, strict TypeScript typecheck, unit tests, and an integration job that spins up Postgres and Redis as service containers. Add branch protection requiring the checks and fail the build on coverage drop below the current baseline.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with lint and test matrix (service containers for Postgres/Redis) plus branch protection rules and a coverage floor

tasks.title: Integration and contract test suite against real dependencies
tasks.description: Replace mocked DB/queue calls with integration tests that run against real Postgres and Redis containers. Cover request validation, error responses, and a typed API contract (OpenAPI/Zod or equivalent) shared between the backend and the TypeScript client so a schema change breaks the build.
tasks.deliverable: Integration test suite running against containerized Postgres/Redis plus a generated typed API client and contract test that fails on breaking schema changes

tasks.title: Write architecture decision records for the codebase
tasks.description: Document 4-5 key decisions in ADR format (why this API shape, sync vs async boundaries, where state lives, how errors/idempotency are handled). This forces you to reason about trade-offs out loud, which is exactly what a system design interview probes.
tasks.deliverable: docs/adr/ folder with 5 concise ADRs, each listing context, options considered, decision and consequences

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Close the three hard gaps - Docker, AWS and Redis - at a production level rather than a tutorial level. Each task produces a reusable component you will deploy and demo later.

tasks.title: Harden Docker builds for production
tasks.description: Rebuild the API image for production: multi-stage build with lockfile-based dependency caching, slim/distroless runtime, non-root USER, read-only filesystem, pinned base image digests, and BuildKit cache mounts. Run a Trivy image scan and cut image size and cold-start time measurably.
tasks.deliverable: Production Dockerfile with digest-pinned slim runtime, Trivy scan report with zero high/critical CVEs, and a before/after image size and cold-start benchmark

tasks.title: Implement Redis caching, idempotency and rate limiting
tasks.description: Use Redis for three real payment-path concerns: cache-aside for read-heavy lookups with TTL and explicit invalidation, idempotency key storage for write endpoints (SET NX with TTL), and a sliding-window rate limiter via a Lua script. Handle Redis being down without taking the API down.
tasks.deliverable: Redis-backed modules for cache-aside, idempotent POST handling and Lua sliding-window rate limiting, each with unit and integration tests and a graceful-degradation path

tasks.title: Get hands-on with core AWS primitives
tasks.description: Work directly in AWS: create an IAM role with least-privilege policies for the app, push your production image to ECR, store config/secrets in SSM Parameter Store or Secrets Manager, and use an S3 bucket with a scoped policy. Do it with IaC (Terraform or AWS CDK), not console clicks, and verify IAM permissions are genuinely scoped.
tasks.deliverable: IaC module provisioning ECR, IAM least-privilege roles, SSM/Secrets Manager entries and an S3 bucket, plus an architecture diagram and account-bootstrap README

tasks.title: Add image build, scanning and push to the pipeline
tasks.description: Extend CI so every merge to main builds the Docker image with BuildKit layer caching, runs vulnerability scanning, tags it with the immutable commit SHA, and pushes to ECR using OIDC (no long-lived AWS keys). Keep PR pipelines fast with a build matrix and dependency caching.
tasks.deliverable: CI job publishing SHA-tagged images to ECR via GitHub OIDC with scan gates and BuildKit cache, documented in the README

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Take the containerized, test-covered app to a real cloud environment and operate it: managed Postgres, managed Redis, autoscaling, observability and a repeatable release process.

tasks.title: Deploy the API to AWS ECS Fargate behind an ALB
tasks.description: Deploy the production image to ECS Fargate across two availability zones behind an Application Load Balancer with health checks and TLS. Wire in RDS Postgres and ElastiCache Redis via private subnets, and inject secrets from Secrets Manager at runtime. Everything defined in IaC and reproducible from an empty account.
tasks.deliverable: IaC stack deploying ECS Fargate + ALB + RDS + ElastiCache in a two-AZ VPC, a live staging URL, and a one-page deploy/teardown runbook

tasks.title: Design the production Redis topology and cache strategy
tasks.description: Move from a single Redis to ElastiCache with a replica and automatic failover. Configure maxmemory-policy, connection pooling, timeouts and retry/backoff in the client, and define which data is cache vs source of truth. Prove the design with a load test comparing cache-on vs cache-off latency.
tasks.deliverable: ElastiCache (primary + replica, multi-AZ) configuration as code, hardened Redis client wrapper, and a load-test report showing p95/p99 improvement from caching

tasks.title: Instrument the stack: logs, metrics, alarms and autoscaling
tasks.description: Emit structured JSON logs and request traces, then build CloudWatch dashboards and alarms on p99 latency, 5xx rate, ALB target health, DB connections and Redis memory. Add ECS autoscaling on CPU/request-count and enable rolling deployments with a health-check grace period for zero-downtime releases.
tasks.deliverable: Dashboards and alarms as code, structured logging + tracing in the app, and an autoscaling policy validated by a load test with no dropped requests during a deploy

tasks.title: Build a full release pipeline with rollback
tasks.description: Complete the pipeline: on merge to main, build, scan, push, run DB migrations as a one-off task, deploy to staging, run smoke tests, then promote to production with manual approval. Ensure a failing smoke test or health check automatically reverts to the previous task definition version.
tasks.deliverable: End-to-end GitHub Actions release pipeline (build -> scan -> migrate -> staging -> smoke tests -> prod promote) with an automatic rollback path demonstrated once

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it runs in the cloud' to 'it holds up under load and partial failure'. This is where the partial System Design skill becomes demonstrable, via a Stripe-shaped payments flow.

tasks.title: Design and build an idempotent payment authorization flow
tasks.description: Model a Stripe-like flow: a /charges endpoint that is safe to retry via idempotency keys, an internal ledger of state transitions, and async webhook delivery to consumers with HMAC signature verification, exponential-backoff retries and a dead-letter queue after N attempts. Document the design with sequence diagrams and explicit failure modes before coding.
tasks.deliverable: Design doc with sequence diagrams + working implementation of idempotent charge creation, signed webhook delivery with retries and a DLQ, covered by tests

tasks.title: Load test and fix the scaling bottlenecks
tasks.description: Write k6/Locust scenarios for the hot paths and run them against staging. Identify the first bottleneck (usually DB connections or N+1 queries), then apply connection pooling, targeted indexes, pagination and caching, and add backpressure/timeouts/circuit breakers so one slow dependency cannot cascade.
tasks.deliverable: Load-test scripts plus a report of p50/p95/p99 and throughput before and after, with each remediation tied to a measured improvement

tasks.title: Make write paths consistent and recoverable
tasks.description: Implement the transactional outbox pattern so DB writes and event publication cannot diverge, make consumers idempotent for at-least-once delivery, and add a reconciliation job that detects and repairs drift. Then write failure-injection tests (kill Redis mid-request, drop a webhook) to prove recovery.
tasks.deliverable: Outbox + idempotent consumer implementation, a scheduled reconciliation job, and a failure-injection test run showing no data loss or duplicate charges

tasks.title: Harden the payment path for security and secrets
tasks.description: Threat-model the API: strict input validation, no sensitive data in logs, secrets only from Secrets Manager, least-privilege IAM verified with the IAM policy simulator, dependency and image scanning in CI, and rate limiting on auth/charge endpoints. Document what is intentionally never stored (raw PAN, CVV).
tasks.deliverable: One-page threat model against OWASP Top 10, a security checklist with evidence (scans, IAM review, log audit), and hardened validation on write endpoints

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the work into interview performance: rehearse system design out loud, sharpen coding fundamentals, and package the project into a portfolio that proves the Docker/AWS/Redis gaps are closed.

tasks.title: Rehearse five system design interviews out loud
tasks.description: Practice full 45-minute whiteboard designs with a timer and a partner or recording: a payment processing pipeline, a distributed rate limiter, a webhook delivery system, a notification service, and a payments dashboard with real-time aggregation. Force yourself to state requirements, back-of-envelope numbers, API contract, data model, bottlenecks and trade-offs in that order.
tasks.deliverable: Five recorded/timed design walkthroughs with diagrams and a self-review rubric noting one concrete improvement per session

tasks.title: Sharpen coding interview fundamentals
tasks.description: Do 40 focused problems in your primary language (hash maps, queues, heaps, streams, concurrency basics), then re-solve the 10 you failed. Practice narrating complexity trade-offs and writing clean, testable code under time pressure - the same rigour your Phase 1 test suite demanded.
tasks.deliverable: A tracked problem log of 40 problems with time-to-solve, complexity notes, and re-solves of every miss

tasks.title: Publish the project as a hiring-manager-ready portfolio
tasks.description: Polish the repo that now spans Docker, AWS deployment and Redis: architecture diagrams, local one-command startup, documented trade-offs, the load-test numbers, and a live demo link. Rewrite resume bullets around outcomes with metrics and map each to the target role's requirements.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repo with README (architecture diagram, quickstart, benchmark table, trade-offs), a live demo URL, and a rewritten resume with quantified bullets

tasks.title: Run a full mock loop and prep behavioural stories
tasks.description: Complete a realistic mock loop (coding + system design + a project deep-dive on the deployment pipeline) and collect written feedback. Prepare 6 STAR stories covering ownership, incident/debugging, cross-team collaboration and disagreeing well, keeping them concise and outcome-focused.
tasks.deliverable: One full mock loop with written feedback plus a STAR story bank of 6 stories, reviewed and trimmed to 2 minutes each

careerPlans.summary: A 9-13 week plan that turns Docker, AWS and Redis from gaps into demonstrated, portfolio-visible strengths while lifting the partial CI/CD and System Design skills to production grade. Phase 1 puts a reproducible containerized environment and automated quality gates in place. Phase 2 goes deep on Docker hardening, Redis patterns (cache-aside, idempotency, rate limiting) and hands-on AWS primitives. Phase 3 ships the app to ECS Fargate with managed RDS/ElastiCache, observability and a full release pipeline with rollback. Phase 4 proves scalability and reliability through an idempotent, webhook-driven payment flow, load testing and failure injection. Phase 5 converts all of it into interview performance, a quantified resume and a public portfolio aimed at a Full Stack Engineer role.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Establish the reproducible container build and automated quality gate that every later phase depends on. Docker is the first hard gap: today nothing in the stack boots from a single command on a clean machine. This phase containerizes a reference full-stack app (React + TypeScript frontend, Node.js REST API, PostgreSQL), locks code quality behind a pre-commit hook and typechecked build, and creates the first GitHub Actions pipeline so Docker and CI/CD stop being gaps and become the daily loop. Everything built here is the substrate the AWS, Redis and system-design phases are deployed onto.

tasks.title: Containerize the Reference Full-Stack App with Multi-Stage Dockerfiles
tasks.description: Build a reference app (React + TypeScript frontend, Node.js/Express API, PostgreSQL) and define every service in containers. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile per service with explicit deps -> build -> runtime stages, so only compiled artifacts and production dependencies land in the runtime image. Pin base-image tags, add a .dockerignore, and set the API to run with NODE_ENV=production. Target the app's core domain as a payments/ledger-adjacent resource (accounts, transactions) so later phases can reuse it for Stripe-style problems.
tasks.deliverable: One multi-stage Dockerfile per service (frontend, API) plus a docker-compose.yml that boots frontend + API + Postgres from a clean checkout with a single `docker compose up`; README quickstart with the container network diagram.

tasks.title: Single-Command Dev Workflow with Hot Reload, Env Config and Healthchecks
tasks.description: Make the container stack usable for daily development. Add bind mounts and volume-anonymous node_modules for hot reload, drive all configuration through a committed .env.example plus a gitignored .env, define a Postgres healthcheck with healthcheck-based `depends_on`, and publish only the ports developers need. Confirm data survives a `docker compose down`/`up` cycle using a named volume.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml with hot reload, .env.example, Postgres healthcheck, named volume persistence test, and a documented 'restart without losing data' procedure.

tasks.title: Language-Level Quality Gate: Strict Types, Lint and Pre-Commit Hook
tasks.description: Make code quality mechanical rather than aspirational. Enable TypeScript strict mode (strict: true, noImplicitAny, noUncheckedIndexedAccess), configure ESLint + Prettier, and add a Husky + lint-staged pre-commit hook with commitlint conventional-commit enforcement. Expose identical `lint`, `typecheck` and `format` npm scripts that run the same way on the host and inside the container so CI reuses one source of truth.
tasks.deliverable: Committed strict tsconfig.json, ESLint/Prettier configs, Husky pre-commit hook, commitlint config, and a script list that fails the commit on any type or lint error.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Automated Test Suite (Unit + Integration)
tasks.description: Prove the API is testable in isolation exactly as a pipeline will test it. Add Vitest unit tests for business logic and Supertest integration tests against a real Postgres spun up with Testcontainers. Cover a happy path, an input-validation failure, an unauthorized-access case, and one money-movement edge case (idempotency key reuse or insufficient balance) since Stripe's domain demands it.
tasks.deliverable: Test suite with Testcontainers-backed integration tests, a `test` script that needs no pre-started database, and a coverage report showing 60%+ on the API layer.

tasks.title: First GitHub Actions CI Pipeline: Lint + Typecheck + Test Matrix
tasks.description: Close the zero-pipeline gap with the smallest useful CI. Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every pull request: cached dependency install, `lint`, `typecheck`, the test suite across a Node version matrix, and a Docker image build without pushing. Upload the coverage artifact and enable branch protection so all checks must pass before merge.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with a lint/typecheck/test matrix and an image-build job, branch protection enabled, and a link to a green PR pipeline run.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take Docker from 'it runs locally' to production bar, because Docker is the missing skill that gates both zero-downtime delivery and reproducible cloud deploys. Images become small, non-root, digest-pinned and scanned; the stack grows into six independently deployable services on isolated networks; and the pipeline becomes reusable with layer caching and a container-scanning gate. By the end the candidate can defend a Dockerfile, a Compose topology and a registry tagging strategy line by line in an interview.

tasks.title: Production Image Hardening and Supply-Chain Scanning
tasks.description: Rebuild the images for production: alpine/slim or distroless bases pinned by digest, a non-root user, only build artifacts copied into runtime, OCI labels, and a layer order that keeps dependency layers cached across code changes. Remove any baked-in secrets, generate an SBOM with Syft, scan with Trivy (fail on HIGH/CRITICAL), and measure the size delta with `docker image ls` and `dive`.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfile producing a runtime image under 300MB running as non-root on a pinned digest, SBOM file, Trivy scan report, and a before/after size and layer comparison.

tasks.title: Multi-Service Orchestration with Dev/Prod Compose Overrides
tasks.description: Model a realistic distributed system locally: frontend, API, background worker, Postgres, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy. Define a base compose file plus dev and prod override files; create custom networks that isolate the data tier (Postgres/Redis) from the public tier; use healthcheck-based `depends_on`, CPU/memory resource limits and JSON-file log rotation. Confirm the app degrades gracefully when Postgres is stopped and restarts cleanly when it returns.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml plus dev/prod overrides orchestrating six services with tier isolation, healthchecks, resource limits and log rotation; a verified volume-persistence test, a failure/restart demo, and a service-topology diagram.

tasks.title: Image Registries, Multi-Arch Builds and Tagging Strategy
tasks.description: Learn the delivery plumbing between build and cloud. Set up a GHCR repository, build multi-arch (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64) images with buildx, and adopt an immutable tagging strategy (git SHA + semver, never `latest` in deploys). Push, pull on a second machine, and prove the exact same digest deploys. Document the promotion path dev -> staging -> prod by tag.
tasks.deliverable: Buildx multi-arch build script, pushed GHCR images with SHA and semver tags and a `latest`-free convention, an image-promotion doc, and proof of a digest-identical pull on a second machine.

tasks.title: Container Debugging and Runtime Operations Runbook
tasks.description: Learn to operate containers, not just build them. Reproduce five incidents on purpose - crash loop from a bad entrypoint, OOM kill under a memory limit, port conflict, Docker-network DNS failure, and a volume permission error from running non-root - and diagnose each with `docker logs`, `exec`, `stats`, `inspect`, `events` and `docker compose`. Implement SIGTERM handling for graceful shutdown and record `docker stats` before/after applying CPU and memory limits.
tasks.deliverable: Container debugging runbook covering five reproduced incidents (symptom, diagnosis command, root cause, fix), a SIGTERM graceful-shutdown demo, and a resource-limit before/after stats report.

tasks.title: Reusable CI with Docker Layer Caching and a Scan Gate
tasks.description: Level the Phase 1 pipeline up for real container delivery. Extract a reusable workflow (`workflow_call`) plus composite actions for setup/test/build so jobs stop duplicating YAML, add path filters and concurrency groups to cancel superseded PR runs, enable buildx GHA layer caching, and add a Trivy job that fails the build on HIGH/CRITICAL findings. Tag and push images to GHCR only on main merges.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable GitHub Actions workflow + composite actions used by CI, buildx layer caching, concurrency groups, a blocking container-scan job, and a documented .github/ directory diagram.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the Phase 2 containers onto managed infrastructure provisioned entirely as code. Everything is Terraform: a least-privilege IAM baseline and remote state, a VPC with public/private subnets and NAT, ECR, ECS Fargate across two Availability Zones behind an ALB, RDS Postgres, S3, Secrets Manager, and ElastiCache Redis. Delivery becomes keyless via GitHub OIDC with a rolling then blue/green deploy and a tested rollback. This is the phase that turns 'I understand cloud concepts' into 'I shipped production on AWS'.

tasks.title: AWS Baseline as Code: IAM, Budgets and Remote State
tasks.description: Set up a clean AWS foundation. Create a dedicated non-root admin identity with MFA, a least-privilege deployment role, AWS CLI v2 profiles, and a budget alarm to prevent runaway cost. Provision everything with Terraform in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking. Write a short notes file mapping the IAM policy/role model and account/tag boundaries so the governance concepts are explicit before building infrastructure.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles/policies, budget alarms and an S3 + DynamoDB state backend; a documented least-privilege deployment policy; and a screenshot of the active budget alarm.

tasks.title: Deploy Containers to ECS Fargate behind an ALB in Private Subnets
tasks.description: Push the hardened images to Amazon ECR and run them on ECS Fargate across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks. Define the VPC, public/private subnets, route tables and NAT gateway in Terraform; place tasks in private subnets and expose only the ALB through a security group. Configure ALB listener rules, target-group health-check path, ECS task definitions with environment/secret references, and CloudWatch log groups.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned VPC (public/private subnets, route tables, NAT), ECR repo, ECS Fargate service on 2+ AZs, ALB with health checks, a reachable public URL, and a deployed-architecture diagram.

tasks.title: Managed Data and Secrets: RDS Postgres, S3 and Secrets Manager
tasks.description: Move off local containers to managed services. Provision RDS Postgres in private subnets whose security group accepts traffic only from the ECS service security group (security-group chaining), a versioned S3 bucket for uploads with a least-privilege bucket policy and lifecycle rule, and Secrets Manager entries for database credentials injected into the task at start. Run the app's migrations against RDS, wire the API to the managed database via environment-injected secrets, and prove an end-to-end upload to S3.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Postgres + S3 + Secrets Manager with security-group chaining and lifecycle rules; a migration run against RDS; proof of an S3 upload; and a screenshot of the app serving data from RDS.

tasks.title: Keyless CI/CD to AWS: OIDC, Blue/Green Deploy and Rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery to AWS without static keys. Configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a scoped trust policy, then extend the Phase 2 pipeline to build, push to ECR, render a new ECS task definition from the image SHA, and perform a rolling then AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment that waits for service stability. Add a GitHub Environment approval gate for production and a tested rollback to the previous task revision.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS rolling and blue/green), the IAM trust policy, a production approval gate, and logs proving both a successful deploy and a successful rollback.

tasks.title: Provision ElastiCache Redis as Managed Infrastructure
tasks.description: Stand up an ElastiCache Redis cluster in private subnets with a security group accepting traffic only from the ECS service, in a replication group with a primary and replica. Inject the endpoint through Secrets Manager/SSM, switch the app's existing local Redis connection to the managed endpoint, and verify a basic SET/GET through the deployed API. This is the infrastructure half of the Redis gap; the application patterns follow in Phase 4.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for an ElastiCache Redis replication group with security-group-restricted access, an endpoint wired through configuration, and a deployed API screenshot confirming a cache round-trip against ElastiCache.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives under load', closing the Redis and System Design gaps together. Redis is used three production ways - cache-aside with real invalidation, a token-bucket rate limiter, and job/session state - while SQS-backed workers add async processing with idempotency. Observability, autoscaling under load, and written system-design documents turn those implementations into the design vocabulary Stripe's interview loop probes. Every task here produces numbers that become interview evidence.

tasks.title: Redis Cache-Aside Layer with TTL, Invalidation and a Benchmark
tasks.description: Add a cache-aside layer to a hot read endpoint (e.g. account balance or transaction history) using ElastiCache Redis. Choose a key-naming convention with version prefixes, define explicit TTLs, invalidate on write, and add stampede protection (single-flight or jittered TTL) plus a negative-cache policy for misses. Benchmark the endpoint with and without cache under concurrent load and record hit rate.
tasks.deliverable: Cache-aside module with versioned keys, TTL and invalidation policy and stampede protection; a test proving a write invalidates the stale key; and a benchmark report showing hit rate and the p95 latency improvement.

tasks.title: Redis Token-Bucket Rate Limiter and Distributed Locks
tasks.description: Implement a Redis token-bucket rate limiter as a reusable Express middleware keyed per API key/IP, returning correct 429 responses with `Retry-After` and rate-limit headers. Use an atomic Lua script so the check-and-decrement is race-free across multiple ECS tasks. Add a Redis-backed distributed lock (Redlock-style or SET NX PX with fencing) and use it to guard one non-idempotent operation, then test both under concurrency.
tasks.deliverable: Rate-limiter middleware with an atomic Lua script, headers and 429 behavior proven by tests; a distributed lock used to protect one operation; and a concurrency test showing no double-execution.

tasks.title: Async Queue Processing with SQS, a Worker and Idempotency
tasks.description: Move slow work (receipt/email generation, report export, webhook fan-out) off the request path. Publish to an SQS queue from the API, run a separate ECS worker service consuming the queue with visibility-timeout tuning and a dead-letter queue, and make handlers idempotent with an idempotency key stored in Postgres/Redis. Track job status in Redis so the API can report progress, and demonstrate redelivery safety by forcing a duplicate message.
tasks.deliverable: SQS-backed worker as a separate ECS service with DLQ, idempotency-key handling, Redis job-status tracking, and a demo proving a duplicate message is processed exactly once with a before/after latency benchmark.

tasks.title: Observability: Structured Logs, Dashboards, Alarms and Tracing
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end. Emit structured JSON logs with request IDs and correlation IDs shipped to CloudWatch Logs; publish custom latency and business metrics (via the CloudWatch SDK or embedded metric format). Build a dashboard (request rate, p95 latency, error rate, ECS CPU/memory, Redis hit rate, SQS queue depth and DLQ count) with alarms on error-rate and latency thresholds and unhealthy ALB targets. Add OpenTelemetry tracing across ALB -> API -> worker.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, three or more CloudWatch alarms (latency, error rate, DLQ depth), an OTel trace of one request spanning API and worker, and a screenshot of the dashboard.

tasks.title: Autoscaling and Load Testing to a Defined SLO
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target; drive load with k6 (or Locust) against the deployed endpoint including the cached read, the rate-limited endpoint and the async write path. Capture p95 latency, throughput and error rate before and after scale-out, state an SLO, and tune target values, cooldowns and min/max task counts to meet it. Document the observed bottleneck and the fix.
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies with tuned min/max, a k6/Locust script and report (throughput, p95, error rate) showing scale-out to SLO, and a bottleneck analysis note.

tasks.title: System Design Documents Backed by the Built System
tasks.description: Turn implementation into design language. Write three design documents - a high-throughput payments/ledger API with exactly-once semantics, a multi-tenant SaaS backend, and an image-upload/processing pipeline - each covering API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy and invalidation, queueing and backpressure, idempotency, consistency tradeoffs, AWS hosting topology, scaling limits and failure modes. Every choice must cite something actually built in Phases 2-4 and include a tradeoff table for each read/write path.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design docs with architecture diagrams, tradeoff tables, capacity/SLO estimates, a failure-mode table (retry, timeout, circuit breaker, DLQ), and a self-critique list of likely interviewer pushback.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert every Phase 1-4 artifact into interview performance for the Full Stack Engineer loop at Stripe: a portfolio that reads like an engineering case study, timed system-design drills, AWS fluency, Docker/Redis deep-dive answers, and a metric-backed STAR story bank. Each deliverable already built becomes a diagram and a defensible decision, so gaps in Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD and system design are answered with shipped work and real numbers rather than theory.

tasks.title: Timed System Design Drills with Whiteboard Diagrams
tasks.description: Convert the Phase 4 design docs into verbal fluency. Run at least six timed 35-40 minute mock prompts alone and two with a peer or on video: a URL shortener, a feed/notification system, a payment-idempotency service, a rate-limited public API, an analytics ingestion pipeline, and a multi-tenant SaaS. For each: clarify requirements, estimate scale, sketch boxes and arrows, choose a data model, place caching and queues, name the bottleneck and the failure mode, then write answers to the three hardest follow-ups.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design drill packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, tradeoff decisions, follow-up answers) plus two recorded mock design sessions with a reviewed list of recurring weak points.

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Architecture Writeup and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate the code, Terraform, compose files, CI/CD workflows, tests, SBOM/scan reports and runbooks into one clean public repository whose README reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment guide, observability screenshots, load-test numbers, cost notes and the rollback runbook. Then write RESUME.md mapping each project feature to a resume bullet tailored to the Full Stack Engineer role.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, container quickstart, AWS deployment + rollback guides, dashboards and screenshots, plus a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping reviewed against the Stripe job description.

tasks.title: AWS Knowledge Consolidation and Practice Exams
tasks.description: Convert practical AWS experience into interview-ready fluency. Work the core SAA-C03 domains - IAM, VPC/networking, ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SQS, CloudWatch, cost models - condensing each service into a one-page cheat sheet that pairs the service with the exact thing built with it in Phase 3-4. Sit at least three timed practice exams and review every wrong answer down to the service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: Cheat sheets for 10+ AWS services each linked to a project artifact, three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log, targeting a consistent 80%+.

tasks.title: Docker and Redis Deep-Dive Q&A Drilling
tasks.description: Prepare tight, evidence-backed answers to the questions these gaps generate. For Docker: image layers and caching, multi-stage vs single-stage, non-root and distroless tradeoffs, Compose vs ECS orchestration, why digests over tags. For Redis: cache-aside vs write-through, TTL and invalidation, stampede and hot-key handling, persistence options (RDB/AOF) and when not to cache. Answer each with the artifact and number produced in Phases 2-4, and drill the ten hardest follow-ups aloud.
tasks.deliverable: A Docker and Redis Q&A bank of 25+ questions with model answers each tied to a specific project artifact and metric, plus a log of drilled follow-ups with corrected answers.

tasks.title: Mock Interviews and a Metrics-Backed STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop: a live coding round (add a tested endpoint to a running containerized app), a Docker/AWS/Redis deep dive, a system design round, and behavioral questions. Build a STAR bank of 8+ stories drawn from real Phase 1-4 work with hard numbers - 'cut image size from 1.2GB to 260MB', 'raised cache hit rate to 85% and cut p95 by 60%', 'diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop', 'deployed keyless via OIDC with a tested rollback'. Log every question asked and tighten the answer.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (one coding, one system design), a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist covering Docker, CI/CD, AWS, Redis and system design.

careerPlans.summary: A 12-week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a candidate targeting Full Stack Engineer at Stripe, sequenced to close the three priority gaps - Docker, AWS and Redis - while leveling up the two partial skills, CI/CD and System Design. Phase 1 builds the reproducible containerized dev/test loop, enforces a strict type-and-lint quality gate, and ships the first GitHub Actions pipeline. Phase 2 takes Docker to production bar: hardened non-root digest-pinned images, a six-service Compose topology with tier isolation, multi-arch registry delivery, an operations runbook, and reusable CI with a blocking scan gate. Phase 3 translates that into AWS as code - IAM and remote state, a VPC, ECS Fargate across two AZs behind an ALB, RDS, S3, Secrets Manager, ElastiCache Redis, and keyless OIDC blue/green delivery with a tested rollback. Phase 4 closes Redis and System Design with three real Redis patterns (cache-aside with invalidation, a token-bucket rate limiter, and SQS-backed idempotent workers), CloudWatch/OTel observability, autoscaling under k6 load to a stated SLO, and three design documents backed by the built system. Phase 5 converts it all into interview performance: timed system design drills, a case-study portfolio repository, AWS exam fluency, Docker/Redis deep-dive answers, and a metric-backed STAR bank. No task is generic - each names the gap it closes and produces an inspectable deliverable with numbers that can be defended in a Stripe interview loop.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Establish the reproducible, tested baseline that every later phase containerizes, deploys and scales. Phase 1 lands the first slice of the Docker gap by putting the application itself into containers, and the first slice of the CI/CD gap by attaching an automated quality gate to every pull request - a working build-test loop that makes the later Docker, AWS and Redis work verifiable instead of theoretical.

tasks.title: Build the Reference Full-Stack Service This Roadmap Will Ship
tasks.description: Create one non-trivial application that every later phase containerizes, deploys and scales: a payments/ledger-style REST API (Node.js + Express/Fastify or FastAPI) over PostgreSQL with an accounts table, a transactions table and an idempotency_keys table, plus a thin React/TypeScript dashboard that lists accounts and posts a transfer. Include token auth, request validation, pagination and structured error responses, and keep all configuration in environment variables.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub repository with API + PostgreSQL schema and migrations + minimal React dashboard, .env.example, idempotent seed script, and a README quickstart that boots on a clean machine.

tasks.title: First Multi-Stage Dockerfile for the API
tasks.description: Containerize the API with a multi-stage build split into named deps, build and runtime stages. Pin the base image to an exact version (not latest), install from the lockfile with a cached layer ordered before source copies, add a HEALTHCHECK, run the process as a non-root user, and write a .dockerignore covering node_modules, .git, tests and secrets. Measure the resulting image and record it next to a naive single-stage build of the same app.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile with named deps/build/runtime stages, pinned base image, non-root runtime user, HEALTHCHECK and .dockerignore, plus a README note comparing image size against a single-stage build.

tasks.title: docker-compose.yml: Whole Stack From One Command
tasks.description: Author a docker-compose.yml that brings up the frontend, API, PostgreSQL and the Redis service the later phases depend on, on a single named network, with a named volume for database data, healthchecks and depends_on service_healthy conditions, configuration injected through env_file, and a bind mount for hot reload in development. Prove a cold `docker compose up` works from a fresh clone and that `docker compose down` preserves seeded data.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml booting four services with healthchecks, named volume, isolated network and env_file, plus a verified one-command cold-start and a data-persistence test documented in the README.

tasks.title: Static Quality Gates and Pre-Commit Enforcement
tasks.description: Turn code quality into an enforced gate rather than a habit: enable strict TypeScript (strict: true, noImplicitAny, noUncheckedIndexedAccess) or mypy/pyright strict for the Python path, configure ESLint + Prettier (or Ruff + Black), add a Husky + lint-staged pre-commit hook and a commitlint conventional-commit rule. Expose lint, typecheck, format and test as scripts that run byte-identically in the local shell, inside the container image and in CI.
tasks.deliverable: Committed strict type configuration, linter and formatter configs, Husky pre-commit hook, commitlint config, and a documented script set that runs unchanged locally, in Docker and in the pipeline.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Test Suite with a Coverage Gate
tasks.description: Prove the app is testable in isolation the way a pipeline will test it. Add unit tests for the ledger logic and integration tests against a real PostgreSQL started on demand with Testcontainers (or a dedicated compose service), covering a happy-path transfer, a validation failure, an authorization failure, and a concurrent double-spend case that exercises the idempotency key. Enforce a coverage threshold of 60% or higher on the API layer inside the test command.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest/Jest + Supertest (or Pytest) suite with Testcontainers-backed integration tests for all four cases, a coverage report at or above 60% on the API layer, and a `test` script that provisions its own database with no pre-started container.

tasks.title: First GitHub Actions Pipeline: Lint + Test Matrix + Image Build
tasks.description: Close the first part of the zero-pipeline gap with the smallest useful workflow. On every pull request, run dependency install with caching, lint, typecheck and the full test suite, then build the Docker image without pushing. Use a version matrix, upload the coverage artifact, add a concurrency group that cancels superseded runs, and enable branch protection requiring the checks before merge. Open a deliberately failing PR, then fix it, to prove red-then-green.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions PR workflow with dependency caching, a lint/typecheck/test matrix and an image-build job, branch protection enabled, and a link or screenshots of the red-then-green PR run.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take the priority gaps from 'it runs' to production bar. Images become small, non-root and scanned; the local stack becomes six independently runnable services with environment overrides; and Redis - currently absent from the profile - is used as a real cache, a rate limiter and a job queue with measured results, not a tutorial. Everything built here is the substrate the AWS phase deploys.

tasks.title: Harden Production Images and Scan the Supply Chain
tasks.description: Rebuild both images for production: distroless or slim base pinned by digest, a runtime stage that copies only build artifacts and production dependencies, non-root user, read-only root filesystem where the app allows it, multi-arch build, OCI metadata labels, and layer ordering so dependency layers cache across code changes. Scan with Trivy, generate an SBOM with Syft, remove every baked-in secret and confirm none leaks into image history, then inspect layers with dive.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfiles, a runtime image under 300MB running as non-root on a pinned digest, .dockerignore, a Syft SBOM, a Trivy scan report with no HIGH/CRITICAL findings, and a dev-vs-production size and layer comparison.

tasks.title: Six-Service Orchestration with Dev/Prod Compose Overrides
tasks.description: Model a realistic distributed system locally: frontend, API, background worker, PostgreSQL, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy terminating TLS and routing to the API. Define one base compose file plus dev and prod override files, use separate front-end and back-end networks so the database tier is unreachable from the public tier, add healthcheck-based depends_on, per-service CPU/memory limits and JSON-file log rotation, then seed and verify state survives a down/up cycle.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml plus dev/prod override files orchestrating six services with tier-isolated networks, healthchecks, resource limits and log rotation, a verified volume-persistence test, and a service-topology diagram.

tasks.title: Redis Deep Dive: Data Structures, TTL Policy and Cache-Aside
tasks.description: Close the Redis gap from first principles. Work through the core data structures hands-on (strings, hashes, sorted sets, sets, streams, expiry) in a scratch CLI, then implement a cache-aside layer for the hot read endpoint (account balance and recent transactions) with a documented key-naming convention, an explicit TTL policy, key versioning for safe schema change, write-time invalidation, and stampede protection via a soft-TTL refresh or a short-lived lock. Instrument hit/miss counters and benchmark the endpoint with and without the cache.
tasks.deliverable: Cache-aside layer with a written key-naming and TTL policy, a documented invalidation strategy, a hit-rate plus p95-latency benchmark before and after, and a short note on hot-key and cache-stampede handling.

tasks.title: Redis as Rate Limiter and Job Queue
tasks.description: Use Redis for two more production jobs. First, a token-bucket or sliding-window rate limiter on the public API implemented as an atomic Lua script with per-API-key limits, returning 429 with Retry-After. Second, move slow work (statements, notifications, report generation) to a background worker that consumes queued jobs from Redis Streams or a queue with visibility timeout, using idempotency keys, bounded retries with backoff, and a dead-letter path; track job status in Redis. Run the worker as its own containerized service in the Phase 2 compose stack.
tasks.deliverable: Atomic Redis rate limiter with tests proving 429, burst handling and per-key isolation, plus a containerized background worker with idempotency keys, retry/backoff policy, dead-letter handling and queue-depth metrics.

tasks.title: Container Debugging and Runtime Operations Runbook
tasks.description: Learn to operate containers, not just build them. Deliberately reproduce five incidents - a crash loop from a bad entrypoint, an OOM kill under a memory limit, a host port conflict, a Docker-network DNS resolution failure, and a volume permission error caused by the non-root user - and diagnose each with docker logs, exec, stats, inspect, events and docker compose. Add SIGTERM handling for graceful shutdown and record before/after CPU and memory behaviour under applied limits.
tasks.deliverable: Container debugging runbook covering five reproduced incidents (symptom, diagnosis command, root cause, fix), a SIGTERM graceful-shutdown demonstration, and a resource-limit before/after stats report.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by running the Phase 2 containers on managed infrastructure provisioned as code: a Terraform baseline, a VPC with private subnets and an ALB in front of ECS Fargate, managed PostgreSQL, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis, a statically hosted frontend, and an OIDC-keyless pipeline that deploys with blue/green and a tested rollback - the level-up half of the CI/CD gap.

tasks.title: AWS Baseline as Code: Least-Privilege IAM, Budgets and Remote State
tasks.description: Set up a clean AWS foundation rather than clicking in the console: a dedicated non-root admin identity with MFA, a least-privilege deployment role, AWS CLI v2 profiles, and a billing budget alarm. Provision the state backbone with Terraform (or AWS CDK) in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking and environment separation via workspaces or var-files. Pin provider versions and document how to destroy every resource to avoid orphaned spend.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles/policies, a budget alarm and an S3 + DynamoDB remote-state backend, a documented least-privilege deployment policy, a pinned provider lock file, and a screenshot of the active budget alarm.

tasks.title: Deploy the Containers to ECS Fargate behind an ALB
tasks.description: Push the hardened images to Amazon ECR and run them on ECS Fargate across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks and connection draining. Place the tasks in private subnets with a NAT gateway for egress, expose only the ALB through a security group, and define the VPC, public/private subnets, route tables, internet/NAT gateways and listener rules entirely in Terraform. ECS task roles are separate from the execution role - configure both and explain the distinction.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned VPC (public/private subnets, route tables, IGW/NAT), ECR repositories, an ECS Fargate service on 2+ AZs and an ALB with health checks, plus a reachable public URL and a deployed-architecture diagram.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Secrets and ElastiCache Redis on AWS
tasks.description: Move off local containers onto managed services. Provision RDS PostgreSQL in private subnets whose security group accepts traffic only from the ECS service security group, a versioned S3 bucket for uploads with a least-privilege bucket policy and private access, Secrets Manager entries for database credentials injected into the task at start, and an ElastiCache Redis cluster in a subnet group reachable only from the app tier. Run the migrations against RDS and point the Phase 2 cache, rate limiter and queue at ElastiCache, proving they work in the cloud and not just on localhost.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS PostgreSQL + S3 + Secrets Manager + ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining, evidence of a migration and an S3 upload, and an application screenshot showing a cache hit served from ElastiCache.

tasks.title: Keyless CI/CD to AWS with Blue/Green Deploy and Rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery to AWS with no stored access keys. Configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a scoped trust policy limited to this repository and branch, then extend the Phase 1 pipeline to run tests, build and tag the image with the commit SHA, push to ECR, render a new ECS task definition and deploy with a rolling strategy first and CodeDeploy blue/green second, waiting for service stability. Add a GitHub Environment approval gate for production, post-deploy smoke tests against the live URL, and a rollback job that redeploys the previous task revision.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based deploy workflow (test -> build -> ECR -> ECS rolling then blue/green), the IAM trust policy, a GitHub Environment approval gate, and logs proving both a successful deploy and a successful rollback.

tasks.title: Ship the Frontend: S3 + CloudFront with Cache-Aware Releases
tasks.description: Deploy the React dashboard as static assets: a versioned S3 origin bucket with public access blocked, a CloudFront distribution using Origin Access Control, an ACM certificate and custom domain, and cache policies that give hashed assets long TTLs while index.html stays revalidated. Add a CI step that builds the frontend, syncs with a delete flag, and invalidates only the changed entry points, with the API base URL injected per environment at build time.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for S3 + CloudFront (OAC, ACM, cache policies, custom domain) with a CI build-and-sync step and a targeted invalidation job, plus proof of a release that serves no stale assets.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives'. Observability answers what the system is doing; autoscaling validated under load proves it holds a stated SLO; Redis is operated with real persistence, eviction and failover decisions; the System Design gap is closed with written, defensible designs; and multi-environment cost and disaster-recovery discipline make the whole system repeatable.

tasks.title: Observability: Structured Logs, Metrics, Alarms and Tracing
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end. Emit structured JSON logs carrying a request ID that flows from the ALB through the API into the worker, ship them to CloudWatch Logs, and publish custom latency and business metrics (transfers processed, cache hit rate, queue depth) using the embedded metric format. Build a CloudWatch dashboard (request rate, p95 latency, 5xx rate, ECS CPU/memory, Redis evictions, queue depth) with alarms on error-rate and latency thresholds and on unhealthy ALB targets. Add OpenTelemetry tracing across ALB -> API -> worker and follow one request end to end.
tasks.deliverable: Request-ID logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, three or more actionable CloudWatch alarms, one OpenTelemetry trace spanning the request path, and a one-page runbook mapping each alarm to a first diagnostic step.

tasks.title: Autoscaling Validated by Load Testing to a Defined SLO
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking on CPU and on ALB request-count-per-target, then drive load with k6 (or Locust) against the deployed endpoint across a ramp, a steady-state and a spike scenario. Capture p95 latency, throughput and error rate before and after scale-out; tune target values, cooldowns and min/max task counts until the stated SLO (for example p95 under 300ms at 200 requests per second) holds. Identify the first bottleneck - typically the database connection pool - and document the fix you applied.
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies on CPU and request count with tuned min/max, a k6/Locust script and report (throughput, p95, error rate) showing scale-out, and a bottleneck analysis note with the fix that was applied.

tasks.title: Operate Redis in Production: Persistence, Eviction and Failover
tasks.description: Stop treating Redis as an in-memory black box. Choose and justify an eviction policy per workload (allkeys-lru for the cache, noeviction for queue or rate-limit keys with a TTL safety net), set maxmemory and monitor evicted_keys, keyspace hit rate and memory fragmentation, and reason explicitly about AOF versus RDB persistence for a cache versus a queue. Add a replica with automatic failover in ElastiCache, use connection pooling and timeouts in the app so Redis latency cannot cascade, and run a failover drill to measure the impact on the API.
tasks.deliverable: Documented Redis configuration per workload (cache, rate limiter, queue) with chosen maxmemory-policy and persistence settings, a keyspace and memory monitoring view, a failover drill report with measured error rate and recovery time, and evidence of graceful degradation when Redis is unavailable.

tasks.title: System Design Fluency: Three Written Designs with Tradeoff Tables
tasks.description: Turn the implementation work in Phases 2-4 into design language. Write three design documents - a high-throughput payments API with idempotency and exactly-once processing concerns, a multi-tenant SaaS backend with isolation and noisy-neighbour concerns, and an image-upload and processing pipeline with async work and backpressure - each covering API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy and invalidation, queueing and retries, consistency tradeoffs, AWS hosting topology, capacity estimates, scaling limits and a failure-mode table (timeout, retry, circuit breaker). Back every decision with something you actually measured, and include a tradeoff table comparing SQL, Redis and queue options for each read and write path.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design documents with architecture diagrams, tradeoff tables, capacity/SLO estimates, a failure-mode table, and a self-critique list of the follow-up questions an interviewer would push on.

tasks.title: Multi-Environment Terraform, Cost Control and Disaster Recovery
tasks.description: Make the infrastructure repeatable and affordable. Parameterize Terraform into dev/staging/prod with environment-specific sizing, stand up a second environment end to end, and confirm the same pipeline promotes a build between them without manual edits. Produce a Cost Explorer analysis of the running stack and apply at least three concrete optimizations (rightsize Fargate task CPU/memory from observed utilization, adjust the RDS instance class and storage, and quantify the savings from the Redis cache and from S3 lifecycle rules). Document and test an RTO/RPO backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-environment Terraform (dev/staging/prod) with a deployed staging stack, a cost analysis with at least three applied optimizations and their actual dollar deltas, and a tested backup/restore DR runbook with measured recovery time.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert Phases 1-4 artifacts into interview performance for the Full Stack Engineer loop at Stripe. Every deliverable becomes a story, a diagram and a defensible decision; system design practice and mock rounds build verbal fluency; and a final gap audit confirms that Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD and System Design are each defended by something you built and measured.

tasks.title: Timed System Design Drills with Whiteboard Diagrams
tasks.description: Convert the Phase 4 design documents into verbal fluency under time pressure. Run at least six timed 35-40 minute prompts alone and two with a peer or on recorded video: a URL shortener, a feed/notification system, a payment-idempotency service, a rate-limited public API, an analytics ingestion pipeline and a multi-tenant SaaS API. For each, clarify requirements, estimate scale, sketch boxes and arrows, choose a data model, place caching and queues, name the bottleneck and the failure mode, then write out the answers you would give to the three hardest follow-ups.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design drill packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, tradeoff decisions, follow-up answers) plus two recorded mock design sessions with a reviewed list of recurring weak points.

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Architecture Writeup and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate the code, Terraform, compose files, CI/CD workflows, tests, SBOM and scan reports and runbooks into one clean public repository whose README reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, a `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment guide, observability screenshots, load-test numbers, cost notes and the rollback runbook. Then write a RESUME.md that maps each project feature to a concrete resume bullet, and rewrite prior experience to foreground the transferable evidence - automated pipelines, containerized delivery, infrastructure as code, measured performance work.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with an architecture diagram, container quickstart, AWS deployment and rollback guides, dashboards and screenshots, a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping, and a rewritten resume section reviewed against the Full Stack Engineer target.

tasks.title: AWS Knowledge Consolidation and Timed Practice Exams
tasks.description: Convert hands-on AWS experience into exam-grade, interview-ready fluency. Work the core SAA-C03 domains - IAM, VPC and networking, ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SQS/SNS, CloudWatch and cost models - condensing each service into a one-page cheat sheet that pairs the service with the exact thing you built with it and the failure scenario it solves. Sit at least three timed practice exams and review every wrong answer down to a service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: Cheat sheets for 10+ AWS services each linked to a project artifact, three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log, targeting a consistent 80%+ before scheduling the real exam.

tasks.title: Mock Interviews and a Metrics-Backed STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop: a live coding round (add a tested, containerized endpoint to the running app), a Docker/AWS/Redis depth round, a system design round and behavioral questions. Build a STAR bank of at least eight stories drawn from real Phases 1-4 work and carried by numbers - 'cut the runtime image from 1.2GB to 220MB', 'diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop from container stats', 'raised cache hit rate to 85% and cut p95 by 60%', 'replaced a manual approval step with an OIDC-gated blue/green deploy'. Log every question asked and tighten each answer.
tasks.deliverable: A STAR story bank of 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (one coding, one system design), a question log with revised answers, and a readiness checklist covering Docker, CI/CD, AWS, Redis and system design.

tasks.title: Close-Out Gap Audit and Targeted Remediation
tasks.description: Score each of the five gaps - Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD and System Design - against the interview bar for a Full Stack Engineer using evidence, not confidence: for each gap list the artifact that demonstrates it and the hardest question you still cannot answer cleanly. Take the two lowest-scoring gaps and spend a focused block closing them with a new small artifact (for example a Redis cluster-mode or pipelining exercise, or a Docker buildkit cache-mount optimization), then re-score.
tasks.deliverable: A scored five-gap audit mapping each gap to its demonstrating artifact and open questions, a remediation log for the two weakest gaps with the new artifacts produced, and an updated readiness score with a go/no-go note on applying.

careerPlans.summary: A 10-week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a candidate targeting Full Stack Engineer at Stripe, built around the three priority gaps - Docker, AWS and Redis - and the two partial skills to level up, CI/CD and System Design. Each phase feeds the next: Phase 1 creates a real full-stack service, containers it and attaches the first quality gate and CI pipeline; Phase 2 hardens images, orchestrates six services with Compose overrides and puts Redis to work as a cache, rate limiter and job queue with measured results; Phase 3 deploys those containers to AWS provisioned as code - Terraform, VPC, ECS Fargate, ALB, RDS, S3, Secrets Manager, ElastiCache and CloudFront - with a keyless OIDC blue/green pipeline and a tested rollback; Phase 4 makes the system observable, autoscaled to a stated SLO under load, operated with real Redis persistence and failover decisions, and documented through written system designs plus multi-environment cost and disaster-recovery discipline; Phase 5 converts every artifact into timed design drills, a case-study portfolio repository, AWS exam fluency and metric-backed STAR stories, closing with a scored gap audit. No task is generic: each names the specific gap it closes and produces an inspectable deliverable - a hardened Dockerfile, a compose override set, a Redis benchmark, a Terraform stack, a blue/green workflow, a load-test report or a design document.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Establish the reference full-stack artifact every later phase builds on: a real React/TypeScript + Node.js app on PostgreSQL that runs reproducibly, is covered by automated tests, and passes a lint/typecheck gate. Docker enters here at the fundamentals level so the app has one reproducible entry point before any cloud work begins.

tasks.title: Build the reference full-stack app (React + TypeScript + Node API + PostgreSQL)
tasks.description: Create the substrate for the whole roadmap: a payments-flavoured app (transactions CRUD + a dashboard view) with a React + TypeScript frontend, a Node.js (Fastify or Express) REST API, and PostgreSQL. Include real auth (session or JWT), input validation, and at least three REST resources with pagination and error envelopes. Write a README quickstart with exact install/run steps and a .env.example.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repo with React/TS frontend, Node REST API and PostgreSQL schema (migrations + seed data), a documented one-command local boot, and a .env.example covering every required variable

tasks.title: Write the first multi-stage Dockerfile for the API
tasks.description: Containerize the Node API with a multi-stage build (deps -> build -> runtime), a pinned Node base image tag, lockfile-based install, non-root runtime user, a HEALTHCHECK hitting /healthz, and a .dockerignore. Build the same app with a naive single-stage file first and record the size difference so the caching story is concrete.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile for the API (non-root user, HEALTHCHECK, .dockerignore) plus a README note with measured before/after image sizes and an explanation of which layer caches on a code-only change

tasks.title: One-command local stack with docker-compose
tasks.description: Author docker-compose.yml bringing up frontend, API and PostgreSQL on one user-defined network with healthchecks and depends_on conditions, config injected via env_file, and database state persisted in a named volume. Add bind mounts for hot reload in development. Verify a cold start works on a clean checkout with no pre-started database.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml with three services, healthchecks, named volume and hot-reload bind mounts; a verified one-command cold start documented in the README plus a container-network diagram

tasks.title: Strict types, lint, and pre-commit quality gate
tasks.description: Turn on TypeScript strict mode (strict: true, noImplicitAny), shared DTO interfaces for the API request/response envelope, ESLint + Prettier, and a Husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook with commitlint. Expose lint, typecheck, format and test as npm scripts so the identical commands run locally, inside Docker, and in CI.
tasks.deliverable: Committed strict tsconfig, ESLint/Prettier/commitlint configs, a working pre-commit hook, and a `tsc --noEmit` build passing with zero type errors on the shared API types

tasks.title: First GitHub Actions CI pipeline: lint, typecheck, test, build image
tasks.description: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml running on every pull request: dependency install with cache, lint, typecheck, unit + integration tests against a containerized Postgres service, then a Docker image build (no push) with buildx layer caching. Upload the coverage artifact and enable branch protection requiring the checks before merge. Deliberately open a red PR, fix it, and capture both runs.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with lint/typecheck/test matrix and an image-build job, branch protection enabled, and links/screenshots of a red PR run and the green run after the fix

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take Docker from 'it runs' to production bar and close the CI/CD gap from change-ticket discipline to owned pipeline authorship. Images get small, non-root and scanned; the local stack becomes a six-service system including Redis; and the pipeline becomes a reusable, environment-aware delivery system with smoke tests and one-click rollback.

tasks.title: Hardened production images with supply-chain scanning and SBOM
tasks.description: Rebuild both images for production: distroless/slim base pinned by digest, only build artifacts copied into the runtime stage, non-root user, OCI labels, multi-arch builds via buildx, and no baked-in secrets. Scan with Trivy, generate an SBOM with Syft, and inspect layer composition with dive.
tasks.deliverable: Production Dockerfiles producing runtime images under 300MB running as non-root on pinned digests, a Trivy scan report with zero HIGH/CRITICAL findings, a generated SBOM, and a dev-vs-prod image size/layer comparison

tasks.title: Six-service orchestration with dev/prod compose overrides and Redis
