tasks.description: Model a realistic distributed system locally: frontend, API, background worker, PostgreSQL, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy. Use a base compose file plus dev/prod overrides, tier-isolated networks (public tier vs data tier), healthcheck-based depends_on, CPU/memory limits and JSON-file log rotation. Seed the database and confirm state survives a down/up cycle.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml plus override files orchestrating six services with tier isolation, healthchecks, resource limits and log rotation; a volume-persistence test result and a service-topology diagram

tasks.title: Redis fundamentals: cache-aside on a hot read endpoint
tasks.description: Introduce Redis properly rather than as a tutorial. Add a cache-aside layer in front of the hottest read endpoint (e.g. account balance / transaction list): documented key-naming convention, explicit TTL policy, cache-key versioning, stampede protection (single-flight or probabilistic early expiry), and correct invalidation on writes. Choose data structures deliberately (string vs hash vs sorted set) and justify each.
tasks.deliverable: Cache-aside implementation with a documented key/TTL policy, an invalidation-on-write path, and a benchmark report showing measured hit rate and p95 latency before vs after caching under a warm cache

tasks.title: Reusable parameterized CI with scanning gates and PR preview environments
tasks.description: Level up from one workflow to a CI system: extract a reusable workflow (workflow_call) plus composite actions for setup/test/build so jobs stop duplicating YAML. Add path filters, concurrency groups that cancel superseded runs, dependency and container scanning jobs that fail the build on HIGH/CRITICAL, buildx layer caching, and a short-lived per-PR preview environment behind a GitHub Environment with required reviewers.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable GitHub Actions workflow + composite actions used by CI, concurrency groups, scanning jobs gating merges, a working PR preview environment URL, and a documented .github/ structure diagram

tasks.title: Continuous delivery with smoke tests, environment gates and one-click rollback
tasks.description: Extend CI into delivery: on merge to main build and tag the image with the commit SHA, push to GHCR, deploy to a hosted environment, run post-deploy smoke tests against the live URL, and notify on failure. Add a rollback job that redeploys the previous image tag without prompting, and track the four DORA metrics from at least three real deploys. Turn the manual change-control rigor of a release ticket into automated, evidence-generating checks.
tasks.deliverable: Deploy workflow (build -> registry -> deploy -> smoke test -> notify) with a tested rollback job, a written release/rollback runbook, and a DORA metrics table from three deploys including one deliberate failure and recovery

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the Phase 2 containers to managed AWS infrastructure provisioned entirely as code: IAM, VPC, ECS Fargate behind an ALB, RDS, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis, with OIDC-based keyless delivery and blue/green deploys. No resource is created by clicking in the console.

tasks.title: AWS account baseline as code: IAM, budgets, remote state
tasks.description: Establish a safe AWS foundation: a non-root admin identity with MFA, a least-privilege deployment role, AWS CLI v2 profiles, and a billing budget alarm. Provision everything with Terraform in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB state locking, and tag all resources for cost attribution.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles/policies, a budget alarm and an S3+DynamoDB remote state backend; a documented least-privilege deployment policy; and a screenshot of the active budget alarm

tasks.title: Push images to ECR and run them on ECS Fargate behind an ALB
tasks.description: Provision a VPC with public/private subnets, route tables and a NAT gateway in Terraform; create an ECR repo and an ECS Fargate service running the API across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks. Tasks live in private subnets; only the ALB is publicly reachable, through a security group that accepts 443 from the internet. Wire the frontend to the service.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned VPC + ECR + ECS Fargate service on 2+ AZs + ALB with health checks; a reachable public URL serving the app, plus a deployed-architecture diagram showing subnet, route and security-group flow

tasks.title: Managed data layer: RDS Postgres, S3, Secrets Manager, ElastiCache Redis
tasks.description: Replace local containers with managed services: RDS Postgres in private subnets whose security group accepts traffic only from the ECS task security group; a versioned S3 bucket for uploads with a least-privilege bucket policy and presigned-URL uploads; Secrets Manager entries injected at task start; and an ElastiCache Redis cluster. Point the app's Redis client at ElastiCache and prove the cache-aside path serves hits in the cloud, not just on localhost.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Postgres + S3 + Secrets Manager + ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining; a successful migration against RDS; a presigned S3 upload demo; and app evidence of a cache hit served from ElastiCache

tasks.title: Keyless GitHub Actions to AWS with blue/green deploy and rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery to AWS without static keys: configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a tightly scoped trust policy and permissions. Extend the Phase 2 pipeline to build, push to ECR, render a new ECS task definition, and deploy rolling first, then blue/green via CodeDeploy, waiting for service stability before shifting traffic. Add a manual approval gate for production and a tested rollback to the previous task revision.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS rolling and blue/green), the IAM trust policy, a GitHub Environment approval gate, and logs proving both a successful blue/green cutover and a successful rollback

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives': full observability, measured autoscaling, and the two remaining gaps closed together - Redis as a production dependency (cache, rate limiter, queue-backed worker) and System Design as the vocabulary for caching, consistency, async and failure tradeoffs that have now actually been implemented.

tasks.title: Observability: structured logs, metrics, alarms and distributed tracing
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end. Emit structured JSON logs with request IDs, ship them to CloudWatch Logs, and publish custom latency and business metrics via the CloudWatch SDK or embedded metric format. Build a dashboard (request rate, p95 latency, error rate, ECS CPU/memory, Redis hit rate) with alarms on error-rate, latency and unhealthy targets. Add OpenTelemetry tracing across the ALB -> API -> worker path.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, three or more alarms with notification targets, and an OTel trace of a single request traversing the ALB, API and worker

tasks.title: Redis in production: token-bucket rate limiting and an async queue worker
tasks.description: Extend Redis from cache to two more production uses. First, a Redis token-bucket (or sliding-window) rate limiter on the public API, with per-API-key limits returned via 429 and Retry-After. Second, move slow work (receipt/PDF generation, email, webhook delivery) to a background worker consuming an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue, idempotency keys and retry-with-backoff, using Redis for job status and progress. Run the worker as its own ECS service with its own image.
tasks.deliverable: A Redis rate limiter with an automated test proving 429 behaviour, and an SQS-backed worker deployed as a separate ECS service with DLQ, idempotency keys, and a before/after latency benchmark for the async path

tasks.title: Autoscaling and load testing to a defined SLO
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target, then drive load with k6 (or Locust) against the deployed endpoint across a warm and cold cache. Capture p95 latency, throughput and error rate before and after scale-out, tune target values, cooldowns and min/max task counts to hit a stated SLO, and document the observed bottleneck (usually the database connection pool) and the fix.
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies for CPU and request count with tuned min/max, a k6/Locust script and load-test report (throughput, p95, error rate, cold vs warm) showing scale-out, and a written bottleneck analysis

tasks.title: System design fluency: caching, queues, consistency and failure modes
tasks.description: Turn implementation into design language. Write three design documents - a high-throughput payments API with idempotency and exactly-once processing, a multi-tenant SaaS backend, and an image-upload/processing pipeline - each covering API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy and invalidation, queueing and backpressure, consistency tradeoffs, hosting topology on AWS, capacity/SLO estimates and a failure-mode table (retry, timeout, circuit breaker, DLQ). Back every decision with something actually built: 'Redis cache-aside with versioned keys and a 60s TTL because we measured X'.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design docs with architecture diagrams, SQL-vs-Redis-vs-queue tradeoff tables per read/write path, capacity estimates, a failure-mode table, and a self-critique list of where an interviewer would push back

tasks.title: Multi-environment Terraform, cost control and disaster recovery
tasks.description: Make the infrastructure repeatable and affordable. Parameterize Terraform into dev/staging/prod workspaces or var-files with environment-specific sizing, stand up staging end to end, and confirm the same pipeline promotes between environments. Produce a Cost Explorer analysis with three applied optimizations (rightsizing Fargate, RDS instance class, cache savings) and document an RTO/RPO backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3, then test a restore.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-environment Terraform (dev/staging/prod) with a deployed staging stack, a cost analysis with three applied optimizations and actual dollar deltas, and a tested backup/restore DR runbook with measured recovery time

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the Phase 1-4 artifacts into interview performance for the Full Stack Engineer loop at Stripe. Every deliverable becomes a story, a diagram and a defensible decision: a portfolio repo read as an engineering case study, timed system design drills, AWS knowledge consolidation, and metric-backed STAR stories with recorded mocks.

tasks.title: Timed system design drills with whiteboard diagrams
tasks.description: Convert the Phase 4 design docs into spoken fluency. Run at least six timed 35-40 minute mock prompts alone and two recorded with a peer: a URL shortener, a feed/notification system, a payment-idempotency service, a rate-limited public API, an analytics ingestion pipeline, and a multi-tenant SaaS. For each: clarify requirements, estimate scale, sketch boxes and arrows, choose a data model, place caching and queues, name the bottleneck and the failure mode, then write the answers you would give to the three hardest follow-ups.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design drill packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, tradeoff decisions, follow-up answers) plus two recorded mock sessions with a reviewed list of recurring weak points

tasks.title: Portfolio repository as an engineering case study and resume mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate the code, Dockerfiles, Terraform, compose files, CI/CD workflows, tests, scan reports and runbooks into one clean public repository whose README reads like a case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment guide, observability screenshots, load-test numbers, cost notes and the rollback runbook. Then write RESUME.md mapping each project feature to a resume bullet targeting the Full Stack Engineer role.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, container quickstart, AWS deploy + rollback guides, dashboard and load-test screenshots, and a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping reviewed against the target role

tasks.title: AWS knowledge consolidation and timed practice exams
tasks.description: Convert practical AWS experience into exam-grade, interview-ready fluency. Work the core SAA-C03 domains - IAM, VPC/networking, ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SQS, CloudWatch, cost models - condensing each service into a one-page cheat sheet that pairs the service with the thing you actually built with it. Sit at least three timed practice exams and review every wrong answer back to a service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: Cheat sheets for 10+ AWS services each linked to a project artifact, and three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log targeting a consistent 80%+ before scheduling the real exam

tasks.title: Mock interviews and a metrics-backed STAR story bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop: a live coding round (add a tested endpoint to the running containerized app), a Docker/AWS/Redis deep dive, a system design round, and behavioral questions. Build a STAR bank of 8+ stories from real Phase 1-4 work with hard numbers - 'cut image size from 1.2GB to 220MB', 'cut p95 from 420ms to 90ms at 85% cache hit rate', 'diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop', 'automated an approval into an OIDC-gated blue/green pipeline' - and log every question asked with a tightened answer.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (one coding, one system design), a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist covering Docker, CI/CD, AWS, Redis and system design

careerPlans.summary: A 10-week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a Full Stack Engineer (Stripe) target, built to close five specific gaps: Docker (missing), AWS (missing), Redis (missing), CI/CD (partial) and System Design (partial). The phases feed each other. Phase 1 builds the reference React/TypeScript + Node + PostgreSQL app, containerizes it with a first multi-stage Dockerfile, adds strict types/lint/test gates and a first GitHub Actions pipeline. Phase 2 takes Docker to production bar - hardened non-root images, Trivy/SBOM scanning, six-service compose with tier isolation - introduces Redis cache-aside on a hot read path, and turns CI into reusable pipelines with scanning gates, PR previews and a smoke-tested deploy with rollback. Phase 3 closes AWS entirely as code: IAM and budgets, VPC + ECR + ECS Fargate behind an ALB across two AZs, RDS/S3/Secrets Manager/ElastiCache, and keyless OIDC blue/green delivery. Phase 4 adds production depth - CloudWatch/OTel observability, Redis rate limiting plus an SQS-backed worker, autoscaling proven under k6 load, three written system design docs, and multi-environment cost/DR discipline. Phase 5 converts all of it into timed design drills, a case-study portfolio repo, AWS exam fluency and metric-backed STAR stories. Every task names the exact gap it closes and produces an inspectable artifact - a Dockerfile, a compose file, a Terraform stack, a benchmark, a design doc or a pipeline run - so progress is provable rather than claimed.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Create the one reference full-stack application every later phase will containerize, deploy, and scale, and lock a quality gate around it. This is not a tutorial exercise: the app needs enough surface (auth, CRUD, a hot read path, a slow write path) for Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD, and system design work to have something real to bite into. CI/CD starts here as a partial skill being leveled up from zero automation.

tasks.title: Build the reference full-stack app that Phases 2-5 will target
tasks.description: Build a single non-trivial application: React/Next.js frontend + Node/Express (or FastAPI) backend + PostgreSQL, with real auth, CRUD on a core resource, one read-heavy endpoint and one slow endpoint (email/report/image work). Keep it a monorepo with /apps/web, /apps/api, /apps/worker and a shared types package so it can later become 3 independently deployable containers. Deliberately include the seam where Redis will be inserted in Phase 4: the read-heavy endpoint must go straight to Postgres with no cache, and record its baseline p95 latency.
tasks.deliverable: Public monorepo with frontend, API, worker skeleton, Postgres schema + migrations, .env.example, README quickstart, and a recorded baseline latency number for the hot read endpoint.

tasks.title: Enforce strict code-quality gates across the monorepo
tasks.description: Turn on TypeScript strict mode (or mypy/pyright strict for Python), configure ESLint + Prettier (or Ruff + Black), and add Husky + lint-staged pre-commit hooks with commitlint. Expose the exact same commands as `lint`, `typecheck`, `format` and `test` scripts at repo root so the identical command runs on a laptop, inside a container, and in CI - one source of truth, no environment-specific variants. Fix every existing violation rather than suppressing rules.
tasks.deliverable: Committed strict tsconfig/mypy config, ESLint/Prettier/Ruff config, Husky pre-commit hook, commitlint config, and a root script manifest with zero lint and zero type errors.

tasks.title: Write a test suite that runs with no pre-started services
tasks.description: Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests that spin up a real Postgres via Testcontainers (or a dedicated compose service) on the fly, so the suite is hermetic and pipeline-ready. Cover one happy path, one validation failure, and one authorization failure on the core resource. Target 60%+ coverage on the API layer and make the coverage report an artifact rather than a console print.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest/Jest + Supertest (or Pytest) suite with Testcontainers-backed integration tests, a `test` script requiring no pre-started database, and a coverage report artifact exceeding 60% on the API layer.

tasks.title: Stand up the first GitHub Actions pipeline with a lint/test matrix
tasks.description: Close the zero-automation gap with the smallest useful pipeline: a GitHub Actions workflow on every pull request that caches dependencies, runs typecheck, lint and the hermetic test suite across a Node/Python version matrix, uploads the coverage artifact, and builds the Docker images without pushing. Enable branch protection requiring these checks before merge so the gate is real.
tasks.deliverable: GitHub Actions workflow with a lint/typecheck/test matrix and an image-build job, branch protection enabled on main, and a link to a green pull-request run.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Deep dive on Docker, the highest-priority missing skill, plus a first hands-on Redis service so the cache dependency exists locally before it exists in the cloud. Images get small, non-root and scanned; the single app becomes six independently deployable services with dev/prod overrides; CI grows into a reusable pipeline that scans and publishes images; and the candidate learns to operate containers under failure, not just build them.

tasks.title: Write multi-stage Dockerfiles and a six-service docker-compose stack
tasks.description: Containerize web, api and worker with dependency-ordered multi-stage builds (deps -> build -> runtime), then orchestrate six services with Compose: web, api, worker, Postgres, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy. Use a custom bridge network, internal-only ports for the data tier, named volumes for Postgres and Redis data, healthcheck-based `depends_on`, restart policies, CPU/memory limits and JSON-file log rotation. Add bind mounts for hot reload in dev only, and confirm state survives `docker compose down` / `up`. Include Redis and prove the worker can connect to it with a real ping-and-set round trip - the first concrete Redis rep.
tasks.deliverable: Three multi-stage Dockerfiles plus docker-compose.yml orchestrating six services with tier isolation, healthchecks, resource limits, log rotation and named volumes; a verified Redis ping from the worker; and a service-topology diagram.

tasks.title: Split Compose into base, dev and prod overrides with configuration parity
tasks.description: Refactor the single compose file into a base file plus dev and prod override files, driven by .env files, so the same Dockerfiles run locally and in a production-like mode. In the prod profile use only built images (no bind mounts), drop the reverse-proxy port exposure to 80/443, force restart policies, and inject secrets via env_file rather than literals. Prove both profiles boot from a clean checkout with a single documented command.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml + docker-compose.dev.yml + docker-compose.prod.yml, an .env.example per profile, a documented cold-start command for each, and a diff note of the configuration differences.

tasks.title: Harden images and scan the supply chain
tasks.description: Rebuild runtime images on slim/alpine or distroless bases pinned to exact digests, run as a non-root user, copy only build artifacts into the final stage, and add a complete .dockerignore plus OCI labels. Order layers so dependency layers cache across code changes. Generate an SBOM with Syft, scan with Trivy, remove any baked-in secret, and measure before/after size with `docker image ls` and `dive`.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfiles producing sub-300MB runtime images running as non-root on pinned digests, a .dockerignore, an SBOM, a Trivy report with all HIGH/CRITICAL resolved or justified, and a dev-vs-prod size/layer comparison.

tasks.title: Grow CI into a reusable, environment-aware pipeline
tasks.description: Promote the Phase 1 workflow into a real CI system: extract a `workflow_call` reusable workflow plus composite actions for setup/test/build so jobs stop duplicating YAML, add path filters, concurrency groups that cancel superseded runs, buildx layer caching, and dependency plus container scanning jobs that fail the build on HIGH/CRITICAL. Inject configuration through GitHub Environments with a required reviewer on the protected environment, and connect Docker/GHCR packaging to the workflow so images are versioned by commit SHA.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable reusable-ci.yml + composite actions, path filters, concurrency groups, buildx caching, security-scanning jobs gating merges, an Environment approval gate, and a tagged image published to a registry.

tasks.title: Reproduce and diagnose five container incidents
tasks.description: Learn to operate containers, not only build them. Deliberately reproduce five failures - crash loop from a bad entrypoint, OOM kill under a memory limit, port conflict, Compose-network DNS failure, and volume permission error from a non-root user - and diagnose each using docker logs, exec, stats, inspect, events and compose. Add SIGTERM handling for graceful shutdown and capture before/after `docker stats` under applied CPU and memory limits.
tasks.deliverable: Container debugging runbook with five reproduced incidents (symptom, diagnostic command, root cause, fix), a SIGTERM graceful-shutdown demo, and a resource-limit before/after stats report.

tasks.title: Redis fundamentals driven by the running compose stack
tasks.description: Build working Redis literacy against the local container rather than a toy REPL. Using redis-cli and the app client: exercise strings, hashes, sorted sets and TTLs; implement a cached key with explicit expiry and inspect it with TTL/OBJECT ENCODING; measure the difference between a Postgres query and a Redis GET for the hot endpoint; configure maxmemory with an LRU eviction policy and observe eviction under load; and enable RDB/AOF persistence, restart the container, and confirm data survives. Document why each Redis data type was chosen.
tasks.deliverable: A Redis notes file mapping each data type to a use case, a cached hot endpoint with TTL, an eviction-policy experiment showing keys evicted under maxmemory, a persistence test surviving a container restart, and a measured Postgres-vs-Redis latency comparison.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the hardened Phase 2 containers to managed infrastructure, provisioned entirely as code. Identity and network foundations first, then compute and load balancing, then managed data including ElastiCache Redis so Redis moves from localhost to a real cloud dependency, then delivery-to-AWS automation with no static credentials, and finally multi-environment reproducibility.

tasks.title: AWS baseline as code: IAM, budgets and remote state
tasks.description: Set up a clean AWS foundation: a non-root admin identity with MFA, a least-privilege deployment role scoped to the services this project uses (ECR, ECS, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, IAM pass-role), AWS CLI v2 profiles, and a budget alarm with an email notification. Provision IAM, budgets and a Terraform S3 + DynamoDB remote-state backend in a version-controlled repo, and enable CloudTrail into a dedicated logging bucket.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning least-privilege IAM roles/policies, a budget alarm and S3+DynamoDB state backend; CloudTrail enabled with one captured audit event; a screenshot of the active budget alarm.

tasks.title: Define the VPC and network layer in Terraform
tasks.description: Define a VPC across two availability zones: public subnets for the load balancer, private subnets for compute and data, an internet gateway, a NAT gateway for egress, route tables per tier, and security groups that whitelist only the ports the app needs. Enforce the rule that nothing is hand-clicked in the console: destroy the stack and re-apply it to prove the network reproduces from code alone.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform VPC module (subnets, IGW, NAT, route tables, security groups) that provisions a clean network after `terraform destroy` and re-apply, with a subnet/CIDR topology diagram.

tasks.title: Deploy the containers to ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer
tasks.description: Push the hardened api and worker images to Amazon ECR and run them as ECS Fargate services across two AZs. The api service sits behind an ALB with a target group and health checks and is reachable only through the ALB security group; the worker runs with no inbound exposure. Tasks live in private subnets with NAT egress, logs stream to CloudWatch, and a rolling deployment replaces tasks with no downtime. Define the cluster, task definitions, services and ALB in Terraform.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned ECR repos, ECS Fargate api service on 2+ AZs plus a worker service, and an ALB with health checks; a reachable public API URL and a deployed-architecture diagram showing request flow.

tasks.title: Add managed data: RDS, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis
tasks.description: Move off local containers to managed services. Provision RDS PostgreSQL in private subnets whose security group accepts traffic only from the ECS service security group, a versioned S3 bucket for uploads with a least-privilege bucket policy, Secrets Manager entries for database and Redis credentials injected at task start, and an ElastiCache Redis cluster in the data subnet. Point the app's Redis client at ElastiCache and prove the cached hot endpoint now reads from a managed Redis cache in the cloud, with the localhost fallback removed.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Postgres + S3 + Secrets Manager + ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining; a migration run against RDS; proof of an S3 upload; and a cache hit served from ElastiCache with the measured latency improvement over the Phase 1 baseline.

tasks.title: Automate the full pipeline from commit to ECS rollout with OIDC and rollback
tasks.description: Extend the Phase 2 pipeline to deploy to AWS with no long-lived keys: configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a tightly scoped trust policy, then on merge to main build the image, tag it with the commit SHA, push to ECR, render the new ECS task definition, deploy, wait for service stability, and run post-deploy smoke tests against the live URL. Add a manual approval gate for production and a rollback job that redeploys the previous task revision.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS -> smoke test -> notify), the IAM trust policy, a production Environment approval gate, and logs proving both a successful deploy and a successful rollback.

tasks.title: Make the whole environment reproducible across dev and prod
tasks.description: Refactor the VPC, ECS, ALB, RDS, ElastiCache, S3 and IAM resources into a single parameterized Terraform stack with dev and prod variable files that differ only in sizing and count. Stand up the second environment end to end, confirm the same pipeline promotes between them, and record a destroy-and-recreate run as evidence the infrastructure is disposable and reproducible.
tasks.deliverable: One parameterized Terraform stack applied to two environments from variable files alone, a recorded `terraform destroy`/`apply` cycle, and a documented promotion path from dev to prod.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives'. Redis is closed out as a real production dependency with three distinct uses, system design becomes the vocabulary for the caching, consistency, queueing and scaling tradeoffs now actually implemented, and the deployed system gets observability, autoscaling validated under load, edge hardening, and cost and disaster-recovery discipline.

tasks.title: Instrument the stack with logs, metrics, dashboards, alarms and tracing
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end. Emit structured JSON logs with request IDs and ship them to CloudWatch Logs; publish custom latency and business metrics and expose /health and /metrics endpoints; build a CloudWatch dashboard (request rate, p95 latency, 5xx rate, ECS CPU/memory, RDS connections, Redis evictions) and at least three alarms on error rate, latency and unhealthy targets wired to a notification channel. Add OpenTelemetry tracing across ALB -> API -> Redis -> worker and capture one trace end to end.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, 3+ CloudWatch alarms with a notification target, and an exported OTel trace of one request spanning API, cache and worker.

tasks.title: Load test to a stated SLO and configure autoscaling on real signals
tasks.description: Write a k6 (or Locust) script that ramps to realistic concurrency against the ALB and capture latency, throughput and error curves. Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target plus tuned cooldowns and min/max task counts, then re-run the test to show scale-out and scale-in. Pick one stated SLO (e.g. p95 under 300ms at 200 rps), document whether it holds, and identify the observed bottleneck - most likely the database connection pool - with its fix.
tasks.deliverable: k6/Locust script and report with before/after throughput, p95 and error rate, ECS autoscaling policies with evidence of scale-out, a stated SLO with pass/fail verdict, and a bottleneck analysis note.

tasks.title: Close the Redis gap with cache-aside, rate limiting and async queues
tasks.description: Implement three production Redis patterns against ElastiCache. First, a cache-aside layer for the hot read endpoint with explicit TTLs, versioned cache keys, negative-cache handling and stampede protection (a lock or single-flight), benchmarked against the Phase 1 no-cache baseline. Second, a Redis token-bucket (or sliding-window) rate limiter on the public API that returns 429 - a policy concept enforced in application code. Third, move the slow write path to a background worker consuming an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue and idempotent handlers, using Redis for job status, and deploy the worker as its own ECS service.
tasks.deliverable: Cache-aside layer with measured hit rate and latency reduction, a Redis rate limiter with a test proving 429 behavior, and an SQS-backed worker ECS service with DLQ, idempotency keys and a before/after latency benchmark.

tasks.title: Write three system design documents grounded in what was built
tasks.description: Turn implementation into design language. Write three design docs - a multi-tenant SaaS API, a file upload and processing pipeline, and a payment/event flow with exactly-once processing concerns - each covering API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy and invalidation, queueing and backpressure, idempotency, consistency tradeoffs, AWS hosting topology, scaling limits and failure modes. Every decision must cite an artifact from Phases 2-4 (e.g. 'Redis cache-aside with versioned keys because we measured X'), and each doc includes a tradeoff table comparing SQL, Redis and a queue for every read and write path.
tasks.deliverable: Three system design docs with architecture diagrams, tradeoff tables, capacity and SLO estimates, a failure-mode table (retry, timeout, circuit breaker), and a self-critique list of where an interviewer would push back.

tasks.title: Harden the production edge and document the architecture
tasks.description: Attach AWS WAF managed rules to the ALB, enforce HTTPS-only with security headers, verify S3 buckets block public access, and re-review IAM for unused permissions after all services exist. Capture the whole system as one labeled architecture diagram covering the request path, each data store (Postgres, Redis, S3, SQS), and the CI/CD deployment path from commit to ECS task.
tasks.deliverable: WAF and HTTPS configuration, security-header check output, an S3 public-access-block verification, a trimmed IAM policy diff, and a one-page annotated architecture diagram.

tasks.title: Produce a cost, scaling and disaster-recovery review
tasks.description: Use Cost Explorer and the AWS pricing calculator to estimate monthly cost, identify the three largest line items, and apply three concrete optimizations (e.g. Fargate Spot for the worker, right-sizing RDS, TTL tuning to reduce Redis memory). Then document RTO/RPO targets and a tested backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3, plus a failure-mode table naming each single point of failure (single NAT gateway, single-AZ Redis, unpooled DB connections) and its mitigation.
tasks.deliverable: A cost estimate with top-three drivers and three applied optimizations with actual dollar deltas, an RTO/RPO statement, a tested backup/restore runbook with measured recovery time, and a failure-mode table with mitigations.

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert Phases 1-4 into interview performance for a Full Stack Engineer loop at Stripe. Every deliverable becomes a story, a diagram and a defensible decision, and the Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD and system design gaps are rehearsed until they can be explained under time pressure without notes.

tasks.title: Run timed system design drills with whiteboard diagrams
tasks.description: Convert the Phase 4 design docs into verbal fluency. Run at least six timed 35-40 minute prompts alone and two recorded: a URL shortener, a feed/notification system, a payment-idempotency service, a rate-limited public API, an analytics ingestion pipeline, and a multi-tenant SaaS API. For each, clarify requirements, estimate scale, sketch boxes and arrows, choose a data model, place caching and queues, name the bottleneck and the failure mode, then write out the answers you would give to the three hardest follow-up questions.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design drill packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, tradeoff decisions, follow-up answers) plus two recorded mock design sessions with a reviewed list of recurring weak points.

tasks.title: Drill the Docker, AWS and Redis question sets from your own build
tasks.description: Answer 40 questions per area, each anchored to a decision made in your own project rather than a textbook definition. Docker: layer caching, multi-stage rationale, CMD vs ENTRYPOINT, network drivers, volumes vs bind mounts, image hardening. AWS: VPC and subnet design, security groups vs NACLs, IAM roles vs users, ECS vs Lambda vs EC2, ALB vs NLB, RDS Multi-AZ vs read replicas, ElastiCache in front of a hot path. Redis: data types and when to use each, TTL and eviction policies, cache-aside vs write-through, stampede protection, persistence modes, and using one Redis instance for cache, rate limiting and job state.
tasks.deliverable: Three question banks (40 answers each) where every answer references the specific artifact you built, plus a flagged list of answers you could not give fluently and a re-drill of those.

tasks.title: Publish the portfolio repository and map it to resume bullets
tasks.description: Consolidate the app, Dockerfiles, compose profiles, Terraform, CI/CD workflows, tests, SBOM/scan reports and runbooks into one clean public repository whose README reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment guide, dashboards and screenshots, load-test numbers, cost notes and the rollback runbook. Then write RESUME.md mapping each project feature to a quantified resume bullet and rewrite the resume's experience section to foreground shipping, containers, cloud and cache work.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, container quickstart, AWS deploy + rollback guides, dashboards, a live demo URL, and a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping with a rewritten experience section.

tasks.title: Build a metrics-backed STAR story bank and run mock interviews
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop: a live coding round (add a tested endpoint to a running containerized app), a Docker/AWS/Redis deep dive, a system design round, and behavioral questions. Build a STAR bank of 8+ stories with real numbers from Phases 1-4 - image size reduced from X to Y MB, an OOM crash loop diagnosed and fixed, cache hit rate raised to 85% cutting p95 by 60%, a pipeline automated from manual deploy to OIDC-gated rollout, a rate limiter added after a load test found abuse - plus one story on scaling the SQS worker. Log every question asked, tighten the answer, and finish with a readiness checklist covering all five target areas.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (one coding, one system design) with feedback logs, a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist covering Docker, AWS, Redis, CI/CD and system design.

careerPlans.summary: A 5-phase, roughly 10-15 week plan built specifically around this Full Stack Engineer (Stripe) candidate's gaps, with no generic filler: Docker and Redis are missing skills, AWS is a missing skill, and CI/CD and System Design are partial skills to level up. Phase 1 creates the single reference full-stack app that every later phase operates on and puts strict linting, hermetic tests and a first GitHub Actions pipeline around it. Phase 2 is the Docker deep dive plus first Redis contact: multi-stage Dockerfiles, a six-service Compose stack including Redis, dev/prod overrides, hardened and scanned images, a reusable environment-aware pipeline, a five-incident container debugging runbook, and Redis fundamentals exercised against the live container. Phase 3 closes the AWS gap from identity and network foundations upward - least-privilege IAM and remote state as code, a two-AZ VPC in Terraform, ECS Fargate behind an ALB, managed RDS plus S3 plus Secrets Manager plus ElastiCache Redis, OIDC-based deploy with smoke tests and rollback, and a second reproducible environment. Phase 4 makes it production-grade: CloudWatch/OpenTelemetry observability, k6 load testing against a stated SLO with ECS autoscaling, Redis closed out as a real dependency through cache-aside, rate limiting and SQS-backed async workers, three grounded system design documents, edge hardening, and a cost plus disaster-recovery review. Phase 5 converts all of it into interview evidence through timed system design drills, Docker/AWS/Redis question banks answered from your own build, a public case-study portfolio with resume mapping, and metrics-backed STAR stories rehearsed in mock interviews. Every task names the gap it closes and ends in an inspectable artifact - a Dockerfile, a compose stack, a Terraform module, a workflow, a dashboard, a benchmark or a design doc - so progress can be verified rather than assumed.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Establish the reproducible, containerized build-test loop that every later phase depends on. The candidate has no container or pipeline ownership on record, so this phase makes Docker the default way the project runs and makes lint, type-check and tests runnable identically locally and in a container — the foundation for the Docker and CI/CD gaps.

tasks.title: Containerize the Reference Full-Stack App
tasks.description: Build or adopt one real full-stack app (React/Next.js frontend + Node/Express or FastAPI backend + PostgreSQL) and define it entirely in containers. Write a multi-stage Dockerfile per service (deps -> build -> runtime), pin the base image to an exact major/minor/tag, install from a lockfile, run as a non-root user, add a HEALTHCHECK and a .dockerignore. Compare the multi-stage image size against a naive single-stage build. This is the artifact all five gaps are closed against.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-stage Dockerfile for frontend and backend, .dockerignore, non-root USER and HEALTHCHECK, plus a before/after image-size note in the README

tasks.title: One-Command Docker Compose Stack with Healthchecked Dependencies
tasks.description: Author a docker-compose.yml that brings up frontend, backend and PostgreSQL together on one named network with named volumes, .env-driven config, depends_on with condition: service_healthy, and a Postgres healthcheck. Add bind mounts for hot reload and prove a cold `docker compose down -v && docker compose up` boots the whole stack with seeded data.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml with three services, healthchecks, named volume and a verified one-command cold start, plus a container-network diagram in the README

tasks.title: Container-Native Quality Gate (lint + strict types + pre-commit)
tasks.description: Configure strict TypeScript (strict: true, no implicit any) or mypy/pyright strict for Python, plus ESLint + Prettier (or Ruff + Black), Husky/lint-staged pre-commit hooks and commitlint. Expose lint, typecheck, format and test as npm/Make scripts that run unchanged inside the Docker image, so the container is the single source of truth for code quality.
tasks.deliverable: Committed strict tsconfig/mypy config, ESLint/Prettier config, pre-commit hook, and a `docker run <image> npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test` command that executes green

tasks.title: Container-Aware Automated Test Suite
tasks.description: Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests against a real database spun up with Testcontainers (or a dedicated compose service), so tests need no pre-started DB. Cover one happy path, one validation error and one authorization failure for the core resource, and produce a coverage report.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest/Jest + Supertest (or Pytest) suite with Testcontainers-backed integration tests, 60%+ API-layer coverage report, and a `test` script that needs no external database

tasks.title: First GitHub Actions CI Pipeline: lint + test matrix + image build
tasks.description: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every pull request: dependency caching, lint, typecheck, the test suite, and a Docker build of all images (no push). Use a version matrix, upload the coverage artifact, and enable branch protection so the checks are required before merge.
tasks.deliverable: .github/workflows/ci.yml with lint/typecheck/test matrix and an image-build job, branch protection enabled, and a link to a green PR pipeline run

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take Docker and the pipeline from 'it runs' to production bar. Images get hardened and scanned, the local stack becomes a six-service distributed system with tier isolation, and CI becomes a reusable, environment-aware delivery system with smoke tests and one-click rollback. This is the container and pipeline literacy the target role assumes and the candidate must be able to defend.

tasks.title: Production Image Hardening and Supply-Chain Scanning
tasks.description: Rebuild the images for production: slim/alpine or distroless base, non-root user, only runtime artifacts copied forward, proper layer ordering for dependency caching, OCI labels, pinned base-image digests. Scan with Trivy, generate an SBOM with Syft, remove any baked-in secrets, and measure size/layers before and after with `docker image ls` and dive.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfile producing a sub-300MB non-root image on a pinned digest, .dockerignore, SBOM, Trivy scan report, and a dev-vs-prod size/layer comparison

tasks.title: Multi-Service Orchestration with Dev/Prod Compose Overrides
tasks.description: Model a realistic distributed system locally: frontend, API, background worker, PostgreSQL, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy. Use a base compose file plus dev and prod override files, separate networks that isolate the data tier from the public tier, healthcheck-based depends_on, resource limits and JSON-file log rotation. Seed the database and prove state survives a down/up cycle.
tasks.deliverable: Base docker-compose.yml plus dev/prod override files orchestrating six services with tier isolation, healthchecks, resource limits and log rotation, a verified volume-persistence test, and a service-topology diagram

tasks.title: Reusable Parameterized CI with Scanning and PR Preview Environments
tasks.description: Extract a reusable workflow (workflow_call) and composite actions for setup/test/build so jobs stop duplicating YAML. Add path filters, concurrency groups that cancel superseded PR runs, dependency and container scanning jobs that fail on HIGH/CRITICAL, buildx layer caching, and short-lived per-PR preview environments. Gate the protected environment with required reviewers.
tasks.deliverable: Reusable GitHub Actions workflow plus composite actions, buildx layer caching, concurrency groups, scanning jobs gating merges, a working PR preview environment, and a documented .github/ structure diagram

tasks.title: Continuous Delivery with Post-Deploy Smoke Tests and One-Click Rollback
tasks.description: On merge to main, build and tag the image with the commit SHA, push to a registry, deploy to a hosted environment, run post-deploy smoke tests against the live URL, and notify on failure. Add a prompt-free rollback job that redeploys the previous image tag, and track DORA metrics (lead time, deploy frequency, change-failure rate, MTTR) across at least three real deploys.
tasks.deliverable: Deploy workflow (build -> registry -> deploy -> smoke test -> notify) with a tested rollback job, a release/rollback runbook, and a DORA metrics table from three or more deploys

tasks.title: Container Debugging and Runtime Operations Runbook
tasks.description: Learn to operate containers, not just build them. Reproduce five incidents on purpose — crash loop from a bad entrypoint, OOM kill under a memory limit, port conflict, network DNS failure, and a volume permission error as non-root — and diagnose each with docker logs/exec/stats/inspect/events and docker compose. Handle SIGTERM for graceful shutdown and capture before/after docker stats under CPU/memory limits.
tasks.deliverable: Container debugging runbook with five reproduced incidents (symptom, diagnostic command, root cause, fix), a SIGTERM graceful-shutdown demo, and a resource-limit before/after stats report

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the Phase 2 containers to managed infrastructure provisioned as code. Work from identity and network foundations upward to a running HTTPS application with managed database, cache and object storage. Any existing cloud or networking experience should be explicitly mapped onto AWS VPC, security groups, route tables and IAM so it transfers rather than resets.

tasks.title: AWS Baseline as Code: IAM, Budgets and Remote State
tasks.description: Set up a clean AWS foundation: a non-root admin identity with MFA, a least-privilege deployment role for CI, AWS CLI profiles, and a budget alarm. Provision everything with Terraform (or AWS CDK) in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB locking. Write an explicit concept-mapping note from any adjacent platform (e.g. Azure RBAC/Policy, resource groups) to AWS IAM roles/policies, SCPs and tagging.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform repo provisioning IAM roles/policies, budget alarms and an S3+DynamoDB remote-state backend, a documented least-privilege deploy policy, a cloud-to-AWS concept-mapping sheet, and a screenshot of the active budget alarm

tasks.title: Deploy Containers to ECS Fargate behind an ALB in Private Subnets
tasks.description: Push the hardened images to Amazon ECR and run them on ECS Fargate across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks. Place tasks in private subnets with a NAT gateway path, expose only the ALB through a security group, and define the VPC, public/private subnets, route tables and routes in Terraform.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned VPC (public/private subnets, route tables, NAT), ECR repository, ECS Fargate service on 2+ AZs and an ALB with health checks, a reachable public URL, and a deployed-architecture diagram

tasks.title: Managed Data, Secrets and ElastiCache Redis on AWS
tasks.description: Move off local containers to managed services: RDS PostgreSQL in private subnets whose security group accepts traffic only from the ECS service, a versioned S3 bucket for uploads with a least-privilege bucket policy, Secrets Manager (or SSM Parameter Store) credentials injected at task start, and an ElastiCache Redis cluster. Point the app's Redis client at ElastiCache and prove caching works in the cloud.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS Postgres + S3 + Secrets Manager + ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining, a migration run against RDS, proof of an S3 upload, and an app screenshot showing a cache hit served from ElastiCache

tasks.title: GitHub Actions to AWS with OIDC, Blue/Green Deploy and Rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery to AWS without static keys: configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a scoped trust policy, then extend the Phase 2 pipeline to build, push to ECR, render a new ECS task definition, and perform a rolling then CodeDeploy blue/green deployment that waits for service stability. Add a manual approval gate for production and a tested rollback to the previous task revision.
tasks.deliverable: OIDC-based deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS rolling then blue/green), IAM trust policy, GitHub Environment approval gate, and logs proving both a successful deploy and a successful rollback

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives'. The Redis and System Design gaps are closed together here: Redis as a real cache, rate-limiter and async dependency; System Design as the vocabulary for the caching, consistency and scaling trade-offs actually implemented. Observability and autoscaling turn the deployed stack into evidence of production judgment.

tasks.title: Observability: Structured Logs, Metrics, Alarms and Tracing
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end: structured JSON logs with request IDs shipped to CloudWatch Logs, custom latency and business metrics via the CloudWatch SDK or embedded metric format, a dashboard (request rate, p95, error rate, ECS CPU/memory, RDS connections) with alarms on error-rate and latency thresholds, and OpenTelemetry tracing across ALB -> API -> worker.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware, a CloudWatch dashboard, three or more CloudWatch alarms with a notification target, an OTel trace of one request across services, and a one-page observability translation table if migrating from another platform's tooling

tasks.title: Autoscaling and Load Testing to a Defined SLO
tasks.description: Configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target tracking on CPU and ALB request-count-per-target, then drive load with k6 or Locust against the deployed endpoint. Capture p95 latency, throughput and error rate before and after scale-out, tune target values, cooldowns and min/max task counts to hit a stated SLO, and document the observed bottleneck (usually the database connection pool) and its fix.
tasks.deliverable: ECS autoscaling policies for CPU and request count with tuned min/max, a k6/Locust script and report (throughput, p95, error rate) showing scale-out, and a bottleneck-analysis note

tasks.title: Redis Caching, Rate Limiting and Async Queue Processing
tasks.description: Close the Redis gap with three production uses, not one tutorial. First, cache-aside on a hot read endpoint with explicit TTLs, cache-key versioning and stampede protection, benchmarked against ElastiCache. Second, a Redis token-bucket rate limiter on the public API with a test proving 429 behaviour. Third, move slow work (email, image processing, report generation) to a background worker consuming an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue and idempotent handlers, using Redis for job status. Containerize the worker separately and run it as its own ECS service.
tasks.deliverable: Cache-aside layer with measured hit-rate and latency improvement, a Redis token-bucket rate limiter with a test proving 429 behaviour, and an SQS-backed worker as a separate ECS service with DLQ, idempotency keys and a before/after latency benchmark

tasks.title: System Design Fluency: Caching, Queues, Consistency and Failure Modes
tasks.description: Turn implementation into design language. Write three design documents — a multi-tenant SaaS API, an image-upload and processing pipeline, and a payment/event flow with idempotency and ordering concerns — each covering API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy and invalidation, queueing and backpressure, idempotency, consistency trade-offs, AWS hosting topology, scaling limits and failure modes. Back every choice with something built in Phases 2-4 and include a trade-off table comparing SQL vs Redis vs queue per read/write path.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design docs with architecture diagrams, trade-off tables, capacity/SLO estimates, a failure-mode table (retry, timeout, circuit breaker), and a self-critique list of where an interviewer would push back

tasks.title: Multi-Environment Terraform, Cost Control and Disaster Recovery
tasks.description: Make the infrastructure repeatable and affordable. Parameterize Terraform into dev/staging/prod workspaces or var-files with environment-specific sizing, stand up a second environment end to end and confirm the same pipeline promotes between them. Produce a Cost Explorer analysis with three applied optimizations (rightsizing Fargate, RDS instance class, savings from the Redis cache) and document an RTO/RPO backup-and-restore runbook for RDS and S3.
tasks.deliverable: Multi-environment Terraform (dev/staging/prod) with a deployed staging stack, a cost analysis with three applied optimizations and actual dollar deltas, and a tested backup/restore DR runbook with measured recovery time

phases.title: Phase 5: Technical Interview Polish & Review
phases.description: Convert the Phase 1-4 artifacts into interview performance for the Full Stack Engineer loop. Every deliverable becomes a story, a diagram and a defensible decision, rehearsed under time pressure. The goal is fluency on the five gap areas plus a portfolio that proves them end to end.

tasks.title: Timed System Design Drills with Whiteboard Diagrams
tasks.description: Convert the Phase 4 design docs into verbal fluency. Run at least six timed 35-40 minute mock prompts alone and two recorded with a peer: a URL shortener, a feed/notification system, a payment-idempotency service, a rate-limited public API, an analytics ingestion pipeline, and a multi-tenant SaaS. For each, clarify requirements, estimate scale, sketch boxes and arrows, choose a data model, place caching and queues, name the bottleneck and the failure mode, then write answers to the three hardest follow-ups.
tasks.deliverable: Six completed design drill packets (requirements, capacity math, diagram, trade-off decisions, follow-up answers) plus two recorded mock design sessions with a reviewed list of recurring weak points

tasks.title: Portfolio Repository, Architecture Writeup and Resume Mapping
tasks.description: Consolidate the code, Terraform, compose files, CI/CD workflows, tests, SBOM/scan reports and runbooks into one clean public repository with a README that reads like an engineering case study: problem, architecture diagram, stack, `docker compose up` quickstart, AWS deployment guide, observability screenshots, load-test numbers, cost notes and the rollback runbook. Then write RESUME.md mapping each project feature to a quantified resume bullet.
tasks.deliverable: Public GitHub repository with architecture diagram, container quickstart, AWS deployment and rollback guides, dashboards and screenshots, and a RESUME.md feature-to-bullet mapping reviewed against the Full Stack Engineer target

tasks.title: AWS Knowledge Consolidation and Practice Exams
tasks.description: Convert practical AWS experience into exam-grade, interview-ready fluency. Work the core SAA-C03 domains — IAM, VPC/networking, ECS/ECR/Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, S3, SQS, CloudWatch, cost models — condensing each service into a one-page cheat sheet that pairs the service with the thing actually built with it. Sit at least three timed practice exams and review every wrong answer to a service-level explanation.
tasks.deliverable: Cheat sheets for 10+ AWS services each linked to a project artifact, three timed practice-exam score reports with a wrong-answer review log, targeting a consistent 80%+ before scheduling the real exam

tasks.title: Mock Interviews and a Metrics-Backed STAR Story Bank
tasks.description: Rehearse the full loop: a live coding round (add a tested endpoint to the running containerized app), a Docker/AWS/Redis deep dive, a system design round, and behavioral questions. Build a STAR bank of 8+ stories from real Phase 1-4 work with numbers — 'cut image size from 1.2GB to 220MB', 'diagnosed an ECS OOM crash loop', 'raised cache hit rate to 85% and cut p95 by 60%', 'automated a manual approval into an OIDC-gated pipeline'. Log every question asked and tighten the answer.
tasks.deliverable: STAR story bank with 8+ metric-backed stories, two recorded mock interviews (one coding, one system design), a question log with revised answers, and a final readiness checklist covering Docker, CI/CD, AWS, Redis and system design

careerPlans.summary: A 9-10 week, container-and-cloud-first roadmap for a Full Stack Engineer target, built around five specific gaps: Docker, AWS and Redis missing; CI/CD and System Design partial. It is sequenced so each phase feeds the next. Phase 1 builds a reproducible containerized dev/test loop and the first GitHub Actions pipeline; Phase 2 hardens images, orchestrates six services locally with Compose, and turns CI into a reusable delivery system with scanning, environment gates, smoke tests and rollback; Phase 3 closes AWS as code — Terraform, IAM, VPC, ECS Fargate, ALB, RDS, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis — with OIDC-based blue/green delivery; Phase 4 adds production depth (CloudWatch/OTel observability, autoscaling under k6 load, Redis cache-aside plus rate limiting plus SQS async workers, system design docs, multi-environment cost and DR discipline); Phase 5 converts every artifact into timed system design drills, a documented portfolio repository, AWS exam fluency and metric-backed STAR stories. Every task names the specific gap it closes and produces an inspectable deliverable.

phases.title: Phase 1: Core Fundamentals & Code Quality
phases.description: Establish the baseline every later phase assumes: one runnable full-stack reference service (typed frontend, REST API, PostgreSQL) that starts with a single command in containers, enforces strict typing and linting as a gate rather than a habit, and has a green CI pipeline on every pull request. No candidate skill could be verified, so this phase also produces the first concrete evidence for Docker and CI/CD instead of assuming either.

tasks.title: Build and Containerize the Reference Full-Stack Baseline
tasks.description: Create the project that every later phase deploys: a TypeScript React frontend, a typed REST API (Node/Express or Fastify), and PostgreSQL. Write a separate multi-stage Dockerfile per service (deps -> build -> runtime) so no build toolchain ships in the runtime image, then a docker-compose.yml that wires frontend, API and Postgres onto one named bridge network with a named volume for Postgres data, .env-driven configuration, and a pg_isready healthcheck the API waits on. Add bind mounts for hot reload so the containerized loop is as fast as running natively.
tasks.deliverable: Two multi-stage Dockerfiles (frontend, API) plus docker-compose.yml booting the full stack; `docker compose up` from a clean machine serves a working page backed by a live API and database; README with quickstart and a container-network diagram.

tasks.title: Strict-Type and Lint Quality Gate with Pre-Commit Enforcement
tasks.description: Turn type safety and style into checks that fail loudly. Enable TypeScript strict mode (strict, noImplicitAny, noUncheckedIndexedAccess) across frontend and API with shared request/response DTO interfaces in a common types package. Configure ESLint plus Prettier (or Ruff plus Black for any Python utility code) and add a Husky + lint-staged pre-commit hook that runs format, lint and typecheck on staged files only. Expose the identical work as `lint`, `typecheck`, `format` and `test` npm scripts so the exact same command runs on a laptop, inside the Docker build and inside CI.
tasks.deliverable: Committed strict tsconfig with zero type errors on a full build, ESLint/Prettier configs, a working Husky pre-commit hook, and a documented script list that behaves identically locally, in-container and in CI.

tasks.title: Container-Aware Automated Test Suite
tasks.description: Prove the service is testable in isolation, the way a pipeline will test it. Add unit tests for business logic and integration tests that exercise the real HTTP layer against a real PostgreSQL started per test run with Testcontainers (or a dedicated compose service on a throwaway port) - not a mocked database. Cover a happy path, a validation failure, an authorization/permission failure, and a database-constraint violation for the core resource. Emit a coverage report and make `npm test` require no pre-started database.
tasks.deliverable: Vitest/Jest + Supertest suite in containers with Testcontainers-backed integration tests, >=60% coverage on the API layer, a published coverage artifact, and a `test` script that provisions its own database.

tasks.title: First GitHub Actions CI Pipeline: Lint, Typecheck, Test Matrix, Image Build
tasks.description: Close the CI/CD gap with the smallest pipeline that actually protects main. Create a GitHub Actions workflow triggered on pull_request and push to main that checks out the repo, installs dependencies with a cached lockfile, runs lint, typecheck and the test suite in a matrix over supported runtime versions, and builds the Docker images without pushing them. Upload the coverage artifact and enable branch protection so the checks must pass before merge. Structure it as small named jobs so Phase 2 can extract them into a reusable workflow.
tasks.deliverable: A committed .github/workflows/ci.yml with lint/typecheck/test matrix jobs, Docker image builds, artifact upload, branch protection on main, and a link or screenshot of a green pull-request run.

phases.title: Phase 2: High-Priority Missing Skill Deep Dive
phases.description: Take Docker from 'it runs on my laptop' to production bar, and put Redis into the stack properly rather than as a tutorial exercise. Images become minimal, non-root and scanned; the local environment becomes a six-service topology with tier isolation and healthchecks; container operations become a documented debugging skill; and Redis 7 becomes a real cache-aside layer with a measured hit rate - the evidence that closes two of the three priority gaps before anything touches the cloud.

tasks.title: Production Image Hardening and Supply-Chain Scanning
tasks.description: Rebuild both images for production: distroless or slim base on a pinned digest, a non-root runtime user, only compiled artifacts copied from the build stage, a strict .dockerignore excluding node_modules, tests and .git, OCI image labels, and layer ordering that keeps dependency layers cached across code changes. Build multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64). Scan with Trivy and fail on HIGH/CRITICAL, generate an SBOM with Syft, verify no secret or .env file is baked into any layer, and measure before/after size and layer count with `docker image ls` and `dive`.
tasks.deliverable: Hardened production Dockerfile per service producing a sub-300MB non-root runtime image on a pinned digest, .dockerignore, Trivy scan report, Syft SBOM, multi-arch build proof, and a dev-vs-prod size/layer comparison table.

tasks.title: Multi-Service Orchestration with Dev and Prod Compose Overrides
tasks.description: Model a realistic distributed system locally: frontend, API, background worker, PostgreSQL, Redis and an Nginx reverse proxy that terminates TLS locally and routes to the API. Use a base compose file plus dev and prod override files, two custom networks so the database tier is unreachable from the public tier, healthcheck-based depends_on ordering, CPU/memory limits, JSON-file log rotation with bounded size, and restart policies. Seed the database and prove state survives a `down` / `up` cycle when the volume is kept and is clean when it is removed.
tasks.deliverable: docker-compose.yml plus dev and prod override files orchestrating six services with tier-isolated networks, healthchecks, resource limits, log rotation and restart policies; a verified volume-persistence test; and a service-topology diagram with the exposed ports marked.

tasks.title: Container Operations and Failure-Mode Debugging Runbook
tasks.description: Learn to operate containers, not just build them. Deliberately reproduce five incidents and diagnose each with the right tool rather than a restart: a crash loop from a bad entrypoint, an OOM kill under a memory limit, a host port conflict, a Docker-network DNS resolution failure between services, and a volume permission error caused by running as non-root. For each, record the symptom, the exact diagnosis command (`logs`, `inspect`, `stats`, `events`, `compose ps`), the root cause and the fix. Handle SIGTERM in the API for graceful shutdown of in-flight requests and open DB connections.
tasks.deliverable: An incident runbook with five reproduced container failures (symptom, diagnosis command, root cause, fix, prevention), a SIGTERM graceful-shutdown demo showing zero dropped requests, and a `docker stats` before/after report under applied CPU/memory limits.

tasks.title: Redis from First Principles: Cache-Aside on a Hot Read Endpoint
tasks.description: Bring Redis into the stack as a real dependency instead of a side-car. Add Redis 7 to compose with a persistent AOF/RDB volume and a healthcheck, then implement a cache-aside layer for the hottest read endpoint: an explicit key-naming convention (namespace:entity:id:version), a documented TTL policy per key class, compact JSON or MessagePack serialization, hit/miss counters, and cache invalidation on every write to the entity. Handle Redis being unreachable by falling back to the database rather than failing the request. Load ~100k rows and benchmark the endpoint with and without the cache.
tasks.deliverable: Redis 7 service in compose plus a cache-aside module with versioned keys, TTL policy table and write-path invalidation; a benchmark report showing cache hit rate, and p50/p95 latency before vs after, with the raw k6 script committed.

phases.title: Phase 3: Cloud Deployment & Distributed Infrastructure
phases.description: Close the AWS gap by deploying the Phase 2 containers onto managed infrastructure that is entirely declared as code. Everything here is provisioned, not clicked: Terraform or CDK for VPC, ECS Fargate, ALB, RDS, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache, with least-privilege IAM and OIDC-based delivery so no static AWS keys exist anywhere. This is the phase that turns three local containers into a multi-AZ, internet-reachable system with a real deploy and a real rollback.

tasks.title: AWS Baseline as Code: Least-Privilege IAM, Budgets and Remote State
tasks.description: Build a clean, safe AWS foundation before deploying anything. Create a non-root administrative identity with MFA, a dedicated deployment role scoped to only the services this project needs, AWS CLI v2 profiles, and a billing budget with an alarm at a low threshold. Provision all of it with Terraform (or AWS CDK) in a version-controlled repo using an S3 remote state backend with DynamoDB state locking and encryption. Note the resource-tagging and naming convention that every later module reuses.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform (or CDK) repository provisioning IAM users/roles/policies, a budget with an active alarm, and an S3 + DynamoDB remote state backend; a documented least-privilege deployment policy; and a screenshot of the budget alarm in the console.

tasks.title: Deploy the Containers to ECS Fargate behind an ALB in Private Subnets
tasks.description: Own the full network and compute path. In Terraform define a VPC with public and private subnets across two Availability Zones, route tables, an internet gateway and a NAT gateway for egress. Push the hardened images to Amazon ECR, then run them as an ECS Fargate service (2+ tasks, spread across AZs) behind an Application Load Balancer with target-group health checks and a listener on HTTPS. Place tasks in private subnets, allow inbound only from the ALB security group, and expose the database only to the tasks security group. Add container health checks, a deployment circuit breaker with automatic rollback, and CloudWatch log groups.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform-provisioned VPC (2 AZs, public/private subnets, NAT), ECR repository, ECS Fargate service and ALB with health checks and HTTPS listener; a reachable public URL serving the Phase 2 app; and a deployed-architecture diagram labelling subnet, security-group and route boundaries.

tasks.title: Managed Data, Secrets and ElastiCache Redis on AWS
tasks.description: Replace the local containers with managed services. Provision RDS PostgreSQL in private subnets with automated backups and a security group that accepts traffic only from the ECS service, a versioned and encrypted S3 bucket for uploads with a least-privilege bucket policy, Secrets Manager entries for the database credentials injected into the task at start (never into an image or repo), and an ElastiCache Redis cluster in the same VPC. Point the application's Redis client at ElastiCache through configuration only, and prove the cache-aside path works against managed Redis, not localhost.
tasks.deliverable: Terraform for RDS PostgreSQL, S3, Secrets Manager and ElastiCache Redis with security-group chaining; a successful database migration run against RDS; proof of an authenticated S3 upload; and an application screenshot with a Redis hit served by ElastiCache.

tasks.title: Keyless CI/CD to AWS: OIDC Federation, Rolling and Blue/Green Deploy, Rollback
tasks.description: Automate delivery to AWS with no long-lived credentials. Configure GitHub OIDC federation to an IAM role with a trust policy restricted to this repository and branch, then extend the pipeline to build the image, push to ECR with a commit-SHA tag, render a new ECS task definition, and deploy - first as a rolling update, then as an AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment that shifts traffic only after the replacement task set is healthy. Wait for service stability, add a manual approval gate via a GitHub Environment for production, and implement a one-command rollback to the previous task revision. Prove both directions with logs.
tasks.deliverable: An OIDC-based deploy workflow (build -> ECR -> ECS rolling -> blue/green), the IAM trust policy, GitHub Environment approval gate, and pipeline logs proving a successful deploy and a successful rollback to the prior revision.

tasks.title: Level Up the Pipeline: Reusable Workflows, Buildx Layer Caching and Failing Scan Gates
tasks.description: Convert the pipeline from a single YAML file into a maintained system. Extract a reusable workflow with `workflow_call` plus composite actions for setup/test/build so no job duplicates steps, add path filters so docs-only changes skip the heavy jobs, and add concurrency groups that cancel superseded pull-request runs. Cache Docker layers with buildx and the registry cache backend so image builds are incremental, and add dependency-review plus Trivy jobs that genuinely fail the build on HIGH/CRITICAL findings. Document the .github/ layout so a reviewer can follow it.
tasks.deliverable: A reusable workflow plus composite actions consumed by both CI and the deploy pipeline, buildx layer caching with a measured build-time reduction, concurrency groups, failing dependency and container scan jobs, and a documented .github/ structure diagram.

phases.title: Phase 4: Production Architecture & Scalability
phases.description: Move from 'it deploys' to 'it survives'. Redis is taken to production depth (rate limiting, stampede protection, async queues), the service is made elastic and observable against a stated SLO, and the system design gap is closed in the language of the tradeoffs now actually implemented rather than in theory. Multi-environment Terraform, cost control and disaster recovery finish the phase so the architecture is repeatable and affordable, not just impressive once.

tasks.title: Observability: Structured Logs, Metrics, Alarms and Distributed Tracing
tasks.description: Instrument the deployed stack end to end so behaviour is measurable. Emit structured JSON logs with a correlation/request ID propagated from the ALB through the API to the worker, shipped to CloudWatch Logs with a documented query for the top five debugging questions. Publish custom business and latency metrics (requests, p95 latency, error rate, cache hit ratio) using the CloudWatch embedded metric format. Build a dashboard and at least three alarms - error-rate, p95 latency, and unhealthy ALB targets - wired to an SNS topic. Add OpenTelemetry tracing so one request can be followed across ALB -> API -> Redis -> Postgres -> worker.
tasks.deliverable: Structured-logging middleware with request IDs, a CloudWatch dashboard, three or more alarms with an SNS notification path, a committed set of CloudWatch Logs Insights queries, and a single OTel trace spanning all services.

tasks.title: Autoscaling and Load Testing to a Defined SLO
tasks.description: Make the service elastic and prove it with numbers. Define an explicit SLO (for example p95 under 300ms and error rate under 0.5% at 500 requests/second), configure ECS Service Auto Scaling with target-tracking on CPU utilisation and ALB request-count-per-target, and tune target values, scale-in/out cooldowns and min/max task counts so the service reaches steady state instead of flapping. Drive load with k6 or Locust against the deployed endpoint, capture throughput, p95 and error rate before and after scale-out, and identify the first bottleneck - typically the database connection pool - and fix it with pooling or a pgbouncer-style layer.
tasks.deliverable: Documented SLO, ECS autoscaling policies for CPU and request count with tuned min/max and cooldowns, a committed k6/Locust script, a load-test report showing scale-out and recovery, and a bottleneck analysis with the applied fix and the resulting metric change.

tasks.title: Redis at Production Depth: Rate Limiting, Stampede Protection and Async Queues
tasks.description: Take Redis past caching into the patterns interviewers probe. Implement a Redis token-bucket (or sliding-window) rate limiter on the public API with per-key limits, correct 429 responses and Retry-After headers, plus a test that proves the limit is enforced under concurrency. Add cache-stampede protection for the hottest key using a single-flight lock so one request repopulates and the rest wait on the value instead of hammering Postgres. Move slow work (email, image processing, report generation) into a background worker consuming an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue, idempotent handlers keyed by a dedupe ID, and Redis used for job status and progress. Run the worker as its own ECS service on its own image.
tasks.deliverable: A Redis rate limiter with a concurrency test proving 429 behaviour, a stampede-protected hot key with a single-flight lock, and an SQS-backed worker as a separate ECS service with a DLQ, idempotency keys and a before/after latency benchmark for the async path.

tasks.title: System Design Fluency: Caching, Queues, Consistency and Failure Modes
tasks.description: Turn everything built into design language. Write three design documents - a multi-tenant SaaS API, an image upload and processing pipeline, and a payment/event flow with exactly-once processing concerns - each covering requirements and scale estimates, API contracts, data model and indexes, caching strategy and invalidation rules, queueing and backpressure, idempotency and dedupe keys, consistency and isolation tradeoffs, the AWS hosting topology, scaling limits and a failure-mode table (timeouts, retries with jitter, circuit breakers, graceful degradation). Every decision must cite an artifact or measurement from Phases 2-4 rather than a blog post, and include a tradeoff table comparing SQL, Redis and queue for each read and write path.
tasks.deliverable: Three written system design documents with architecture diagrams, capacity/SLO estimates, a caching-versus-queue tradeoff table per data path, a failure-mode table with mitigations, and a self-critique list of where an interviewer would push back.

tasks.title: Multi-Environment Terraform, Cost Control and Disaster Recovery
tasks.description: Make the infrastructure repeatable and affordable.
